items.head: Not in line to be ready following bye
items.body: With regard to the availability of Adams (hamstring)  -- who remains on IR -- head coach Sean McVay said Friday "we'll take it a week at a time" with the wideout, while adding that he doesn't "think he's ready quite yet," Zach Edwards of the Rams' official site reports.

items.head: Not yet ready to practice
items.body: Coach Sean McVay noted Friday that Adams (hamstring) isn't expected to practice this weekend, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.

items.head: Reportedly targeting Week 12 return
items.body: According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN,  Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return to action Nov. 25 against the Packers. Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.

items.head: Could return by Week 12
items.body: Coach Sean McVay noted of Adams (hamstring) on Wednesday that he thinks a return to action by the wideout on Nov. 25 against the Packers "is a realistic timeline for us," Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports. In that scenario, Adams could back back in action as soon as Week 12, following the Rams' bye week. Meawhile, Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is destined to miss multiple weeks, which, for the time being leaves Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Danielsand Xavier Smith as the healthy WRs on the team's active roster.

items.head: Sean McVay: Rams optimistic WR Davante Adams will return 'sooner than later'
items.body: The Rams are optimistic that injured wide receiver Davante Adams will return from his hamstring injury "sooner than later," coach Sean McVay said.

items.head: Davante Adams (Hamstring) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Coach Sean McVay noted of Adams (hamstring) on Wednesday that he thinks a return to action by the wideout on Nov. 25 against the Packers "is a realistic timeline for us," Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.

items.head: Welcoming back Monangai
items.body: Swift will be rejoined in the Bears backfield by Kyle Monangai (toe) on Sunday against the Saints, Larry Mayer of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Trending to be Buffalo's TE1 vs. Miami
items.body: Knox will likely be the Bills' top tight end against the Dolphins on Sunday, given that Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for that contest, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports. Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he is trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox would operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches on 20 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season games, and the Bills face a Dolphins defense that ranks 25th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.

items.head: Catches one pass in win
items.body: Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of Buffalo's 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

items.head: Asserted by McDaniel as top RB
items.body: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports. "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week...I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Thursday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

items.head: Season-best rushing yardage in win
items.body: Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. He also fumbled once but recovered. On the momentous occasion of the Chargers' long-awaited first win of the season, Hampton made a significant contribution with a season-high rushing yardage total. The performance also marked the first time Hampton eclipsed the century mark this season, and he added his fourth rushing touchdown of 2026 on a one-yard power run on fourth-down on the first play following the two-minute warning in the first half. Hampton is now up to 474 rushing yards and a 12-63-0 receiving line heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Leading rusher as Chargers remain winless
items.body: Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

items.head: Back at practice again, Bengals QB Burrow optimistic he'll be at full strength
items.body: A full participant at practice for the second straight day despite the bug that he has battled, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is optimistic that he'll be at full strength when Cincinnati plays the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football.

items.head: Expects to be full strength for MNF
items.body: Burrow (illness) said Friday that he's getting better, noting that he "for sure" feels optimistic he'll be at full strength for Monday night's game against the Commanders, Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer reports.

items.head: Turns in full practice Thursday
items.body: Burrow (illness) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports. After appearing on the injury report with an illness, Burrow's full practice Thursday suggests the Bengals quarterback isn't facing any obvious limitations ahead of Monday night's date with the Commanders. A frontrunner in the MVP conversation, Burrow has been playing lights-out football for the past month-plus, as he and Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are firing on all cylinders.

items.head: Record-tying performance in win
items.body: Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and added one rush for eight yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. The latest installment in what is looking like an MVP-worthy campaign for Burrow included quite a milestone, as the 2020 first overall pick became the only other player in NFL history beside Peyton Manning in 2004 to score four-plus total touchdowns in five consecutive games. All of Burrow's scores Sunday night came through the air, as he connected with Drew Sample (three yards), Chase Brown (two, four yards) and Dohnte Meyers (15 yards) for his quartet of TD strikes. Burrow also found the bulk of his success when focusing on top wideout Ja'Marr Chase, who was responsible for 11 of Burrow's completions and 231 of his yards on 14 targets. Burrow has now exceeded 400 passing yards on three occasions this season, including twice in the last three games, heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Commanders on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.head: Sportsbook liability Joe Burrow overtakes Josh Allen as NFL MVP favorite
items.body: Bengals QB Joe Burrow has overtaken Bills star Josh Allen as the betting favorite for NFL MVP honors, a development that could prove costly for sportsbooks.

items.head: Another stellar effort in Week 9 win
items.body: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries. It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

items.head: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
items.body: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.

items.head: Drake Maye (Lower Leg) is Out
items.body: Maye has suffered a fractured right fibula that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him for some time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Patriots QB Drake Maye has fractured fibula, sources say
items.body: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has a fractured right fibula, and receiver A.J. Brown has a hamstring injury, sources told ESPN's Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter.

items.head: Not expected to be available after bye
items.body: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't have a definitive diagnosis for the injury Maye (ankle) sustained in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but indicated that the quarterback will miss time," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.  "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said. Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. At the very least, Maye can be expected to miss the Patriots' next game Nov. 29 against the Chargers. In the meantime, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests that the team is expected to explore the quarterback market in the coming days, though top backup Tommy DeVito is currently next in line to start in place of Maye.

items.head: Drake Maye (Ankle) is Doubtful
items.body: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't have a definitive diagnosis for the injury Maye (ankle) sustained in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but indicated that the quarterback will miss time," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.  "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said.

items.head: Ankle fracture feared
items.body: The Patriots are concerned that Maye fractured his ankle during Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Per Schefter, Maye remained in Germany to undergo additional testing to determine whether he needs surgery or not. In any case, Maye looks destined to miss some time beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye, if not the rest of the season. Tommy DeVito came on in relief of Maye in Sunday's contest and would be the next man up at quarterback for the Patriots, while rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton is also on hand. The Patriots seem likely to add depth to the position group in the coming days, either to the 53-man roster and/or the practice squad.

items.head: May have significant lower-leg inury
items.body: Maye is believed to have sustained a significant lower-leg injury in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich that could sideline him for an extended period of time, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Maye, who was forced out of Sunday's game with what the Patriots referred to as an ankle injury, is slated to undergo additional medical tests before a formal diagnosis of his injury is provided. While the Patriots won't have a projected timeline for Maye's recovery until testing is completed, Rapoport suggests that the quarterback could miss the rest of the season. In the event that Maye is sidelined for any length of time following New England's Week 11 bye, Tommy DeVito -- who replaced Maye on Sunday -- and Behren Morton are currently next in line for reps under center. Moreover, while the NFL trade deadline has come and gone, it's still possible that the 5-5 Patriots could explore options at the position via the free-agent market or other teams' practice squads.

items.head: Set for more tests on ankle
items.body: Following Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions, coach Mike Vrabel said that Maye will need additional testing to determine the severity of the ankle injury he suffered during the contest, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. The Patriots have a well-timed Week 11 bye, so Maye has some added healing time ahead of the team's Nov. 29 contest against the Chargers. However, if Maye isn't available by then, Tommy DeVito -- who replaced him Sunday -- would continue to do so in Week 12.

items.head: Ian Thomas (Calf) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Good to go for Sunday's game
items.body: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.

items.head: Another full practice
items.body: Waddle (concussion) was a full practice participant Thursday. A full practice participant for the second day in a row, Waddle looks to be close to clearing the NFL's concussion protocol after he sustained the head injury in a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers. Assuming he can receive clearance from an independent neurologist by the weekend, Waddle will be removed from the protocol and suit up Sunday versus the Raiders.

items.head: Practices fully Wednesday
items.body: Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Waddle sustained a concussion during a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers, and it looks like the Broncos' Week 10 bye has afforded their most productive wideout enough recovery time to be available Sunday against the Raiders. However, since it has yet to be officially confirmed that Waddle has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol,  his status will still need to be monitored until that happens.

items.head: Practices Wednesday
items.body: Waddle (concussion) was present for Wednesday's practice, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of Sunday's game
items.body: Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports. After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.

items.head: Jaylen Waddle (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.

items.head: Being checked for concussion
items.body: Waddle is being evaluated for a potential concussion during Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports. Per Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette, Waddle headed to the locker room Sunday after having absorbed a hard hit, leaving  Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims as the Broncos' available WRs. Prior to his exit, Waddle caught his only target for 22 yards.

items.head: DNP on Friday
items.body: Burks (foot) did not practice Friday. The Commanders have been managing Burks' practice reps, as he deals with a foot injury that's been nagging him for several weeks. He missed practice time last week but was still able to play against the Giants last Thursday, securing two of three targets for 27 yards. Washington will provide final injury designations Saturday ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.

items.head: Logs two catches in return from foot injury
items.body: Burks caught two of three targets for 27 yards Thursday in a 24-21 win over the Giants. Burks missed Week 9 due to a foot injury but was able to limit his absence to one game. The veteran wideout logged a 60 percent offensive snap share, third among Washington wideouts behind Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. Burks has a chance to take on a larger role in the Commanders' passing game with Terry McLaurin (knee) lost for the season, though Diggs and Williams may be better bets for weekly production given their higher spots in the pecking order.

items.head: Cleared for TNF
items.body: Burks (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Giants. Despite logging DNPs Monday and Wednesday, Burks is good to go after getting in a limited session Tuesday. He missed last Sunday's loss to the Rams but figures to return to his role in three-wide sets alongside rookie Antonio Williams and veteran slot man Stefon Diggs, which would push Van Jefferson down the depth chart after he popped up for 5-58-1 receiving against Los Angeles. Burks has produced seven catches for 147 yards on 11 targets over his last two games with Terry McLaurin (knee) sidelined.

items.head: Upgrades to limited activity
items.body: Burks (foot) was a limited participant in Tuesday's practice. After sitting out the Commanders' Week 9 loss to the Rams, Burks was listed as a non-participant to kick off Week 10 prep but was able to take a step forward in terms of activity during Tuesday's session. The wideout's availability for Thursday's game against the Giants remains murky, but if he's able to turn in another limited practice Wednesday, he'll stand a good chance at taking a questionable tag into the contest. Burks has drawn exactly five targets in each of his last three appearances, and he could end up holding down a top-three role in the Commanders' wideout corps for the rest of the season while Washington is without Terry McLaurin (knee).

items.head: Treylon Burks (injury) is Out
items.body: Burks (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Giants.

items.head: Treylon Burks (Foot) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Estimated as DNP on Monday
items.body: Burks (foot) was deemed a non-participant on the Commanders' practice report Monday, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Washington didn't actually practice Monday, so Burks' participation -- or lack thereof -- Tuesday should be more useful in providing insight into the wideout's chance of suiting up Thursday against the Giants. Burks didn't play this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams after sitting out practice all of last week. Terry McLaurin (knee) is out for the season, and Dyami Brown (calf) landed on IR on Saturday, so Burks will likely have a prominent role in the Commanders' passing game Thursday if he's able to suit up.

items.head: Could be back for Week 10
items.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Monday that he's "more optimistic" that Burks (foot) will be available for Thursday's game against the Giants, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Quinn expects to have better feel for Burks' status Tuesday, when the team will hold the most intense of its light practices leading up to Thursday's game. Burks was unable to play in this past Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams due to the foot injury, but once healthy, he'll likely be in line for a regular top-three role at receiver while Terry McLaurin (knee) is lost for the season.

items.head: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) cleared to start vs. Chargers
items.body: Jets quarterback Geno Smith made it through the practice week with no setbacks and was cleared to face the Chargers.

items.head: Cleared to play Week 11
items.body: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers. Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

items.head: Geno Smith (injury) is Active
items.body: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.head: Looking good for Week 11
items.body: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Smith (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. Smith also was deemed limited on Wednesday's practice estimate, so he may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Chargers without an injury designation. For his part, the Jets' QB1 isn't worried about his Week 11 availability, with Rich Cimini of ESPN.com noting Wednesday that while Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp at that point, the signal-caller stated that he intends to play this weekend. "That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."

items.head: Limited, but plans to play Sunday
items.body: Smith (ankle), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, said afterward that he intends to play in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Beyond noting that Smith will start if healthy, head coach Aaron Glenn hasn't confirmed that Smith will be available this weekend, but the quarterback's ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday is at least an encouraging sign for his status. Cimini notes that Smith was walking with a noticeable limp three days after injuring his left ankle in a Week 10 loss to the Bills, so the veteran signal-caller's mobility could be compromised to some degree if he gets the green light to play against the Chargers. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line for his first NFL start in the event Smith isn't deemed healthy enough to play this weekend.

items.head: Jets QB Geno Smith (ankle) intends to play vs. Chargers: 'That's the plan'
items.body: Jets quarterback Geno Smith says he intends to play Sunday against the Chargers despite still walking with a noticeable limp due to an ankle injury.

items.head: Opening Week 11 with limited practice
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith (ankle) will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports. Smith was unable to return to this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after tweaking his left ankle in the third quarter, but medical tests conducted after the game revealed no major injury. The veteran signal-caller will still be operating with a cap on his reps to begin Week 11 prep, and Glenn acknowledged that the Jets will wait and see how Smith fares as the week rolls along before a decision is made on his status for Sunday's game against the Chargers. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to start in Los Angeles if Smith isn't cleared to play.

items.head: In clear for Week 11 action
items.body: Barkley (hamstring) told EJ Smith of PHLY Sports on Friday that he "feels better physically" after the team's Week 10 bye, and the running back doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Steelers.

items.head: Cleared for Week 11
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.

items.head: Limited in Thursday's session
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited participation Wednesday to no activity during Thursday's practice.

items.head: Limited to kick off Week 11
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. Rodriguez was listed on injury reports both of the past two weeks due to the hand issue, but he proceeded to suit up for wins against the Ravens and Titans and handled his usual backup duties behind lead back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot). Assuming his limitations Wednesday were maintenance-related and not the result of any setback, Rodriguez should be ready to play Sunday against the Giants.

items.head: Not involved much in Week 10 win
items.body: Rodriguez rushed for five yards on four carries in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. Rodriguez was out-carried 26 to four by Bhayshul Tuten, who has very much proven himself as the Jaguars' clear RB1 in one of the league's best offenses. Tuten also out-snapped Rodriguez 52 to 10, while LeQuint Allen (12 snaps) saw more playing time. Rodriguez is little more than a deep-league bench stash should something happen to Tuten.

items.head: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (injury) is Active
items.body: Rodriguez rushed for five yards on four carries in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.

items.head: Cleared to face Titans on Sunday
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports. Rodriguez was listed as a limited practice participant all week,  but his hand issue is something he'll play through, while working alongside Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who returned to a limited session Friday and was also cleared for Week 10 action. Rodriguez has 55 carries in eight games to date, while Tuten has logged 122 rushes in that span, but Rodriguez has at least helped out his fantasy managers of late by scoring in each of his last two contests.

items.head: Limited at practice Thursday
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was a limited practice participant Thursday, while Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) didn't participate. The catch is that Tuten didn't practice last week and ended up playing in a 33-10 win at Baltimore on Thursday night. Rodriguez played through his hand injury, so he should be able to take on an expanded workload this week if Tuten doesn't play.

items.head: Practices on limited basis
items.body: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. While Rodriguez fit some work in on Wednesday, fellow RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a 'DNP' by the Jaguars. The duo's status is thus work monitoring closely in the coming days, but if Tuten ends up limited or out this weekend, Rodriguez -- if available -- and Ameer Abdullah would be next up for the team's backfield touches Sunday against the Titans.

items.head: Listed questionable
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bucs. If Vaki is unable to play against Tampa Bay, Jacob Saylors would move up to RB2 status, but Jahmyr Gibbs would have a chance to see an even bigger share of the backfield opportunities in that scenario.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Vaki (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. A limited participant for Wednesday's walkthrough, Vaki continued to operate with some restrictions while the Lions held a more traditional practice Thursday. Vaki's involvement in any capacity is nonetheless a good sign for his Week 11 status, though he may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.

items.head: Limited during Wednesday's practice
items.body: Vaki (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice. Vaki has been listed on Lions injury reports over the past two weeks due to the lingering ankle issue, but it hasn't kept him from playing in either contest. With the Lions running away with a 25-point win over the Patriots in Munich in Week 10, Vaki saw more work than usual behind lead back Jahmyr Gibbs, finishing with six carries for 28 yards and a 17-yard reception.

items.head: Accumulates 45 yards in Week 10 win
items.body: Vaki turned six carries into 28 yards and added a 17-yard catch on his only target during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. Lead back Jahmyr Gibbs dominated with 252 yards and three touchdowns on 29 total touches (22 carries, seven catches on eight targets), but Vaki also had his moments during Sunday's game, including a 17-yard catch on the first play of the second quarter. Vaki was working through an ankle issue during Week 10 prep before being cleared to play, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield behind Gibbs. Through eight regular-season games, Vaki has turned 36 carries into 163 yards (4.5 YPC) and eight catches on nine targets for 81 yards. The Lions will be at home for three of their next four games, starting with Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

items.head: Sione Vaki (injury) is Active
items.body: Vaki turned six carries into 28 yards and added a 17-yard catch on his only target during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.

items.head: Suiting up in Week 10
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich. Vaki is playing through an ankle issue for a second straight contest, but last Sunday at Miami he was able to handle an above average 34 percent snap share, indicating he again is good to serve as Jahmyr Gibbs' top backup. On the season, such a workload has amounted to 37 touches for 199 yards from scrimmage and no TDs in eight appearances for Vaki.

items.head: Sione Vaki (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Vaki (ankle) did not participate at practice Wednesday.

items.head: Active for Week 9
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Miami. Vaki didn't practice Friday, resulting in a questionable tag for Week 9. However, he will be out there against the Dolphins and may continue to be more involved after totaling 11 carries in the Week 8 win over the Vikings.

items.head: Brenen Thompson (Hamstring) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: Cleared for Sunday's game
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

items.head: At stretching portion of Friday's practice
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

items.head: Could do some running Friday
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot), per head coach Liam Coen, "will maybe run around a little bit" at Friday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

items.head: How Bhayshul Tuten became the clear No. 1 running back for the Jaguars
items.body: After a lackluster rookie season, Tuten ranks 14th in NFL in rushing yards entering Sunday's game against the Giants.

items.head: Sidelined for practice Thursday
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Tuten was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, so his downgrade in activity a day later is notable, though the listing could be maintenance-related rather than due to a setback.  O'Halloran previously relayed that the running back was working off to the side during the media-access portion of Thursday's session. The extent of Tuten's participation in Friday's practice bears watching, as the Jaguars look to determine whether he'll take an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Giants.

items.head: Works off to side at practice
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) was working off to the side during the stretching portion of Thursday's practice, according to Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union. Tuten has been listed as a limited participant in the Jaguars' last two practices (including this past Friday) as he continues to manage ankle and foot issues. It appears as though that approach is in play again Thursday, though the running back's official participation level won't be clarified until the team's upcoming injury report is posted.

items.head: Logs limited practice Wednesday
items.body: Tuten (ankle/foot) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. As were fellow RBs Chris Rodriguez (hand) and LeQuint Allen (hamstring), though there's a decent chance that the listed limitations of Tuten and Rodriguez were maintenance-related as opposed to being indicative of setbacks on their part. Both players were limited at practice this past Friday by the same injuries and headed into Week 10 action without injury designations. Though we'll continue to track both players in the coming days, there's no indication so far that either of their statuses for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any danger.

items.head: Tops 100 scrimmage yards against Titans
items.body: Tuten carried the ball 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown and caught three of four targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over Tennessee. It's the second time this season that Tuten has reached triple-digit scrimmage yards in a game, with both those performances coming since the Jaguars' Week 7 bye. The second-year RB capped the rout with a six-yard TD run in the fourth quarter, extending his scoring streak to four games -- a stretch in which Tuten has racked up 260 rushing yards and three touchdowns on the ground while adding a 9-128-3 line on 10 targets through the air. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 11 against the Giants.

items.head: No designation for Sunday
items.body: Likely didn't practice Friday to a strained groin, but he doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Jaguars, Patricia Traina of SI.com reports.

items.head: Should be OK for Week 11
items.body: Head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Likely is tending to a "minor thing" but should be good to play Sunday against the Jaguars, Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports.

items.head: Not spotted at practice Friday
items.body: Likely (undisclosed) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Career-high receiving yardage in loss
items.body: Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category was also a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components are already career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.head: Catches TD from Winston in win
items.body: Likely caught five of six targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Likely finished two targets shy of Malik Nabers' team-leading total and one receiving yard shy of Darnell Mooney's team-best mark, but the TE scored the Giants' lone touchdown of the game. That TD came on a five-yard pass in the third quarter from Jameis Winston, who replaced J.J. McCarthy (hip) for a drive and change before McCarthy returned to the game. Whether it's Winston or McCarthy under center, Likely projects to remain a key cog in the Giants' passing game for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, whose defense Likely carved up for 11 catches, 94 yards and two TDs in their Week 5 tie.

items.head: Faces uncertain status Sunday
items.body: Bowers (ankle) said Friday that his availability for Sunday's game against the Broncos remains up in the air, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Listed as questionable versus Denver
items.body: Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers (ankle) is slated to be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Practicing again Friday
items.body: Bowers (ankle) was present for Friday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Returns to limited practice Thursday
items.body: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports. Bowers missed Wednesday's practice, but his return a day later, albeit in a limited fashion, is a positive sign as Sunday's game against the Broncos approaches. Head coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that the star tight end doesn't need to practice this week in order to play this weekend, per Sam Warren of The Athletic ,but Bowers already has cleared his first hurdle toward that end by virtue of his participation in Thursday's session.

items.head: Back at practice Thursday
items.body: Bowers (ankle) was on the field for the start of Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports. After Bowers was a non-participant in Wednesday's session, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak reiterated that the tight end was still being viewed as day-to-day while working through the ankle injury he sustained in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. Kubiak added that Bowers didn't necessarily need to practice this week in order to play Sunday in Denver, but Bowers' return to the field Thursday offers some reassurance about his chances of suiting up against the Broncos. The Raiders will reveal the extent of Bowers' practice participation when they post their second Week 11 injury report later Thursday.

items.head: Could play this week without practicing
items.body: Coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that Bowers (ankle) doesn't need to practice this week in order to play Sunday Sunday against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "If he's ready to go, we'll get him out there," said Kubiak, who previously noted that Bowers is progressing in his recovery from the ankle injury he sustained in Week 10. While it's encouraging that Bowers -- who is viewed as day-to-day -- could play this weekend, a determination on that may not arrive until game day. The Raiders kick off at 4:25 pm ET on Sunday, but Bowers is obviously the kind of player whose status is worth waiting on. An ideal scenario for his fantasy managers is rostering Michael Mayer as a pivot option.

items.head: Absent from practice Wednesday
items.body: Bowers (ankle) wasn't spotted on the field for Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports. Bowers will go down as a non-participant in the Raiders' first Week 11 session, after head coach Klint Kubiak deemed the star tight end day-to-day due to the ankle injury he sustained in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. Though Kubiak suggested that Bowers' injury isn't anything significant, the 24-year-old will still likely need to practice in some fashion Thursday or Friday to have a shot at playing this Sunday in Denver.

items.head: Labeled day-to-day by coach
items.body: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Monday that Bowers (ankle) is considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury," Kubiak said. Bowers checked in and out of Sunday's contest as he managed the ankle issue, finishing with two catches for 18 yards on two targets while logging just 11 snaps on offense. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak added that Bowers will continue to be evaluated throughout the week as the Raiders look to determine whether the star tight end will be available for next Sunday's game in Denver. If Bowers is forced to miss his third game of the season, the Raiders would have more targets up for grabs for the likes of tight end Michael Mayer, running back Ashton Jeanty and wideouts Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

items.head: Limited by heel issue
items.body: White was limited at Friday's practice due to a heel injury. White was tacked on to the Commanders' Week 11 practice report Friday, joining Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), who has been a full participant this week but remains on injured reserve. It adds another question mark to the team's backfield situation ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals, and Saturday's injury report will reveal the odds of both players to suit up in the coming days.

items.head: Rachaad White (Heel) is Questionable
items.body: White was limited at Friday's practice due to a heel injury.

items.head: Leads backfield in win
items.body: White rushed 11 times for 47 yards and brought in one of two targets for five yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

items.head: Finds little running room in Week 9 loss
items.body: White carried the ball seven times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. The 28 rushing yards led the Commanders on the afternoon, although Austin Ekeler saw one more carry than White did. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) set to miss at least one more contest while on IR, White seems likely to lead the backfield again in Week 10 against the Giants. Over the three games Croskey-Merritt has been sidelined so far, White has produced 186 scrimmage yards and two TDs -- one rushing and one receiving -- while averaging 4.4 yards per carry.

items.head: Dontayvion Wicks (Ankle) is Out
items.body: Wicks (ankle/foot) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

items.head: Practicing again Friday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) was present for Friday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday. Wicks is seeking his first game action since Week 6 due to an ankle injury, and he still has some work to do after kicking off Week 11 prep with back-to-back capped sessions. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to play Sunday versus the Steelers.

items.head: Practicing Thursday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) is participating in practice Thursday, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports. Wicks now has logged back-to-back practices to begin Week 11 prep, with his activity level to become known once the Eagles post an injury report Thursday. He practiced in a limited fashion Wednesday, which marked his first on-field work since Week 6.

items.head: Practices in limited fashion
items.body: Wicks (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday. Wicks was sidelined by an ankle issue in Weeks 7-9, but a Week 10 bye has him trending toward a return to action after getting back on the practice field Wednesday. Friday's injury report will reveal his odds to suit up Sunday against the Steelers.

items.head: Practicing Wednesday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) participated in Wednesday's practice, Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports. Wicks is taking his first on-field reps since Week 6 prep, as he's been sidelined in the meantime due to an ankle injury. Following a Week 10 bye, head coach Nick Sirianni said Wednesday that he feels good about Wicks' chances to return to action Sunday against the Steelers, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Ultimately, how Wicks fares in drills Wednesday through Friday will determine if he's cleared ahead of the weekend.

items.head: Could be back this week
items.body: Coach Nick Sirianni relayed Wednesday that he feels good about the chances of Wicks (ankle) returning to action Sunday against the Steelers, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports. The same goes for DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and if the duo is available this weekend, they'd provide a big boost to WR corps that has been paced by Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper of late. That said, while Sirianni is hopeful that Wicks and Smith and are ready to return, per Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia, at this stage he's not ready to make any promises regarding their Week 11 availability.

items.head: Dontayvion Wicks (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Limited in return to practice
items.body: Bell (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Bell was sidelined for the Dolphins' final two Week 10 practices before being listed as doubtful and ultimately ruled out ahead of Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, but the rookie wideout looks to be in a better spot on the health front in Week 11. After head coach Jeff Hafley described Bell as day-to-day prior to Wednesday's session, the receiver was able to turn in a limited practice. Bell will likely need to upgrade to full activity by Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

items.head: Considered day-to-day
items.body: Bell (knee) is viewed as day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports. Bell, who was inactive for Miami's Week 10 contest against the Colts, didn't practice this past Thursday and Friday after taking what coach Jeff Hafley described as a knock to his knee last week. In his absence versus Indianapolis, Kevin Coleman logged added WR snaps alongside Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas.

items.head: Inactive in Week 10
items.body: Bell (knee) is inactive for Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Colts. The rookie sat out both Thursday and Friday's practices before being given a doubtful designation for Sunday's contest, and his inactive status is now official. With Bell, who'd posted a 7-56-0 line on 10 targets in Weeks 7 and 8 before being blanked against the Lions in Week 9, sitting out Sunday, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert could share No. 3 receiver snaps while working with new starting quarterback Kyle McCord.

items.head: Deemed doubtful
items.body: Bell (knee) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Colts. Bell was a limited practice participant Wednesday before sitting out Thursday and Friday. The injury is to his surgically repaired knee, but coach Jeff Hafley was quick to specify that the current issue isn't related to the ACL repair from last year. It sounds like Bell could be back within a week or two. For now, No. 4 receiver Kevin Coleman figures to get more playing time.

items.head: Unlikely to play
items.body: Bell (knee) is unlikely to play in Sunday's game against the Colts, but his injury isn't considered long-term and isn't related to the ACL repair surgery he had last December, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Bell reportedly got hit on his surgically repaired knee, and coach Jeff Hafley said the current injury has "nothing to do with [Bell]'s surgery." Hafley even left the door open for Bell to play Sunday, though the coach's other comments suggest it's highly unlikely. An absence would leave more playing time for fellow rookie Kevin Coleman, who has been been Miami's No. 4 receiver for most of the season.

items.head: Not seen at practice Thursday
items.body: Bell (knee) wasn't spotted at practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Bell was listed as limited Wednesday, so his apparent downgrade in participation a day later puts the focus on what the wideout is able to do Friday as it relates to his status for Sunday's game against the Colts. Through eight contests overall, Bell has 12 catches for 148 yards and no TDs on 27 targets, and he's coming off a zero-catch effort in the Dolphins' Week 9 loss to the Lions, during which the 2026 third-rounder was on the field for 63 percent of his team's snaps on offense.

items.head: Limited on injury report
items.body: Bell (knee) is listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. This is likely just maintenance for Bell's surgically repaired knee. His role as the No. 3 wide receiver in Miami hasn't yielded much, with Bell drawing targets on just 16.7 percent of routes and catching only 44.4 percent of his targets. Things can't get much worse, at least from a statistical standpoint, with QB Kyle McCord replacing Malik Willis (abdomen) for at least the next four weeks.

items.head: Cleared for Week 11
items.body: Kelce (ankle/calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Kelce was forced from last Sunday's game against the Falcons with the ankle injury, but he's good to go for Week 11 against a hapless Arizona squad. The Chiefs should run all over the Cardinals' defense and likely won't need much pass volume from Patrick Mahomes. Kelce is more of a fringe TE1 for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Managing injuries, but practices fully
items.body: Kelce was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, despite being listed with ankle and calf injuries. During this past Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons, Kelce exited for a brief spell in the first half after injuring his ankle, but he ultimately returned to the contest. In addition to the ankle issue, Kelce may have tweaked his calf at some point in Week 10, but head coach Andy Reid indicated prior to Wednesday's practice that the veteran tight end was "doing well" in his recovery from the injuries, per Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com. His ability to take every rep for the Chiefs' first Week 11 session suggests his status for Sunday's game againt the Cardinals isn't in any peril.

items.head: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's top moments at Arrowhead Stadium
items.body: Kelce's greatest Arrowhead moments include his first catch, lots of playoff magic, and meeting the love of his life, Taylor Swift.

items.head: Quiet after ankle injury
items.body: Kelce secured both targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Kelce recorded a 23-yard catch on the Chiefs' first play from scrimmage, seemingly a harbinger of a productive day. However, the veteran tight end also suffered an ankle injury on the tackle, and although he was able to return to the game, he had only one more reception the rest of the way. Despite the modest numbers, Kelce managed to keep his season-long streak of games with multiple receptions going, and he's averaging a career-best 14.6  per catch heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

items.head: Back in Sunday's game
items.body: Kelce (ankle) has returned to Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the team's official site reports. Kelce had been listed as questionable to return to the contest, but was able to return to the field in the second quarter. While the team's backfield is banged up this week, Kelce ability to return to action Sunday at least assures the Chiefs that their top pass catchers are available for QB Patrick Mahomes to target.

items.head: Questionable to return Sunday
items.body: Kelce (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports. Kelce injured his right ankle at the tail end of his 23-yard catch early in the first quarter, and he's been taken to the locker room to undergo further tests to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Noah Gray, Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley are all in line for more snaps at tight end for as long as Kelce is sidelined.

items.head: Goes to locker room Sunday
items.body: Kelce went to the locker room during Sunday's game in Atlanta due to an apparent ankle injury, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Per Nate Taylor of ESPN.com, Kelce had his right ankle twisted up during a 23-yard catch on the Chiefs' first possession and then walked off the field slowly. For as long as Kelce is sidelined, Noah Gray, Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley will man tight end for Kansas City.

items.head: Team-high receiving yards in win
items.body: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard. Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

items.head: Full practice, but questionable for Sunday
items.body: Tate (shoulder), who was a full participant in Friday's practice, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

items.head: Limited at Thursday's practice
items.body: Tate (shoulder) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. Tate appears to be tracking toward a Week 11 return against Dallas after he's missed the last two games against Cincinnati and Jacksonville. The Titans could definitely use the rookie wideout after Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was placed on season-ending injured reserve earlier this week. Tate's return would likely push Chimere Dike back into WR4 duties, with Xavier Restrepo the more sensible slot replacement for Robinson.

items.head: Present for practice Thursday
items.body: Tate (shoulder) was present for practice Thursday, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports. Tate, who last played in Week 7, returned to a limited practice Wednesday and is back out there a day later in some capacity. The Titans' upcoming injury report will reveal the wideout's participation level, but Tate seems to be inching closer to a return to the lineup as Sunday's game against the Cowboys approaches.

items.head: Limited in return to practice
items.body: Tate (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. Back at practice for the first time since Week 7, Tate operated with a cap on his reps. So long as he progresses to full participation at some point over the next two days, Tate should be on track to end his two-game absence this Sunday in Dallas. The rookie first-round pick had seen most of his snaps on the perimeter over the Titans' first seven games, but he could be in store for more snaps out of the slot moving forward after Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sustained a season-ending injury in Week 10.

items.head: Back at practice Wednesday
items.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that Tate (shoulder) will practice Wednesday, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports. Tate has been sidelined for the Titans' past two games and wasn't able to practice in advance of either contest while he managed the shoulder injury, but he'll take a notable step forward in his recovery by getting back on the field. While the Titans won't reveal until after practice concludes whether Tate was a full or limited participant, the rookie's involvement in the team's first Week 11 session is generally a positive sign for his chances of playing Sunday in Dallas.

items.head: Expected back for Week 11
items.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that he's hopeful that Tate (shoulder) will return to action in Week 11 versus the Cowboys, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports. Even with the benefit of a Week 9 bye, Tate still wound up being sidelined for a second straight game in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on account of the shoulder injury. Though Saleh is optimistic that the rookie wideout will be ready to go for the Titans' upcoming game in Dallas, Tate will first need to return to practice in some fashion to make that a reality. Tate remained a non-participant in practice throughout Week 10 prep.

items.head: Sits out Thursday's practice
items.body: Tate (shoulder) didn't practice Thursday. Turron Davenport of ESPN.com previously noted that Tate was able to work on the side with the Titans' training staff during Thursday's session, but in the end he was officially listed as a 'DNP' for the second consecutive day. Friday's practice will thus loom large in terms of Tate's potential availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. Next up for added WR snaps this weekend in the event that Tate remains sidelined is Chimere Dike, Elic Ayomanor and Calvin Ridley.

items.head: Does side work Thursday
items.body: Tate (shoulder) was spotted doing work on the side with the Titans' training staff during Thursday's practice, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports. After sitting out Wednesday's practice, Tate figures to log another 'DNP' a day later, which puts his activity level in Friday's session in the spotlight. If Tate ends up limited or out Sunday against the Jaguars, some combo of Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and Calvin Ridley would be in line to log added snaps/targets alongside Wan'Dale Robinson.

items.head: Jonathan Mingo (Ankle) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: Ticketed for lead-back duties again Week 11
items.body: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Johnson is in line to handle workhorse duties for the second straight week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Stellar showing in Week 10 win
items.body: Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

items.head: Will be Kansas City's RB1 vs. Atlanta
items.body: Johnson will be the Chiefs' top running back for Week 10 after Kenneth Walker (groin) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Walker popped up on Friday's practice report as a DNP due to groin tightness, and the injury is severe enough for the fifth-year running back to miss his first game of the season. That leaves Johnson -- the Chiefs' fifth-round pick of the 2026 NFL Draft -- as the lead back for Sunday's game, and with Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the team could elevate Nate Carter from the practice squad to provide additional backfield depth. Through eight regular-season games, Johnson has turned 26 carries into 111 yards (4.3 YPC) and a touchdown and caught 14 passes on 16 targets for 237 yards and a score.

items.head: Could lead backfield Sunday
items.body: Coach Andy Reid noted that Johnson would take the bulk of the Chiefs' carries in the event that Kenneth Walker -- who didn't practice Friday due to groin tightness -- is forced to miss Sunday's game against the Falcons, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports. Added context regarding Walker's status will arrive via Friday's final injury report when the Chiefs assign their Week 10 injury designations. Chances are, Walker will be deemed questionable, but if he ends up sidelined this weekend, Johnson would provide those who roster Walker, or otherwise need RB help, with a viable pivot option.

items.head: Scores rush TD in easy win
items.body: Johnson rushed six times for 34 yards and a touchdown and returned one kickoff for 29 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. The Chiefs held a 28-12 lead by the end of three quarters, which provided the opportunity for head coach Andy Reid to give Kenneth Walker, who scored three total touchdowns, some down time in the latter portion of the contest. Johnson took advantage of his opportunities, recording a six-yard touchdown run with 3:35 remaining. The rookie fifth-round pick's yardage total was a new career high, while his carry tally was his highest since Week 3. Johnson will remain in a modest No. 2 role for a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Douglas (shoulder) is expected to play Sunday against the Bills, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Douglas said earlier this week that he was planning to play Sunday, and head coach Jeff Hafley backed up that statement while speaking prior to Friday's practice. The Dolphins will reveal whether or not Douglas carries an injury designation into Sunday's contest at some point Friday afternoon.

items.head: Another limited practice session
items.body: Douglas (shoulder) remained a limited practice participant Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. The listing makes sense, given that Douglas, who was also deemed limited Wednesday, worked in a  non-contact jersey Thursday. Fellow WR Chris Bell (knee) also has logged back-to-back 'LP' listings, with the duo's game statuses for Sunday's game against the Bills set to be revealed after Friday's practice.

items.head: Still in non-contact jersey
items.body: Douglas (shoulder) continued to don a non-contact jersey during Thursday's practice, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Douglas also practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, per C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald, but despite that, the wideout said he will play Sunday against the Bills. Officially, Douglas was limited Wednesday, and that's probably how he'll be listed one day later.

items.head: Nursing shoulder injury
items.body: Douglas was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a shoulder injury, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Per C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald, Douglas was spotted wearing a red non-contact jersey during the open portion of practice, but the rookie wideout said afterward that he fully expects to play Sunday against the Bills. So long as Douglas continues practicing in some fashion over the next two days, he should be on track to suit up in Buffalo, though he may need to upgrade to full participation to avoid taking a designation into the weekend.

items.head: On track to be available Sunday
items.body: Douglas (undisclosed) practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, but he said he will play Sunday against  the Bills, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. The Dolphins' upcoming injury reports is slated to reveal what issue led to Douglas donning a non-contact jersey Wednesday, but at this stage, his Week 11 availability doesn't appear to be in much danger. During his team's 24-22 loss to the Colts this past weekend, Douglas recorded an 84 percent snap share, while catching three of his team-high eight targets for 71 yards, also a team high.

items.head: Caleb Douglas (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: Douglas (undisclosed) practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, but he said he will play Sunday against  the Bills, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.

items.head: Team-high yardage total in loss
items.body: Douglas brought in three of eight targets for 71 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Douglas posted a team-high yardage total with a big hand from his game-long 38-yard grab. Douglas garnered plenty of first-time starter Kyle McCord's attention as evidenced by the receiver's team-high target tally, and he's now hit or exceeded the 70-yard mark in three of the past four games. The 2026 third-round pick will look to carry over the momentum into a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

items.head: Chiefs expect to be without Kenneth Walker III vs. Cardinals
items.body: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III is not expected to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals after not participating in practice this week due to a groin injury.

items.head: Likely out in Week 11
items.body: Head coach Andy Reid said Friday that Walker (groin) "most likely" won't be available Sunday against the Cardinals, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.

items.head: Not spotted Friday
items.body: Walker (groin) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.

items.head: Misses Thursday's practice
items.body: Walker (groin) did not practice Thursday. Walker is looking extremely unlikely to play Sunday against a Cardinals team that Kansas City should handle with ease at home. The Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround against the Bills on Thanksgiving, and it may make sense to let Walker rest for another week in preparation for that contest, especially after rookie Emmett Johnson showed in Week 10 against Atlanta that he's more than capable of carrying the torch in the backfield. Fantasy players need to be prepared to be without Walker for at least one more week.

items.head: Not in line to practice Wednesday
items.body: Walker (groin) won't practice Wednesday, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports. Walker was sidelined for the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson erupted for 171 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on 28 touches. Now sidelined to begin Week 11 prep, Walker will have two more chances to practice before the Chiefs make a call on his status for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Walker's sore groin isn't believed to a major concern, and head coach Andy Reid told Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site on Wednesday that the tailback is "feeling a lot better." The Chiefs will see how Walker progresses as the week rolls along, but it wouldn't be surprising if the team erred on the side of caution and held him out for another game. Kansas City will be heavy favorites for its matchup with Arizona before facing a quick turnaround in Week 12 for what should be a more competitive matchup with the Bills next Thursday.

items.head: Won't play against Atlanta
items.body: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports reports. Walker was a late addition to the Chiefs' practice report Friday as a DNP due to what was described as "groin tightness." He was initially tagged as questionable for Sunday's contest, but the injury is severe enough for the fifth-year running back to miss his first game of the regular season. Rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson is projected to lead Kansas City's backfield against Atlanta in Walker's absence, and with Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the Chiefs could elevate Nate Carter from the practice squad to the active roster. Walker's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.head: Deemed questionable for Sunday
items.body: Walker (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons. Walker was added to the Chiefs' Week 10 injury report due to groin tightness that kept him from practicing Friday. Now that he's carrying an official 'questionable' designation heading into the weekend, the running back's status will need to be tracked as Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff approaches. In the event that Walker -- who is averaging a robust 109.0 rushing yards per game and has scored 11 total TDs through eight contests -- is made inactive for the contest,  Emmett Johnson would be in line to handle the bulk of the team's carries versus Atlanta.

items.head: Sits out Friday's practice
items.body: Walker (groin) sat out Friday's practice due to groin tightness, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports. Per McDowell, coach Andy Reid noted of Walker on Friday, "we'll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow." Based on this report, there's a good chance Walker will be deemed questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons. If he ends up limited or out this weekend, the door would be open for rookie Emmett Johnson to step into an expanded role in Week 10.

items.head: A.J. Brown (Hamstring) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: Expected to miss multiple weeks
items.body: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Limping following loss Sunday
items.body: Brown (hamstring) was spotted limping out of the locker room following Sunday's Week 10 loss to Detroit, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports. Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday in Munich, Germany. However, the veteran wideout suffered a hamstring injury while making a catch in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the defeat, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is once we get back and kind of go from there." New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays, which will be Sunday, Nov. 29, against the Chargers.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of Sunday's game
items.body: Brown (hamstring) won't return to Sunday's game against the Lions, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports. Brown was initially deemed questionable to return after his exit, but now the WR's next chance to see game action will arrive Nov. 29 versus the Chargers, following the Patriots' bye. In his return from a two-game absence, Brown had caught two of his six targets for 27 yards prior to hurting his hamstring. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will handle New England's wide receiver duties for the remainder of Sunday's contest.

items.head: Exits Sunday's game
items.body: Brown (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions. After heading for the medical tent during the contest, per Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald, Brown was officially deemed questionable to return versus Detroit. Prior to his exit, the WR caught two of his six targets for 27 yards.

items.head: Active for Sunday's game versus Detroit
items.body: Brown (knee/ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich. Brown, who hasn't played since Week 7, was able to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday through Friday before being deemed questionable for Sunday's contest. The Patriots' marquee offseason acquisition has had trouble staying on the field to this point, but following a two-game absence, he'll return to bolster a WR corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams. In three games thus far, Brown has compiled a 9/101/0 receiving line on 20 targets, but he's capable of bringing a higher level of productivity to the table going forward, provided he's able to avoid any further injury setbacks.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Brown practiced on a limited basis all week, and it appears that was what he needed to do in order to return from a two-game absence. The Patriots will officially reveal Brown's status for Week 10 when they release their inactives 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 9:30 am ET kickoff.

items.head: Practices again Friday
items.body: Brown (ankle/knee) practiced Friday for a third straight day, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. Brown was listed as a limited participant on both Wednesday's and Thursday's injury reports, and it appears he is getting at least some work in for a third straight day. The Patriots will reveal his official status for Sunday's matchup with the Lions in Munich when they release their final injury report later Friday.

items.head: Wants to play Monday
items.body: Croskey-Merritt (groin) said Friday he's taking things "day by day," but his goal is to play Monday against the Bengals, John Keim of ESPN reports.

items.head: Full practice Thursday
items.body: Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. The Commanders designated Croskey-Merritt for return from injured reserve Tuesday, and in the team's first official practice of Week 11 prep, he was uninhibited. Assuming he's able to maintain that activity level Friday and Saturday, he's a good bet to miss the minimum four games on IR due to the groin injury that bothered him multiple weeks through the first five contests of the campaign.

items.head: Back at practice Thursday
items.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that Croskey-Merritt (groin) will practice Thursday, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports. Washington opened Croskey-Merritt's 21-day evaluation window two days earlier, but he'll take part in his first practice Thursday since landing on injured reserve Oct. 19. Per Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C., Quinn said that Croskey-Merritt is considered fully recovered from his groin injury, but the Commanders want to see how he responds to football activity over the course of the team's three practices this week before deciding his next step. If Croskey-Merritt is able to practice fully by Saturday and checks out well from a physical standpoint, he could be reinstated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals.

items.head: Cleared to resume practicing
items.body: The Commanders designated Croskey-Merritt (groin) for return from injured reserve Tuesday. As a result of the transaction, the Commanders will have a 21-day window wherein they can evaluate Croskey-Merritt for a return to the 53-man roster. Depending on how he fares in practice during Week 11, Croskey-Merritt could be reinstated ahead of Monday's game against the Bengals. Whenever the Commanders elect to activate him, Croskey-Merritt will likely step back in as the team's lead runner, allowing Rachaad White to shift into more of a complementary role as the top pass-catching back.

items.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (Groin) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Commanders designated Croskey-Merritt (groin) for return from injured reserve Tuesday.

items.head: Trending in right direction, per coach
items.body: head coach Dan Quinn said Monday that while the 21-day practice window for Croskey-Merritt (groin) hasn't been opened yet, he notes that the running back is "trending in the right direction," Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports. Croskey-Merritt landed on IR back on Oct. 19, but now that the running back has missed the required four games his stint on the list entailed, he's eligible to return to practice once he's ready to do so. Quinn's comment Monday suggests that's not an imminent outcome, though Croskey-Merritt's Week 11 outlook could brighten by the time the Commanders' first injury report ahead of next Monday's game against the Bengals is posted. In Washington's latest game -- a Nov. 12 24-21 win over the Giants -- Rachaad White (11 carries, one catch) and Austin Ekeler (nine carries, four catches) handled the bulk of the team's backfield load in Week 10.

items.head: Listed as questionable
items.body: Pittman (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Mark Kaboly reports. Pittman was designated for return from injured reserve earlier this week and had progressed to full participation Thursday, so his questionable tag keeps him in the mix for a potential activation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Eagles. With both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger) nearing a return, it's unclear what that will mean for rookie Germie Bernard's role going forward, as the rookie has hit a slow spot in the box score the last couple weeks.

items.head: Practices fully Thursday
items.body: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports. After he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman practiced for the second day in a row. Pittman took a step forward in activity after he was a limited participant a day earlier, potentially putting him on a path to return from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Philadelphia. In order for Pittman to be eligible to play against the Eagles, the Steelers would have to activate him prior to Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline for Week 11 roster moves.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Pittman (foot) participated in practice Thursday, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman was able to return to a limited practice. The WR's presence at Thursday's session implies that there were no setbacks, with the Steelers' upcoming injury report set to reveal his official participation level. In any case, Pittman will need to be activated off IR no later than Saturday afternoon in order to have a chance to play Sunday against the Eagles.

items.head: Limited in first practice back
items.body: Pittman (foot) was limited in his return to practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.

items.head: Back practicing Wednesday
items.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that Pittman (foot) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. Pittsburgh opened the 21-day evaluation windows of both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger), clearing the way for both receivers to resume practicing Wednesday. McCarthy suggested earlier in the week that Pittman has a shot at suiting up Sunday in Philadelphia, though the wideout's availability will likely depend on how he looks in practice over the next three days. Prior to landing on injured reserve Oct. 10 after aggravating a left foot injury, Pittman had gotten off to an underwhelming start to the season, recording seven receptions for 89 yards and no touchdowns on 12 targets through three appearances.

items.head: Could be back for Week 11 action
items.body: Coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that the Steelers are "hopeful" they can get Pittman -- who last played in Week 4 -- back from his foot injury this week, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. The same goes for Roman Wilson (finger), who saw his last game action in Week 5. In the duo's absence, DK Metcalf has led Pittsburgh's WR corps, with Germie Bernard having seen his role expand in the process. Prior to his injury, Pittman caught seven of his 12 targets for 89 yards in three games, but once he rejoins the lineup, the 29-year-old -- who had at least 111 targets in each of his last five seasons with the Colts -- could resurface on the fantasy radar in PPR formats.

items.head: Takes part in Thursday's warmups
