items.body: Pittman (foot) is warmed up with his teammates Thursday, though he remains on IR and wasn't wearing a helmet, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

items.head: Not ready to practice
items.body: Pittman (foot) is making progress but won't have his practice window opened this week, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports. Pittman resumed running in late October and could resume practicing at some point in November. It won't happen this week, however, leaving the Steelers with minimal WR depth beyond DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

items.head: Ready to return in Week 11
items.body: Monangai (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Saints.

items.head: Listed as full Wednesday
items.body: Monangai (toe) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate. Monangai told Courtney Cronin of ESPN on Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints, and after being spotted in full pads at Tuesday's unofficial practice, the running back would have logged an uncapped session one day later if the team had held drills. Monangai is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a turf toe injury and a right thumb concern.

items.head: Kyle Monangai (injury) is Active
items.body: Monangai (toe) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate.

items.head: Practices again Tuesday
items.body: Monangai (toe/thumb) was seen wearing full pads for the Bears' unofficial practice Tuesday, Adam Jahns of AllCHGO.com reports. After their Week 10 bye, the Bears won't post their first Week 11 practice report until Wednesday, but Monangai may be trending toward being listed as a full participant. The second-year back was on the field for a second straight day Tuesday and didn't appear to be operating with any limitations while mixing into drills. Monangai had missed the Bears' previous five games due to turf toe and a right thumb injury, but he looks poised to return to action this Sunday against the Saints.

items.head: Kyle Monangai (Toe) is Questionable
items.body: Monangai (toe/thumb) was seen wearing full pads for the Bears' unofficial practice Tuesday, Adam Jahns of AllCHGO.com reports.

items.head: 'On track' to be back in Week 11
items.body: Monangai (thumb/toe) said Monday that he's "on track" to return to action Sunday against the Saints, Courtney Cronin of ESPN reports. Monangai was a limited practice participant Nov. 6, which marked his first on-field work since suffering a turf toe injury Oct. 4 versus the Jets. He still missed his fifth consecutive game as a result of that injury and a right thumb issue, but after a Week 10 bye, he's aiming to resume game action. "The time off definitely helped, but I mean it's going to be there," Monangai relayed about the toe concern. "Offseason, I'll heal it. ... It's something I can manage now." He also mentioned that he'll need the support of plates and orthotics inside his cleats the rest of the campaign. The Bears logged an unofficial practice Monday, which Monangai took part in, and Wednesday's injury report will reveal his initial activity level of Week 11 prep.

items.head: Eyeing return in Week 11
items.body: Monangai (toe/thumb) was spotted working out during Monday's unofficial practice and is eyeing a return to action Sunday against the Saints, Chris Emma of 104.3 The Score Chicago reports. Monangai hasn't played since Week 4 while recovering from a bout with turf toe and a right thumb injury, but he appears to be gearing up for a return following the Bears' Week 10 bye. Chicago won't release its first Week 11 injury report until Wednesday, when it will be known whether Monangai has been cleared to practice as a full or limited participant. He'll presumably need to turn in at least one full practice this week to put himself on a path to play Sunday, when he would likely settle back into a complementary role behind starting running back D'Andre Swift.

items.head: Inactive in Week 9
items.body: Monangai (thumb/toe) is inactive for Sunday's contest against the Buccaneers. Monangai finally was able to mix into drills Friday for the first time since emerging from Week 4 with a turf-toe injury, going down as a limited participant. The Bears kept the door open for him to return by giving him a questionable designation, but after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Monangai isn't expected to play in Week 9, his inactive status doesn't come as a surprise. However, Rapoport also noted that Monangai is on pace to be back in Week 11 versus the Saints following a Week 10 bye. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will be Chicago's lead runner, with Roschon Johnson backing him up.

items.head: Zavion Thomas (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Jeshaun Jones (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: The Vikings signed Jones (shoulder) off the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.

items.head: Clear for Week 11
items.body: Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago.

items.head: Jordyn Tyson (injury) is Active
items.body: Tyson (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.

items.head: Stays limited Thursday
items.body: Tyson (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday. Tyson maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he tends to a chest injury in the wake of his 11-80-0 line on 13 targets from the second game of his career this past Sunday versus the Panthers. Friday's practice report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

items.head: Present for practice Thursday
items.body: Tyson (chest) took part in the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports. Tyson was limited at Wednesday's session due to a chest injury, and he at least is maintaining that activity level one day later. Thursday's practice report will reveal if he again was limited or upgraded to full. In the second game of his career this past Sunday against the Panthers, Tyson gathered in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards.

items.head: Limited by chest issue
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said Tyson was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. Tyson missed the first seven games of the campaign due to a hamstring issue, but he increased his sway in the Saints offense from Week 9 to 10, upping his snap share (24 to 71 percent) and target count (five to 13). In this past Sunday's loss to the Panthers, he recorded an 11-80-0 line, but he emerged from that contest with a new health concern. As a result, Tyson's status will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

items.head: Jordyn Tyson (Chest) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Breakout performance in Week 10 loss
items.body: Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. That bang you just heard was the sound of the window closing on your chances of acquiring Tyson cheaply in your fantasy league. In just his second career NFL game, Tyson dominated looks from Tyler Shough, as no other New Orleans pass catcher handled more than five targets, hauled in more than three passes or topped 30 receiving yards. It may be tough for the team's struggling offense to keep both Tyson and Chris Olave busy at the same time, so the duo may end up trading big games rather than opening things up for each other, but this kind of volume can't be ignored. Tyson will look for his first career touchdown in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

items.head: Increased role on tap?
items.body: Tyson was working with the Saints' first-team offense pregame ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. In his pro debut last Sunday against the Browns, Tyson ranked fourth in snap share (24 percent) among his position mates behind Devaughn Vele (93), Chris Olave (85) and Bryce Lance (51). Tyson still hauled in four of five targets for 30 yards, and head coach Kellen Moore told Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio on Wednesday that the rookie WR should receive "a healthy dose more" of work in his second NFL outing. Considering Tyson has swapped in for Lance with the first-teamers, the former is poised to do just that this Sunday.

items.head: Gets questionable tag
items.body: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that the 49ers will make a decision on Evans' (Achilles) Week 11 status Saturday after listing the wide receiver as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Officially limited Thursday
items.body: Evans (Achilles) officially was limited at Thursday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports. Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

items.head: In uniform Thursday
items.body: Evans (Achilles) is suited up for Thursday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports. Assuming Evans is able to log at least a limited practice Thursday, it'll officially mark his first on-field work since aggravating a right Achilles injury during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. How he fares in drills Thursday and Friday likely will determine if he's cleared to return to action Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City.

items.head: Could be back at practice Thursday
items.body: San Francisco general manager John Lynch said that "there's a chance" Evans (Achilles) will take part in a padded practice Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports. Evans joined up with the 49ers in Colorado Springs on Wednesday as the team began prepping for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City, but the wideout was merely a spectator for the first Week 11 practice. The veteran wideout looks as though he could see some involvement in drills Thursday, which would mark his first on-field activity since Week 6. Evans has been sidelined for the 49ers' past three games after aggravating a right Achilles injury in an Oct. 19 win over the Commanders.

items.head: DNP on Wednesday, may practice Thursday
items.body: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (Achilles) won't practice Wednesday but hopes the wide receiver will return to drills Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. If Evans gets back on the field Thursday, it'll mark his first on-field work since Week 6, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. He's missed the past three games as a result -- benefiting from the 49ers' Week 9 bye -- and it appears how he fares in practice the next two days will determine if game action is possible Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City.

items.head: Poised to practice this week
items.body: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that the 49ers are "hoping to" have Evans (Achilles) back at practice this week, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Evans missed the 49ers' last three games while recovering from right Achilles tendinitis, but he has a chance at returning to action in Week 11. After staying behind in the Bay Area this past weekend for the team's 46-40 win in Dallas, he's scheduled to meet back up with the 49ers this week in Colorado Springs, where the team will be holding practices at high altitude to get acclimated for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City. If Evans is able to practice in some capacity Wednesday through Friday and if his Achilles responds well, he'll likely be cleared to play for the first time since Week 6.

items.head: May return in Week 11
items.body: Evans (Achilles) has a chance to return to action next Sunday against the Vikings, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Evans is missing his third consecutive game this Sunday in Dallas due to right Achilles tendinitis that he suffered during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. He hasn't practiced in the meantime, and while he's a rare player who doesn't need on-field reps during the week to be available on game days, he would provide confidence in his ability to play again with an appearance in drills at some point this Wednesday through Friday.

items.head: Ruled out for Week 10
items.body: Evans (Achilles) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports. Evans thus will miss his third game in a row due to the right Achilles injury that he aggravated during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is "real close" to returning to action and likely would play this weekend if it was a playoff matchup. Instead, the 49ers will continue to exercise caution with their No. 1 WR. With Evans again sidelined Sunday, Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing represent the options at the position available to QB Brock Purdy.

items.head: Good to go for Week 11
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.

items.head: T.J. Hockenson (injury) is Active
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.

items.head: Another limited practice
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) practiced on a limited basis Thursday. After sitting out this past Sunday's win at Green Bay due to wrist and chest injuries, Hockenson has logged back-to-back capped sessions to begin Week 11 prep due to just the wrist issue. He'll have one more opportunity to get back to full Friday, at which point the Vikings may tag him with a designation ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

items.head: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday. After sitting out the entirety of Week 10 prep due to wrist and chest injuries, Hockenson was ruled out ahead of this past Sunday's game at Green Bay. It marked his first absence of the season, but in his return to drills Wednesday, he was listed with only the wrist issue, signaling progress in his recovery. In the end, though, Hockenson may need to practice fully Thursday and/or Friday to enter the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest against the 49ers in Mexico City.

items.head: Chance to return in Week 11
items.body: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that the Vikings hope Hockenson (wrist/chest) returns to action Sunday against the 49ers in Mexico City, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports. Hockenson was sidelined this past Sunday in Green Bay due to wrist and chest injuries. He likely will need to practice in some capacity this week in order to make a return possible, so how he's listed on Wednesday's injury report will be of keen interest.

items.head: Expected to progress ahead of Week 11 action
items.body: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that the Vikings expect Hockenson (wrist/chest) to make progress ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. Hockenson was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, but it sounds like the tight end has a chance to return to practice after logging DNPs last week. In Hockenson's absence versus Green Bay in Week 10, fellow TE Gavin Bartholomew caught three of his four targets for 36 yards and a TD.

items.head: Ruled out for Week 10
items.body: Hockenson (wrist) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Hockenson wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep due to wrist and chest injuries and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. In Hockenson's absence, Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew will step into more prominent roles in the Vikings offense, while Devin Culp will be a candidate to be elevated from the practice squad.

items.head: Not spotted Friday
items.body: Hockenson (wrist/chest) wasn't seen during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports. Hockenson appears set to go down as a non-participant for a third consecutive practice due to wrist and chest issues, and the Vikings now may make a ruling on his status for Sunday's game in Green Bay on their final Week 10 injury report Friday. If Hockenson is inhibited or sidelined this weekend, Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew are the other tight ends on the active roster, while Devin Culp can be elevated from the practice squad.

items.head: Cardinals QB Carson Beck dealing with back spasms; Josh Johnson may start
items.body: The Cardinals are preparing veteran quarterback Josh Johnson to start Sunday vs. the Chiefs as rookie Carson Beck deals with back spasms, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday.

items.head: Won't practice Friday
items.body: Beck (back) will not practice Friday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.

items.head: Limited by back injury
items.body: Beck was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report due to a back issue, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports. Per Sureck, Beck dealt with back spasms a "few weeks ago," so his sudden appearance on Arizona's Week 11 injury report has a reasonable explanation. In any case, his status now will be monitored in advance of Sunday's game at Kansas City, with Friday's practice report potentially providing clarity in that regard.

items.head: Carson Beck (Back) is Questionable
items.body: Beck was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report due to a back issue, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Throws two picks in NFL debut
items.body: Beck was 11-for-18 passing for 108 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions and had one rush for one yard during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams. The Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens after Week 8, and then Gardner Minshew tore the UCL in his right elbow in Week 9, setting the stage for the first appearance (a start) of Beck's career. Beck, a rookie third-rounder, generated just two drives of 30-plus yards among his nine possessions overall, and two others ended in interceptions in Rams territory. He also didn't find much success with his top available skill-position talent, TE Trey McBride, who gathered in all five of his targets for 37 yards. They'll look to improve their rapport next Sunday in Kansas City.

items.head: Gets doubtful tag
items.body: Kincaid (thumb) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Matt Parrino reports.

items.head: Sidelined for Thursday's practice
items.body: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) wasn't spotted on the field for Thursday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports. Kincaid has now kicked off Week 11 prep with consecutive absences from practice, but he'll be able to erase some concern about his status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins if he's able to get back on the field Friday in some capacity.

items.head: Dalton Kincaid (Thumb) is Questionable
items.body: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) did not practice Wednesday, David Furones of the Sun Sentinel reports.

items.head: Gains 58 yards on three targets
items.body: Kincaid caught two of three targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Kincaid contributed catches of four and 54 yards to finish second on the team in receiving yards behind DJ Moore (90). The 2023 first-round pick has seen his usage fluctuate throughout the campaign, as Kincaid has failed to exceed three targets on five occasions but has drawn at least six looks from Josh Allen in each of the other four games. Kincaid is making the most of his opportunities for a second consecutive regular season, averaging 11.9 yards per target in 2026 after leading all qualified TEs with 11.7 YPT in 2025. Next up for Kincaid is a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

items.head: Dalton Kincaid (injury) is Active
items.body: Kincaid caught two of three targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.

items.head: No injury designation
items.body: Kincaid (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets. Kincaid was a full practice participant Friday after logging limited sessions the previous two days. He should be fine for his usual role against a porous Jets defense.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Kincaid (ankle) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice. Kincaid has opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. He has faced plenty of practice limitations throughout the season, but Kincaid has yet to sit out a game. That pattern seems unlikely to change in Week 10 against the Jets.

items.head: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: Kincaid (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's walk-through. Kincaid began last week with a limited session due to a chest issue, but was able to suit up for Monday night's win over the Vikings while seeing the field on 50 percent of the Bills' snaps on offense. In the process, the tight end caught all three of his targets for 28 yards. It's unclear if Kincaid's ankle injury occurred versus Minnesota or is something that occurred Wednesday, but either way added context regarding his status for this weekend's game against the Jets will arrive via Thursday's injury report.

items.head: New starting QB in Indy
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen announced Friday that Richardson will be the Colts' starting quarterback moving forward after the team waived Daniel Jones.

items.head: Being let go by Indianapolis
items.body: Jones will be waived by the Colts, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

items.head: Another forgettable performance in loss
items.body: Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed once for three yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday before being replaced by Anthony Richardson with 7:51 remaining. Jones' final line underscores how ineffective he was for the fifth straight game, once again finishing well under 200 passing yards, extending his streak of games with at least one interception to six and taking a safety early in the second half. Although the 3-8 Colts don't have any realistic designs on the postseason, James Boyd of The Athletic reports Colts head coach Shane Steichen said, "I'll evaluate everything," when asked if he'll consider benching Jones ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Forgettable numbers in win
items.body: Jones completed 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while adding five carries for nine yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered. Jones failed to eclipse the 200-yard mark for the fourth straight game while throwing multiple picks for the second time in that span. Neither turnover led to any Dolphins points, and Jones also threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to new interim No. 1 receiver Laquon Treadwell in the second quarter. Jones has completed just 59.6 percent of his passes and has a 7:12 TD:INT across 10 games, and with Indianapolis devoid of any realistic postseason aspirations, it may not be long before Anthony Richardson is given an opportunity under center. However, Joel A. Erickson of The Indy Star reports that head coach Shane Steichen has already named Jones the starter for Thursday's Week 11 road matchup against the Texans.

items.head: NFL Week 10 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips, post-trade deadline news
items.body: No deals for Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones or Brian Thomas Jr.? Vikings seeking QB answers with their Kirk Cousins trade? Here's the latest intel.

items.head: Pedestrian numbers in loss
items.body: Jones completed 20 of 34 passes for 180 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding three rushes for 11 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. Jones took a pair of sacks and averaged a modest 5.3 yards per attempt in what would have to be termed a disappointing performance overall considering the struggles the Cowboys defense had endured. Jones' one touchdown pass came on a 55-yard catch-and-run on a wide receiver screen by Ashton Dulin late in the third quarter. Jones has now failed to eclipse 180 passing yards in three straight games while also tossing six interceptions over his last four contests, and reports emerged late in the week that the Colts were fielding calls from multiple teams about a potential trade for the veteran signal-caller before Tuesday's deadline.

items.head: Drawing interest on trade market
items.body: The Colts have been contacted by multiple teams regarding the availability of Jones ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN report. Coming off a torn right Achilles last Dec. 7, Jones has struggled for much of the season but especially over the last five contests, a stretch that has included 186.2 passing yards per game, 5.5 YPA and a 2:6 TD:INT. After the last two games in particular, head coach Shane Steichen first decided to stick with Jones as the starter in Week 8 at Jacksonville, and after benching him for Anthony Richardson in that matchup, he eventually opted to stay with Jones for Week 9 action. Despite the uneven play, Baltimore reportedly checked in with Indianapolis before trading for Jacoby Brissett, and Rapoport and Schefter speculated the Vikings are a team that may have interest in Jones, who spent the final month-plus of the 2024 campaign with the organization.

items.head: Expected to start Sunday
items.body: Johnson is expected to start Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. With Carson Beck (back) not expected to practice Friday or play Sunday, Johnson appears in line to step into the starting quarterback role for Arizona. Johnson has a career 14:18 TD:INT across 50 regular-season appearances. The entire Arizona offense is one to avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions for Week 11.

items.head: Listed as questionable Sunday
items.body: Brooks (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Brooks remains on injured reserve, so the questionable tag suggests Carolina at least may activate him ahead of Sunday's contest. If he's cleared to play, the running back would be in line to make his first appearance since Week 2, though he's no real threat to Chuba Hubbard's standing as the Panthers' lead back.

items.head: Full practice again Thursday
items.body: Brooks (groin) remained a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports. Brooks is still on injured reserve but appears to be tracking toward a Week 11 return against Baltimore on Sunday. Chuba Hubbard should remain head-and-shoulders above Brooks on the depth chart as the clear RB1 for Carolina, but the Panthers likely also want to use the rest of the season to see if Brooks can stay healthy for a stretch and produce when given opportunities. Brooks is worth adding in fantasy, but his role will need to be defined before plugging him in lineups.

items.head: Listed as full Wednesday
items.body: Brooks (groin) was a full participant at Wednesday's walkthrough. Brooks was listed similarly last Wednesday before capping the week with back-to-back limited practices and receiving a doubtful tag for Week 10 action. He then was downgraded to out before this past Sunday's game at New Orleans. Brooks is seeking a return from injured reserve, where he's resided since after Week 2 due to core muscle surgery.

items.head: Won't return for Week 10
items.body: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Saints, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Brooks ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The third-year running back is not quite fully recovered from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, so his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22. Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus will continue to operate in rotational backfield roles behind Chuba Hubbard while Brooks is sidelined.

items.head: Listed as doubtful for Week 10
items.body: Brooks (groin) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at New Orleans after being limited in practice throughout the week, Kassidy Hill of the Panthers' official site reports. Brooks remains on injured reserve and isn't likely to be activated by the 4:00 p.m. ET deadline Saturday. He was listed as a full practice participant at the beginning of the week, but coach Dave Canales revealed Friday that there was a reporting error with Brooks and CB Mike Jackson (groin), both of whom should have been listed as limited. Both were then listed as limited Thursday and Friday, with 'doubtful' designations for Sunday's game. Brooks appears on track to return for Week 11 or 12, at which point he could take a few touches away from Chuba Hubbard.

items.head: Full practice participant Thursday
items.body: Brooks (groin) was a full practice participant Thursday. The Panthers also listed Brooks as 'FP' on Wednesday's estimated practice report. Now that he's actually logged a full practice, Brooks may have a real shot to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game at New Orleans. The Panthers would need to make that move by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Brooks on the active roster Sunday.

items.head: Listed as full Wednesday
items.body: Brooks (groin) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 due to a groin injury that required core-muscle surgery and a stint on injured reserve. The Panthers designated him for return from IR on Wednesday, and he kicked off Week 10 prep with an uncapped walkthrough. How Brooks is listed on the injury report when Carolina holds practice Thursday and/or Friday may be the determining factor in his chances to play Sunday at New Orleans.

items.head: Awaits update on status ahead of Week 10
items.body: Coach Dave Canales said Monday that the Panthers will spend the next two days discussing the status of Brooks (core), Mike Kaye of ESPN.comreports. Brooks, who remains on IR, was seen working off to the side during the Panthers' unofficial practice last Tuesday, per Joe Person of The Athletic, perhaps signaling some progress for the oft-injured RB, who last saw game action in Week 2. In Brooks' absence, Chuba Hubbard has dominated Carolina's backfield touches.

items.head: Trending toward Sunday start
items.body: Mayfield (foot) is trending in the right direction to start Sunday's game against the Lions after looking good in Friday's practice, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.

items.head: Practicing again Friday
items.body: Mayfield (foot) is practicing again Friday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. With Mayfield having progressed from sitting out Wednesday to being limited Thursday, Friday's participation is another positive sign for his availability Sunday against Detroit. The Buccaneers' upcoming injury report is destined to reveal both Mayfield's participation level Friday, as well as his Week 11 game status.

items.head: Bucs QB Baker Mayfield hopes to play Sunday despite foot injury: 'I feel ready'
items.body: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is hoping to play Sunday against the Lions after he sustained a foot injury two weeks ago against the Chicago Bears.

items.head: Calls himself 'limited' Thursday
items.body: Mayfield (foot/right thumb) said that he felt good but was "limited" at Thursday's practice, and he's hopeful to do more at Friday's session, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports. The Buccaneers are on the heels of their Week 10 bye, but Mayfield himself has a foot injury in tow stemming back to a Week 9 loss in Chicago. In addition to the new issue, he touched on the dislocated thumb that sidelined him in Weeks 4-6, telling Smith that he had to "grind some things out" in his return to action. Mayfield's status for Sunday's contest at Detroit appears to be truly up in the air, but his ability to practice in some capacity Thursday indicates he at least is putting in every effort to be available.

items.head: Back at practice Thursday
items.body: Mayfield (foot/thumb) was seen participating in Thursday's practice, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. Coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Mayfield didn't practice Wednesday while receiving more time off to recover from the foot strain he sustained in a Nov. 8 loss to the Bears. The extent of Mayfield's involvement in Thursday's session won't be known until after it concludes, but the signal-caller was seen participating in ball-security drills and looked to be moving around well. So long as Mayfield steers clear of any setbacks over the next few days, he could be ready to start Sunday's game in Detroit.

items.head: Not practicing Wednesday
items.body: Mayfield (foot) isn't practicing Wednesday, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. It's not a great sign that coming off the Buccaneers' bye week, Mayfield was at Wednesday's session in street clothes, per Auman, albeit with no wrap or boot on his injured foot. In any case, at this stage, Mayfield is looking iffy for Sunday's game against the Lions, and if he's unavailable for Week 11 action, Jalon Daniels -- who was getting starter reps in drills Wednesday -- would be in line handle QB1 duties for Tampa Bay this weekend.

items.head: Looking unlikely for Week 11
items.body: The Buccaneers aren't ruling Mayfield (foot) out from playing in Sunday's game at Detroit, but the team views the quarterback as "probably a long shot for this week," Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. Though head coach Todd Bowles has yet to comment on Mayfield's status for Week 11, media reports over the last few days have pointed toward the veteran quarterback missing his fourth game of the season after he sustained a foot strain late in a Nov. 8 loss to the Bears that resulted in him being in and out of a walking boot during the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye. Fowler acknowledges that Mayfield will likely "push to get ready and play" Sunday, but the Buccaneers may be motivated to hold him out this weekend to ensure he's in optimal health for a matchup with the division-leading Panthers in Week 12. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels would receive the starting nod against the Lions in the event Mayfield is ruled out.

items.head: Baker Mayfield (Foot) is Questionable
items.body: Mayfield (foot) "seems to be trending" toward sitting out Sunday's game against the Lions, with Jalon Daniels likely to draw the Week 11 start, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Will be activated from IR
items.body: Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports. Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation would at least keep him off season-ending injured reserve, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

items.head: Could see more opportunities Sunday
items.body: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Taylor could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers. Isaiah Williams (ribs) has also been ruled out for the Jets, so they'll be down their Nos. 3 and 4 receivers, which could lead to more multiple-tight end sets for New York. Taylor is averaging 2.8 catches for 20.9 yards per game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

items.head: Grabs four passes vs. Buffalo
items.body: Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday. Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.head: One catch in loss
items.body: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

items.head: Back practicing in full
items.body: Taylor (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. Taylor was limited Wednesday, but his return to full Thursday puts him on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. The tight end has been a surprisingly big part of the passing offense this season despite the selection of Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's Draft. Taylor has secured 17 of 23 targets for 136 yards and two touchdowns across six games.

items.head: Limited to begin Week 9 prep
items.body: Taylor was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a back injury. Since sitting out Weeks 3 and 4 due to a thumb injury, Taylor has played north of 50 percent of the snaps on offense in each of the Jets' last four games, cobbling together a 15-138-2 receiving line on 20 targets over that stretch. Provided the back issue doesn't prevent him from practicing Thursday and Friday, Taylor should be able to handle his usual role this Sunday in Kansas City.

items.head: Could see more work with Cooper out
items.body: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Sadiq could see more pass-catching opportunities Sunday against the Chargers. In addition to Cooper, Isaiah Williams (ribs) will also be sidelined against Los Angeles. Sadiq could essentially handle WR3 duties behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, though it's not the easiest matchup against the Los Angeles defense. Still, Sadiq has a chance to see elevated snaps, which could obviously translate to more targets in the passing game. He's still difficult to get behind as a fantasy starter.

items.head: Another quiet showing in Week 10
items.body: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time has been a factor in Sadiq's listless production of late; he's logged fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in five of those seven games while second-year tight end Mason Taylor typically has handled larger snap shares.

items.head: Pops for 49 yards in loss
items.body: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

items.head: Elevated role on tap sans Cooper
items.body: With Omar Cooper (ankle) ruled out, Mitchell is expected to play an elevated role on offense Sunday against the Chargers. Cooper was injured early in last Sunday's loss to the Bills, and Mitchell went on to see eight targets, as the Jets were playing catch-up most of the afternoon. They might be able to keep things closer against the 1-8 Chargers, though Los Angeles is still favored in the contest. Mitchell is a big-play threat as a WR4 for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Three catches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Mitchell caught three passes for 59 yards on eight targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, Mitchell was left fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.head: Active in Week 10
items.body: Mitchell (knee) is listed as active Sunday versus the Bills. Mitchell followed up a 7-142-1 performance on nine targets in Week 8 with no catches on his seven targets last Sunday at Kansas City. It was a missed opportunity for him in Week 9 with Garrett Wilson out due to a concussion, and Mitchell himself was added to the Week 10 practice report Friday due to a knee injury, leaving him questionable for Sunday along with Wilson and Omar Cooper (ankle). All three are available this weekend, but with Wilson poised to take on his typical No. 1 role, Mitchell will be the second option, at best, among his position group.

items.head: Listed as questionable after FP
items.body: Mitchell (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills after he was a full participant in Friday's practice. Fellow wideouts Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper (ankle) also are listed as questionable despite being full practice participants Friday. Both figure to play, as does Mitchell, who finished without a catch on seven targets (two drops) in last week's loss to the Chiefs -- one week after catching seven passes for 142 yards and a TD against the Raiders. Wilson's likely return to the lineup means Mitchell isn't assured of similar volume moving forward.

items.head: No catches in Week 9
items.body: Mitchell failed to reel in any of his seven targets during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now gone without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.

items.head: Another huge opportunity?
items.body: Mitchell and Omar Cooper will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports. Mitchell is coming off the best performance of his career -- a 7-141-1 receiving line on 26 routes (nine targets) in last week's 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Cooper also ran 26 routes but finished without a target, despite topping 100 yards in back-to-back games beforehand. Both wide receivers now have a big opportunity with Wilson out of the lineup against a Kansas City defense that's missing cornerbacks Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and L'Jarius Sneed (IR - knee).

items.head: Set to miss a "couple months, " per coach
items.body: Coach Sean McVay revealed Friday that Nacua (knee) had surgery to repair his MCL on Tuesday and is on track to miss a couple of months, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Rams WR Puka Nacua to serve 3-game suspension while on IR
items.body: Los Angeles Rams standout wide receiver Puka Nacua has been suspended three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, the NFL announced Thursday.

items.head: Suspended three games
items.body: Nacua has been suspended three games for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Nacua currently resides on injured reserve due to PCL and MCL sprains and a turf toe injury, for which he still must miss at least three games. The announced suspension conveniently lines up with his remaining expected time away from the field, and he'll be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14, following the completion of the the Rams' Week 14 contest versus the 49ers. Schefter's report also notes that the league communicated to the wideout that that any further violation of the personal conduct policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, would subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league.

items.head: Has expected return date of mid-December
items.body: Nacua (knee/toe) has an expected return date of "mid-December," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. After the Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve Thursday, Nacua must miss at least four games, which means his earliest return date is Sunday, Dec. 20 against the Cowboys. Considering the timeline given in Rapoport's report, Nacua thus may miss only the minimum number of contests while on IR after suffering PCL and MCL sprains and also a turf-toe injury last Sunday at Washington. With Davante Adams (hamstring) out at least one more outing, L.A. is rolling with a receiving corps of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley in Week 10.

items.head: May be tracking for Week 14 or 15 return
items.body: The Rams are optimistic that Nacua (knee/toe) will be able to return to action Week 14 versus the 49ers or Week 15 versus the Cowboys, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports. While the Rams have yet to officially rule Nacua out for their Week 10 game at Arizona, head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday that the wideout was likely to land on injured reserve. It's unclear if the Rams are still planning on deactivating Nacua, however; they placed fellow receiver Jordan Whittington (back) on IR on Tuesday, while Nacua remained a member of the 53-man roster. With a bye on tap Week 11, the Rams could be compelled to keep Nacua off IR if they believe he can play Week 14, which would mean that he misses three games rather than the four required for an IR stint. Whatever the case, the Rams will have to get by with a depleted pass-catching group in the short term, as Nacua, Whittington, Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) are all sidelined with injuries.

items.head: Puka Nacua (Knee - MCL) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: Puka Nacua (Knee) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: IR stint appears likely
items.body: Coach Sean McVay indicated Monday that Nacua (knee) is likely headed to injured reserve with a PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports. With Davante Adams (hamstring) already on IR, Nacua's injury situation represents another huge blow to the Rams offense. Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and CJ Daniels are the team's remaining healthy WRs, but a trade to bolster the position seems imperative ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

items.head: Present for practice Friday
items.body: Waller (knee) is practicing again Friday, Joseph Person of The Athletic reports. The same applies to fellow TE Tommy Tremble (knee), with both players having logged limited practices Thursday after being deemed 'DNPs' a day earlier. The Panthers' upcoming Friday injury report will clarify the duo's game statuses heading into the weekend. Waller is coming off a two-catch, 24-yard effort on four targets in Week 10 versus the Saints, but the week prior he put up an 8/90/1 receiving line on 10 targets versus the Broncos.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Waller (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN reports. One day removed from being a non-participant Wednesday due to a knee injury, Waller was able to mix into some drills, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point his odds to suit up Sunday against the Ravens will become known.

items.head: Practicing Thursday
items.body: Waller (knee) is suited up for Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports. Head coach Dave Canales called knee injuries for Waller and fellow TE Tommy Tremble concerning when they didn't practice Wednesday, but both players returned to drills one day later. Ultimately, Thursday's injury report will reveal their respective activity levels.

items.head: DNP due to knee injury
items.body: Waller didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, and afterward head coach Dave Canales called the tight end's injury a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports. The Panthers' top two tight ends in Waller and Tommy Tremble (knee) showed up as DNPs to begin Week 11 prep, and Canales' "concern" comment also extended to Tremble. It's unclear if either of both are in danger of missing Sunday's game against the Ravens, but Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are the healthy TEs on Carolina's active roster.

items.head: Darren Waller (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: Waller didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, and afterward head coach Dave Canales called the tight end's injury a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.

items.head: Two catches in Week 10
items.body: Waller caught two of four targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. One week after his 8-90-1 receiving outburst, Waller came back to normalcy in the Panthers' three-man committee at tight end. Waller has big upside, but his ceiling games are difficult to predict. He's been held below 40 yards with no touchdowns in five of nine games this season. Waller will be a low-floor TE2 with upside for Week 11 against the Ravens.

items.head: Leading receiver in Week 9 loss
items.body: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.

items.head: Two touches in Week 11 loss
items.body: Giddens rushed one time for five yards and caught his lone target for 11 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans. With Seth McGowan (hamstring) exiting early with an injury, Giddens spelled Jonathan Taylor and played seven offensive snaps. Through three games this season, Giddens has rushed seven times for 48 yards and registered one catch for 11 yards. If McGowan's injury costs him time, Giddens figures to handle RB2 duties in his absence.

items.head: Only two offensive snaps vs. Miami
items.body: Giddens played two offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Giddens barely saw the field during Sunday's win, and his two offensive snaps were well behind fellow running backs Jonathan Taylor (40) and Seth McGowan (17). Giddens -- a fifth-round pick of the Colts in the 2025 NFL Draft -- has seen little playing time since making his 2026 regular-season debut in Week 8 against the Jaguars. His role will likely stay minimal for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

items.head: No action in Week 9
items.body: Giddens did not appear in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan upon Taylor's departure.

items.head: Injury not considered serious
items.body: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

items.head: Kayshon Boutte (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: Boutte (hip) was deemed questionable to return to Thursday's Week 11 win over Indianapolis and didn't return to the game.

items.head: Goose egg versus Cleveland
items.body: Boutte failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. Even with Marvin Harrison (hamstring) out and Jaylin Noel (toe) done for the season, Boutte was targeted one just one of C.J. Stroud's 38 pass attempts versus Cleveland. His 47 snaps on offense were fewer than both Nico Collins (57) and Xavier Hutchinson (51) but 14 more than Tank Dell, though Dell out-targeted Boutte four to one. Boutte popped off for 4-125-2 in Week 9 against the Chargers but has otherwise failed to reach 40 receiving yards in any of his eight other appearances this season.

items.head: Strikes for two TDs in Week 9
items.body: Boutte erupted for four catches (on five targets) for 125 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 44-22 road win against the Chargers. Boutte entered Week 9 action with a cumulative 15-194-0 line on 23 targets through seven appearances this season, so Sunday's performance was a true outburst. It didn't hurt that Boutte and his teammates were facing the only winless team in the NFL, but QB C.J. Stroud took full advantage of the opportunity, including Boutte (twice) among his five TD tosses. Ultimately, the Texans' receiving corps has a clear No. 1 in WR Nico Collins, who is the best bet among the group to produce most weeks.

items.head: Won't play Sunday
items.body: Williams (ribs) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers. With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.

items.head: Sits out another practice
items.body: Williams (ribs) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice. The Jets' wideout depth could be tested in Sunday's game against the Chargers, as both Williams and Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) have been sidelined for the team's first two Week 11 practices. Both receivers will likely need to practice in some fashion Friday to avoid being ruled out ahead of the weekend. If neither Williams nor Cooper can suit up against the Chargers, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick would be the available backup options behind starting receivers Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell.

items.head: Sidelined for practice with rib injury
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Williams won't practice Wednesday due to a rib injury, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports. New York will be without two of its wideouts to begin Week 11 prep, as rookie Omar Cooper (ankle) is also sidelined for Wednesday's practice. Williams drew a season-high seven targets in this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills, finishing with four catches for 24 yards across 50 offensive snaps while apparently picking up an injury at some point along the way.

items.head: Isaiah Williams (Ribs) is Questionable
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Williams won't practice Wednesday due to a rib injury, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports.

items.head: Season-high seven targets in Week 10
items.body: Williams caught four passes on seven targets for 24 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday. Williams' seven targets were his most of the season, and most of those looks came after Omar Cooper left early in the first quarter of Sunday's game due to an ankle injury. The injury was to the same foot that Cooper sustained a high-ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Titans, and an extended absence of the rookie first-rounder would result in Williams stepping into the WR3 role behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell. The Jets will hit the road for Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.head: Two grabs against Indy
items.body: Hutchinson caught two of three targets for 13 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Colts. Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.

items.head: Should benefit sans Harrison in Week 11
items.body: Hutchinson is expected to continue to benefit from elevated playing time Thursday against the Colts while Marvin Harrison (hamstring) is sidelined for a second straight game, Jared Koch of SI.com reports. Harrison hasn't exceeded a 50 percent snap share in any of his three appearances with the Texans since coming over in a trade with the Cardinals, but his absence for the Week 10 loss to the Browns still proved beneficial for Hutchinson. The fourth-year wideout out of Iowa State tied his season high with nine targets against the Browns, finishing with four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown while playing more than three-fourths of the offensive snaps for a second consecutive contest. Another healthy snap share should await Hutchinson in Week 11, and he could represent the No. 2 option in the Houston passing game behind top target Nico Collins.

items.head: Records TD grab in loss
items.body: Hutchinson brought in four of nine targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Hutchinson, who was checked for a concussion during the fourth quarter, finished second across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Texans. He also recorded a touchdown grab for the third straight game on an 11-yard catch early in the second quarter, and his receiving yardage tally was his highest since Week 5. Hutchinson now sports a 28-345-3 receiving line on 54 targets as he continues to function in a steady complementary role heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

items.head: Back in Sunday's game
items.body: Hutchinson (head) returned to Sunday's contest at Cleveland, Aaron WIlson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. After being checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter Sunday, Hutchinson was cleared to reenter this Week 10 matchup. Before his exit, he notched four catches (on seven targets) for 58 yards and one touchdown.

items.head: Being evaluated for possible concussion
items.body: Hutchinson is under evaluated for a possible concussion during Sunday's game in Cleveland. At the time of his exit in the fourth quarter, Hutchinson had four catches (on seven targets) for 58 yards and one touchdown. With Marvin Harrison (hamstring) inactive, Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Kayshon Boutte and Nikko Remigio are the Texans' healthy and available wide receivers.

items.head: Scores TD in high-scoring win
items.body: Hutchinson caught three of five targets for 29 yards and a touchdown and  added a 28-yard kick return during Sunday's 44-22 win against the Chargers. Hutchinson finished tied with Kayshon Boutte for second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tank Dell (nine). Hutchinson was able to reach paydirt for the second straight contest, reeling in a 17-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud for the team's first score of the day in the first quarter. There are many mouths to feed in Houston's passing attack, so Hutchinson will remain a volatile fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Browns.

items.head: Goose egg against Houston
items.body: Treadwell failed to catch his lone target in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans. Treadwell played a position-high 40 of 50 offensive snaps but continues to run wind sprints in an offense that doesn't throw the ball down the field. Through 11 games this season, Treadwell has just 19 catches for 239 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets.

items.head: Hauls in first touchdown of 2026
items.body: Treadwell caught three passes on as many targets for 24 yards and a touchdown during Indianapolis' 24-22 win over Miami on Sunday. Week 10 was the Colts' first game without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, who were traded to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, on Tuesday. Treadwell led all Colts wide receivers with three catches and 52 offensive snaps, and he connected with Daniel Jones for a seven-yard touchdown pass late in the second quarter to give Indianapolis a 14-7 halftime lead. It was the first time Treadwell found the end zone this season, and the 2016 first-rounder figures to maintain a larger role in the offense given the departure of the Colts' top targets at the trade deadline. The Colts will hit the road for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday, and Houston's defense ranks 28th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing wide receivers.

items.head: Blanked in Week 9
items.body: Treadwell logged 52 of the Colts' 64 snaps and was held without a reception on one target in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.

items.head: Titans' Calvin Ridley facing misdemeanor assault charge over airport incident
items.body: Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley is facing a misdemeanor assault charge as a result of a Nov. 7 incident at Nashville International Airport.

items.head: Plays only four snaps in Week 10 loss
items.body: Ridley played four offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. Even though Carnell Tate (shoulder) was sidelined for a second consecutive week, Ridley was barely involved in the Titans' offensive game plan. Ridley's four offensive snaps were by far a season low, and his role figures to shrink even more given that Tate is expected to return for Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22. Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) could be sidelined for that contest, although those offensive snaps likely will go to Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike and even practice-squad wideout Xavier Restrepo rather than Ridley.

items.head: Titans' Calvin Ridley addresses incident with valet at Nashville airport
items.body: Titans WR Calvin Ridley addressed the incident that occurred over the weekend at Nashville International Airport involving a valet as he attempted to recover the keys to his truck.

items.head: Involved in incident at airport over weekend
items.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh confirmed Monday that Ridley was involved in an "unfortunate" interaction over the weekend at Nashville International Airport that is now in the hands of law enforcement, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports. Though neither the Titans nor the police have publicly shared details pertaining to the incident, Saleh described it as a "very minor miscommunication." Saleh didn't indicate that Ridley's availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars is in any jeopardy following the incident, though the 31-year-old wideout could be a candidate to get dealt elsewhere ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Ridley has been limited to six receptions for 91 yards on 13 targets through seven appearances and doesn't look to be a major part of the 1-7 Titans' immediate or long-term plans.

items.head: C.J. Stroud stays in 'groove' with another 3-TD night in Texans' blowout of Colts
items.body: C.J. Stroud had his third straight game with at least three touchdown passes and led the Texans to their fourth win in six games Thursday night against the Colts.

items.head: Keeps piling up TDs in win
items.body: Stroud completed 21 of 26 passes for 194 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed six times for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and he'll take a sparkling 22:4 TD:INT into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Three more TDs in loss
items.body: Stroud completed 20 of 38 passes for 211 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 20 yards in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Stroud looked like he was on his way to another highly productive day early while helping stake the Texans to a 17-0 lead in the first half, but the fourth-year signal-caller and his offense largely stagnated in the second half. Stroud spread the ball around while connecting with eight different targets overall, and his trio of scoring strikes went to Nico Collins (12 yards), Xavier Hutchinson (11 yards) and Dalton Schultz (11 yards), the latter accounting for Houston's only second-half points. Despite the Texans' monumental collapse, Stroud's highly impressive season continues, as he's up to 2,462 passing yards, a 19:3 TD:INT and 120 rushing yards and another score heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

items.head: A 'confident' C.J. Stroud soaks in five-TD day against Chargers
items.body: Stroud matched his career high with five TD passes and added 384 passing yards in the win.

items.head: Tosses five touchdowns
items.body: Stroud completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception and recorded two carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win at the Chargers. Stroud matched a career high with his five TD strikes, which went to Xavier Hutchinson (17 yards), Tank Dell (63), Kayshon Boutte (12 and 63) and Nico Collins (13). Moreover, Stroud's 384 passing yards matched the second most in a game in his career. He's now thrown for multiple touchdowns in four of the last five games, a stretch in which he's accounted for a remarkable 1,457 yards through the air and a 13:2 TD:INT. Stroud will attempt to keep things rolling next Sunday, when the Texans visit the Browns.

items.head: Records first career touchdown
items.body: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Paces pass catchers in lopsided loss
items.body: Gould secured two of three targets for 48 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. Gould was the rather unlikely leader in receiving yards for the Colts on the night, with a team-high 31-yard catch playing a big role in getting him there. The 2024 fifth-round pick has seen an expanded role in the wake of the trades of Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and for as long as Alec Pierce (IR, heel) is sidelined, Gould could function as one of Indianapolis' top downfield threats for either Daniel Jones, Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard.

items.head: Anthony Gould (injury) is Active
items.body: Gould secured two of three targets for 48 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.

items.head: Active versus Houston
items.body: Gould (toe) is active for Thursday night's game against the Texans. Gould was listed as questionable but is good to go for the divisional affair. He played 32 of 59 offensive snaps last Sunday against Miami, the Colts' first game since trading both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. Gould manned the slot role vacated by Downs and secured two of four targets for 28 yards. He's a non-flashy but viable click in PPR-based fantasy formats.

items.head: Limited in Tuesday's session
items.body: The Colts listed Gould (toe) as a limited participant in Tuesday's walk-through practice. Indianapolis has now estimated Gould as limited on both of its first two practice reports of Week 11, after he emerged from Sunday's 24-22 win over the Dolphins with the toe injury. His status for Thursday's game against the Texans is muddled for the moment, but Gould could clear up any concern about his availability by turning in a full practice Wednesday. After Indianapolis shipped out two receivers (Keenan Allen and Josh Downs) at the trade deadline, Gould stepped in as the Colts' top option in the slot in Week 10 and finished with two receptions for 28 yards on four targets.

items.head: Anthony Gould (Toe) is Questionable
items.body: The Colts listed Gould (toe) as a limited participant in Tuesday's walk-through practice.

items.head: Estimated as limited Monday
items.body: Gould (toe) was estimated as limited in Monday's walkthrough practice. It's a new injury for Gould, who started Sunday against the Dolphins in the Colts' first game without both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, who were both dealt at the trade deadline last week. Gould played 32 of 59 offensive snaps versus Miami and registered two catches for 28 yards on four targets.

items.head: Stepping into slot role
items.body: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Gould is in line to step into the slot role previously held by Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. With both Downs and Keenan Allen having been dealt by the Colts on Tuesday, the team will be operating with a re-shaped WR corps going forward. According to the Colts' latest unofficial depth chart, Gould is indeed listed a first-teamer along with Ashton Dulin and Laquon Treadwell. Also expected to have additional opportunities in the coming weeks will be 2026 seventh-rounder Deion Burks, with veteran pass catcher Nick Westbrook-Ikhine in the mix as well after being signed off the practice squad. Though a wait-and-see approach is in order in term's of Gould's fantasy lineup viability, his production beginning this weekend versus Miami is worth tracking by those in deeper PPR formats.

items.head: Double-digit yardage on one catch
items.body: Schultz brought in his only target for 11 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Schultz had a minimal role on a night when C.J. Stroud threw for a modest 194 yards and recorded completions to nine different targets. The veteran tight end now has consecutive one-catch, 11-yard tallies after recording multiple receptions in each of his first eight games of the season, and Schultz's production will remain hard to trust heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: First TD of season in loss
items.body: Schultz caught one pass for an 11-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. While Schultz got into the end zone for the first time this campaign, his catches and targets were new single-game lows for 2026. Schultz has yet to produce more than 45 yards in a game when Nico Collins is healthy this season. The veteran tight end is a low-floor, TD-or-bust fantasy bet.

items.head: Two grabs in Week 9 win
items.body: Schultz caught two of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.

items.head: Three catches in Week 11 win
items.body: Dell secured three of four targets for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Three receptions in Week 10 loss
items.body: Dell brought in three of four targets for 21 yards and rushed once for no gain in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. One week after posting a 105-yard effort against the Chargers in only his second game since 2024, Dell saw a big downturn in yardage Sunday. Nevertheless, the fact he retained a solid complementary role was encouraging, and the speedy wideout seems to be playing unencumbered by any physical or mental limitations following the recovery from his devastating knee injury. Dell will look to boost his yardage back up in a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday
items.body: Dell (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Browns, while teammate Marvin Harrison (hamstring) has been ruled out. Last week, Dell caught four passes for 104 yards and a TD in a 44-22 win over the Chargers, leading Houston in targets (nine) in his second game back from a lengthy absence. His snap share (45 percent) and route share (55 percent) were less encouraging, but Dell and Kayshon Boutte are candidates for more playing time with Harrison out for at least one week.

items.head: Limited in practice Wednesday
items.body: Dell (hand) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Dell operated as the Texans' third receiver for much of last Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers, running 22 routes on C.J. Stroud's 38 dropbacks. In just his second game since Week 16 of the 2024 campaign, Dell turned nine targets into five catches for 104 yards and a touchdown against Los Angeles. He's become a legitimate name to add in fantasy football ahead of Sunday's Week 10 date with the Browns.

items.head: Tank Dell (Hand) is Questionable
items.body: Dell (hand) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.

items.head: First touchdown since 2024
items.body: Dell turned a team-high nine targets into four catches for 105 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 44-22 road victory against the Chargers In his second appearance since returning from a brutal left knee injury suffered in December 2024, Dell again recorded a reception of 40-plus yards, connecting with C.J. Stroud for a 63-yard TD in the second quarter. It was one of five touchdown passes for Stroud, who spread the ball around to nine different pass catchers and four that reached the end zone at least once. Dell will aim to build on the momentum next Sunday at Cleveland.

items.head: Good yardage on one catch
items.body: Warren brought in one of five targets for 22 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday. The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick now has recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Jones, who James Boyd of The Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after the game, is replaced by Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard under center.

items.head: Next to nothing with three touches
items.body: Warren rushed once for three yards and brought in two of three targets for one yard in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. The new-look Colts offense was without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen after trade-deadline moves, but Warren was still surprisingly uninvolved. Daniel Jones completed only 50.0 percent of his passes and threw for just 108 yards, however, so Warren's minimal production is somewhat understandable in that context. Jones has thrown for under 200 yards in four consecutive games and is playing generally uninspired football, so Warren's fantasy outlook remains shaky for the time being but could improve if Anthony Richardson takes over under center at some point.

items.head: More targets on tap?
items.body: Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports. The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.

items.head: Solid yardage with four catches
items.body: Warren brought in four of seven targets for 44 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. Warren tied for second in receptions and finished as the runner-up in both receiving yards and targets after a slow start to Sunday's loss. The second-year tight end's role could be even bigger by next Sunday's Week 10 home matchup against the Dolphins, as the Colts could conceivably move both Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, not to mention quarterback Daniel Jones, by Tuesday's trade deadline. Warren has at least four receptions in every game with the exception of Week 1 heading into the aforementioned matchup against Miami.

items.head: Minimal production with 15 touches
items.body: Taylor rushed 11 times for 21 yards and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
