Taylor put some distance between himself and promising rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan in terms of workload, as the former outpaced his teammate in carries by an 11-3 margin, even with the latter exiting before halftime with a hamstring injury. However, the extra opportunity was a moot point, as Taylor couldn't find any space to operate as either a runner or receiver. Daniel Jones' mediocre play under center certainly isn't helping the ground attack's cause, and Taylor now has recorded less than 50 rushing yards in three of the last four contests. The star running back will have some additional time to prepare for a relatively favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Clears century mark in scrimmage yards
items.body: Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards and brought in two of four targets for 20 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Indianapolis. Taylor made it through the trade deadline unscathed after rumors swirled around a possible change of scenery, but the talented back still split plenty of work with rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan, who logged 12 carries. Taylor still remained the No. 1 option and was the only one of the two to see any targets, and the rushing yardage total was his best since Week 7, just before serious trade speculation began. Taylor is staying put for the rest of the campaign, but it seems likely that he'll continue ceding a fair share of touches to McGowan moving forward.

items.head: Jonathan Taylor focused on being leader for Colts with trade deadline drama over
items.body: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor said he has turned his attention toward the future after the team's big moves ahead of the NFL trade deadline.

items.head: Sticking around in Indy
items.body: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams offered no more than a second-round pick as the best asset in any trade pitch. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

items.head: NFL Week 10 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips, post-trade deadline news
items.body: No deals for Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones or Brian Thomas Jr.? Vikings seeking QB answers with their Kirk Cousins trade? Here's the latest intel.

items.head: Set to play Sunday amid trade rumors
items.body: Taylor was a full participant at Thursday's practice, and Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports that both Taylor and head coach Shane Steichen have maintained that Taylor will play Sunday against the Cowboys despite ongoing trade rumors surrounding the star running back. "You can't avoid it," Taylor said of the trade rumors. "But it's more about trying to block that out." Taylor's preparing for what could well be his last game as a member of the Colts. Per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, the 2-6 Colts have received trade calls on numerous players including Taylor, but Indianapolis doesn't intend to complete any additional trades prior to the conclusion of Sunday's game.

items.head: Gets into end zone Thursday
items.body: Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Very busy in Week 10 loss
items.body: Collins secured nine of 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Collins comfortably paced the Texans across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he added his fifth touchdown of the season on a 12-yard catch in the first quarter. Collins also had a 16-yard reception on Houston's last-gasp drive wiped out by an offensive holding penalty, but he still finished with season highs in receptions and targets. Collins retains an unquestioned No. 1 role in the Texans' prolific air attack, affording him an enticing combination of floor and upside heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

items.head: First TD since Week 4 on Sunday
items.body: Collins corralled all four of his targets for 55 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 44-22 victory at the Chargers. Collins was one of four Texans to reach the end zone via a pass from QB C.J. Stroud, who tossed five TDs in all. It marked Collins' first touchdown since Week 4, when he struck twice against the Cowboys, but overall his output from week to week this season has been a bit inconsistent, as he sits on a 28-384-4 line on 39 targets through his six appearances. He'll seek better results next Sunday in Cleveland.

items.head: Season-best effort in win
items.body: Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards and brought in three of four targets for 17 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday. Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Montgomery functioned as the clear lead back with Woody Marks (concussion) unavailable. The former put together the best rushing yardage total of his brief Texans tenure, handling his highest number of carries since Week 4 of his 2023 debut campaign with the Lions. Montgomery also was encouragingly involved in a complementary role in the passing game, and he'll now have some extra time to recover from Thursday's workload ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29. However, if Marks is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of that contest, Montgomery will see his touch count take a hit.

items.head: Ready to go for Thursday
items.body: Montgomery (groin) doesn't have an injury designation and is expected to play in Thursday's game against the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Montgomery was sidelined for the Texans' past four games due to the groin injury, but he's good to go for the Week 11 matchup after he was listed as a full practice participant from Monday through Wednesday. Before going down with the injury, Montgomery had been part of a timeshare with Woody Marks, but Montgomery will have a fairly clear path to a lead role Thursday with Marks sidelined due to a concussion. Montgomery made a splash in his Texans debut with three touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bills, but he accrued just 126 scoreless yards on 36 touches (32 carries, four receptions) across his subsequent four contests prior to the four-game absence.

items.head: On track to play Thursday
items.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed that Montgomery (groin) is trending toward playing in Thursday's game against the Colts, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. Montgomery has been sidelined for the Texans' past four games, but he concluded Week 10 prep as a full practice participant and appears to have shown continued improvement in his recovery from the groin injury in Week 11. After being listed as a full participant for Monday's walkthrough, Montgomery was on the practice field again Tuesday, with Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston noting that the 29-year-old was "feeling and moving a lot better" compared to previous weeks. With Woody Marks (concussion) expected to be sidelined Thursday, Montgomery should have a clear path to a lead role out of the backfield in his return to action.

items.head: David Montgomery (injury) is Active
items.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed that Montgomery (groin) is trending toward playing in Thursday's game against the Colts, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.

items.head: Taking part in practice Tuesday
items.body: Montgomery (groin) is slated to practice Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Listed as a full participant Monday for a walk-through session, Montgomery will take part in a proper practice Tuesday. According to Wilson, Montgomery is "feeling and moving a lot better" compared to previous weeks, so assuming he emerges from Tuesday's session no worse for the wear, the 29-year-old will likely lead the Houston backfield Thursday against the Colts in his first appearance since Week 5. Before missing time with the groin injury, Montgomery had fallen into a timeshare with Woody Marks after averaging just 2.7 yards per carry through the Texans' first five contests. Montgomery may not face much competition for reps in Week 11 with Marks tracking toward sitting out after sustaining a concussion in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.

items.head: Full walkthrough Monday
items.body: Montgomery (groin) was a full participant at Monday's walkthrough. Montgomery was held out of Sunday's loss at Cleveland, which marked his fourth absence in a row due to a groin injury. Head coach DeMeco Ryans said afterward that he's "not certain" if Montgomery will be able to play Thursday against the Colts, per DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com. Montgomery's full session was his second straight going back to last week, and assuming he's trending toward a return to action this week, he's poised to take on a large workload considering fellow RB Woody Marks is in the concussion protocol and was a DNP on Monday.

items.head: Status for Thursday to be determined
items.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Sunday that he's "not certain" if Montgomery (groin) will be able to play Thursday against Indianapolis, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN reports. Montgomery hasn't suited up since he suffered a groin injury Week 5 in Tennessee. However, he practiced in full this past Friday for the first time since getting hurt, and the Texans described his work during Week 10 prep as a "ramp-up" ahead of potentially returning Week 11. Ryans didn't sound certain after Sunday's loss to Cleveland that Montgomery will be able to play versus the Colts, but if the veteran running back does suit up, it could be a huge boost to a Houston offense that may be without the RB who has been filling in as the starter for Montgomery. Woody Marks suffered a concussion Sunday and isn't likely to be cleared in time to play Thursday.

items.head: Questionable for Sunday's game
items.body: Montgomery (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, while Woody Marks (knee) doesn't have an injury designation. Montgomery returned to practice Thursday after missing a month, and he upgraded from limited participation to full for Friday's practice. It's still not clear he'll be active ahead of the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday, so Marks could be tasked with a heavy workload for a fifth straight game. If Montgomery does return, he'll likely share work with Marks, making it difficult to trust either Houston RB in fantasy lineups.

items.head: Won't return to Thursday Night Football
items.body: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Texans, Jane Slater of NFL Network reports. McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

items.head: Questionable to return to TNF
items.body: McGowan is dealing with a hamstring injury and is questionable to return to Thursday's Week 11 game against Houston. McGowan appeared to get injured while returning a kickoff just before halftime. The rookie running back had three carries for seven yards and one catch for one yard before getting hurt. Should McGowan not be able to return to action Thursday, Jonathan Taylor would likely get an even bigger share of carries for the Colts, and DJ Giddens should get more opportunities as well.

items.head: Retains expanded role Sunday
items.body: McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. The rookie had shown well in recent weeks while trade speculation swirled around Jonathan Taylor, and even though the latter ultimately stayed put at the deadline, McGowan still compiled a new career high in rush attempts and rushing yards. The Kentucky product also followed up his first career rushing touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys with a four-yard scoring run early in the second quarter Sunday, and McGowan was also productive in his returner role. While Taylor should remain the de facto top backfield option for the Colts, McGowan should remain in an elevated role for what remains of Indianapolis' non-contending season.

items.head: Gets into end zone in loss
items.body: McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for minus-3 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. McGowan recorded his first NFL touchdown on a two-yard run in the first quarter, perhaps a harbinger of a larger role as early as next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins. McGowan came just a rush yard short of equaling his career-best tally in that category, and if Jonathan Taylor is indeed moved off the roster by Tuesday's trade deadline, the former would be in line to serve as the lead back moving forward.

items.body: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback for Thursday's game at Houston.

items.head: Back to limited practice
items.body: Spears (knee) was limited in practice Thursday. The running back returned to action last Sunday against the Jaguars and logged 16 snaps behind Tony Pollard's 41. Spears is only playable in Week 11 against Dallas as a desperation fantasy option.

items.head: Sits out Wednesday's practice
items.body: Spears (knee) didn't practice Wednesday. Spears has been regularly listed with a knee issue on Titans injury reports dating back to Week 6, but he was able to put an end to a two-game absence in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars and finished with four carries for 28 yards to go with one reception for no gain. The Titans haven't indicated that Spears experienced a setback with his knee coming out of that game, so it's possible that his absence from practice to kick off Week 11 prep may be maintenance-related. Spears' activity over the next two days should help determine his status for Sunday's game in Dallas.

items.head: Tyjae Spears (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: Spears (knee) didn't practice Wednesday.

items.head: Five touches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He turned one catch into zero yards on one target. After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Spears returned to play 16 offensive snaps. Tony Pollard (41 snaps) remains the clear-cut lead back on this cellar-dwelling Tennessee team. Spears has minimal fantasy appeal now that Pollard survived the trade deadline and will finish out the season with the Titans.

items.head: Tyjae Spears (injury) is Active
items.body: Spears rushed four times for 28 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He turned one catch into zero yards on one target.

items.head: Cleared to return for Week 10
items.body: Spears (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. After entering the weekend listed as questionable, Spears has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence due to a knee injury. Nicholas Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's AFC South tilt, so Spears and Julius Chestnut will serve as the Titans' backfield depth options behind RB1 Tony Pollard.

items.head: On track to return Sunday
items.body: Spears (knee) is expected to play Sunday against the Jaguars, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. Spears, who hasn't played since Week 6, advanced from a 'DNP' on Wednesday to a limited session Thursday, before working fully Friday and being listed as questionable heading into the weekend. His looming return would provide a boost the Titans' Week 10 RB depth, but prior to his injury, Spears' fantasy impact was modest, with 18 carries for 66 yards and 15 catches for 75 yards on 17 targets in six contests.

items.head: Questionable after full practice
items.body: Spears (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jaguars after upgrading to full practice participation Friday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports. A return to action after missing two games would hurt Tony Pollard's workload projection, though Pollard would still be in line for most of the carries. There have also been hints of rookie Nicholas Singleton getting playing time in the second half of the season, leaving Spears without much of a path to mainstream fantasy value.

items.head: Jordan James (Calf) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Limited to return duties vs. Dallas
items.body: James returned five kickoffs for 101 yards during the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. James set the tone right out of halftime with a 49-yard kickoff return, although the yards gained were mitigated by a holding penalty by the Niners. All eight of his snaps came on special teams, and it looks like the second-year pro is out of the mix for backfield touches behind RB1 Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black, the latter of whom found the end zone for the second time in his last three outings. The 49ers will travel to Mexico City for Week 11 to face the Vikings on Nov. 22.

items.head: Logs three carries in Week 9 win
items.body: James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas. As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second-most this season behind the four touches he logged Week 2 versus Miami. James will likely be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black were to miss time.

items.head: Ray Davis (injury) is Active
items.body: Davis (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Davis (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice. It's a new injury for the running back, which clouds his status for Week 11 against the Dolphins. If Davis is unable to handle his normal handful of snaps, Frank Gore could be elevated from the practice squad.

items.head: Nursing hamstring injury
items.body: Davis was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury. Davis is making his first appearance on the injury report since Week 8, when he missed a practice due to an illness. Unless the hamstring issue was something that resulted in him exiting Wednesday's session early, Davis should still have decent odds of being ready to play Sunday against the Dolphins. The third-year back has seen limited playing time behind James Cook and Ty Johnson this season, earning no more than six touches in any of his nine appearances to date.

items.head: Ray Davis (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Minimal production in Monday night win
items.body: Davis logged two carries for two yards and didn't catch his only target Monday in a 23-6 victory against the Vikings. Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in the Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.

items.head: Remains limited at Thursday's practice
items.body: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, also was limited Wednesday. Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

items.head: In non-contact jersey Thursday
items.body: McConkey (back) was spotted at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports. McConkey was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and the fact that he's in a non-contact jersey a day later suggests that the WR will log another limited listing Thursday. If that's the case, McConkey likely will have to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Jets without an injury designation.

items.head: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. After missing the Chargers' last game with a back issue, McConkey's return to limited work is an encouraging step in his preparation for Week 11 against the Jets. His practice status over the rest of the week should provide more clarity on his availability for Sunday. There's no sugar-coating it that McConkey's season has been a complete disappointment to date, as he's battled multiple different injuries that have caused him to miss three entire games and parts of several others. He's difficult to trust for fantasy until he puts something together in the box score and makes it through an entire game healthy.

items.head: Questionable for Monday Night Football
items.body: McConkey (back) is listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports. Although he was active for the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, McConkey didn't end up playing a single snap due to back spasms. His practice reps were restricted during Week 10 prep, and the questionable tag means McConkey's official status may not be known until the Chargers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before Monday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. If McConkey is ruled out or available only on an emergency basis, then Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith would operate as the Chargers' top wideouts against Baltimore.

items.head: Remains sidelined at practice Friday
items.body: McConkey (back) didn't practice Friday. McConkey -- who dealt with back spasms last Sunday and as a result didn't log any snaps in the 0-8 Chargers' loss to the Texans, has now missed back-to-back practices, so what he's able to do Saturday will be pivotal with regard to his status for Monday night's game against the Ravens. If McConkey is unavailable for the contest, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith would be in line to head Los Angeles' WR corps, as they did versus Houston.

items.head: Sits out Thursday's practice
items.body: McConkey (back) didn't practice Thursday. Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com relayed Monday that Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh viewed McConkey as "day to day" with the back spasms that led to the wideout not logging any snaps in this past Sunday's loss to the Texans. With a 'DNP' on the record for Thursday, McConkey now has two more chances to practice ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

items.head: Deemed day-to-day by Harbaugh
items.body: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that McConkey is viewed as "day to day" with back spasms, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but he didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

items.head: Pregame back spasms lead to Week 9 absence
items.body: McConkey was active but didn't play any snaps in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports. Because McConkey sustained the injury after the Chargers had already announced their inactive list, the wideout ended up being active but unavailable for the second time in three games. Back in Week 5, McConkey had been managing a foot injury but still proceeded to suit up for a matchup with Denver, though he didn't see any action and was active only because the Chargers had seven other players dealing with more significant health concerns. McConkey also made early exits in Week 1 due to a rib injury, Week 4 due to the foot issue and in Week 6 due to a concussion. The mounting injuries have made it increasingly difficult for fantasy managers to depend on McConkey, whose lack of availability has been one of many reasons that the 0-8 Chargers have taken a massive step back on offense in 2026.

items.head: Ditches protective glove on left hand
items.body: Shough is no longer wearing a protect glove on his left (non-throwing) hand at Thursday's practice, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.

items.head: Weak showing in loss to Carolina
items.body: Shough completed 25 of 35 targets for 187 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added 25 rushing yards on six carries and was charged with a lost fumble. The second-year QB had more turnovers than TDs for only the second time this season, although his fumble may have been been more Audric Estime's fault, and Shough fell short of 200 passing yards for the third time. Rookie Jordyn Tyson was his top downfield option, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in a breakout performance, but no other Saint saw more than five targets or hauled in more than three passes. Shough will take a 15:7 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Bears.

items.head: Does just enough in OT win
items.body: Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. New Orleans got by with three Charlie Smyth field goals and an Audric Estime two-yard TD run in regulation, but Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in OT that held up as the winning score when the Browns scored on the subsequent possession but failed on a two-point attempt -- the same way the Saints lost to the Lions in their season opener. Shough will take a 14:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

items.head: Still has glove on non-throwing hand
items.body: Shough was still wearing a glove on his left hand during pregame warmups ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, according to Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune. As Johnson notes, Shough wasn't listed on the Saints' Week 9 injury report, as he was (as a full participant) in Week 7, prior to the team's bye. With no reported reported setbacks, Shough -- who sustained two broken bones in his left (non-throwing) hand Oct. 5 -- is presumably simply protecting his hand until it's 100 percent healed. On the plus side from the QB's perspective as he continues to play through the issue is the fact highly-touted rookie WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) -- the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is making his much-awaited regular-season debut for New Orleans.

items.head: Logs full practice Thursday
items.body: Smith (hamstring) practiced fully Thursday. Smith followed up Wednesday's limited showing with an uncapped session one day later, thereby paving the way for his first game action since Week 6. Despite missing five of the last six contests due to a hamstring injury, he put together a 26-310-2 line on 41 targets in his four appearances this season. However, with Jalen Hurts (blood clots) out for the rest of the 2026 campaign, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from Joe Milton on Sunday against the Steelers.

items.head: DeVonta Smith (injury) is Active
items.body: Smith (hamstring) practiced fully Thursday.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Smith (hamstring) is taking part in Thursday's practice, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports. Smith got back on the practice field Wednesday for the first time since his last game action in Week 6, going down as a limited participant. He has sessions lined up Thursday and Friday to be listed as full, at which point he may be tagged with a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Steelers.

items.head: Limited in return to practice
items.body: Smith (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Calls himself '100 percent'
items.body: Smith (hamstring) said Wednesday that he's "100 percent healthy," Eliot Shorr-Parks of Sports Radio 94 WIP Philadelphia reports. That's not to say Smith will go down as a full participant Wednesday, which marked his first on-field work since Week 6 due to a lingering hamstring injury. His activity level will become known once the Eagles post their first Week 11 practice report.

items.head: Back at practice Wednesday
items.body: Smith (hamstring) was spotted practicing Wednesday, Tim McManus of ESPN reports. The Eagles are getting healthier coming out of the bye, with both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) present for the media viewing period of practice. That Smith is practicing in any capacity on a Wednesday bodes well for his status going into the Week 11 matchup with Pittsburgh, though the injury reports will give more detail on how much he's progressing. Regardless, this is a step in the right direction for Smith's return to action.

items.head: Trending toward being back this week
items.body: Coach Nick Sirianni indicated Wednesday that he feels good about Smith (hamstring) returning to action Sunday against the Steelers, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports. The same applies to fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), and if the duo is available this weekend, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon could see decreased opportunities in Week 11. While Sirianni is hopeful that Smith and Wicks are ready to return, per Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia, at this stage he's not ready to make any promises regarding their availability versus Pittsburgh.

items.head: DeVonta Smith (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Sidelined for Thursday's practice
items.body: Cooper didn't practice Thursday due to ankle and hip injuries. Cooper made an early exit from this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle, and the rookie wideout is also nursing a hip issue as the Jets prepare for a matchup this weekend with the Chargers. With two straight absences from practice to begin the week, Cooper will likely need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance at suiting up Sunday.

items.head: Won't practice Wednesday
items.body: Cooper (ankle) isn't practicing Wednesday, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports. Cooper logged just one snap this past Sunday against the Bills after tweaking the same ankle he hurt in Week 1, which led to an IR stint. The rookie WR will now have two more chances to practice this week, but if he's sidelined this weekend against the Chargers, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell would likely be busy in Week 11, with Isaiah Williams (seven targets versus Buffalo) also factoring in.

items.head: Headed for imaging on ankle
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Cooper (ankle) will undergo imaging Monday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports. Cooper played just one snap before exiting Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle. Notably, the rookie first-round pick tweaked the same ankle in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, which resulted in a stint on injured reserve. The Jets are hoping that Cooper avoided as significant of an injury this time around, though even if his imaging yields good news, he still could be hard-pressed to suit up next Sunday versus the Chargers.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of Sunday's game
items.body: Cooper (ankle) won't return to Sunday's game against the Bills, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports. After being deemed questionable to return to the contest earlier Sunday, Cooper has now been ruled out and will target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Chargers. In his absence versus Buffalo, Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams are available lead New York's WR corps.

items.head: Active Sunday
items.body: Cooper (ankle) is active for Sunday's contest against the Bills. Cooper opened Week 10 prep listed as limited on back-to-back practice reports due to an ankle injury, but despite logging a full session Friday, the Jets tagged him as questionable for Sunday. Fellow WRs Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Adonai Mitchell (knee) also were listed as questionable, but all three now are available to the Jets offense. Cooper has been hit or miss this season, with two outings of at least 100 yards and exactly one TD, while he combined for a 9-88-0 line on 14 targets in his other three appearances.

items.head: Will practice fully Friday
items.body: Cooper (ankle) will be a full practice participant Friday, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports. After logging limited practices earlier in the week, Cooper may avoid an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with the Bills. Fellow Jets wideout Garrett Wilson (concussion) also has a chance to be cleared before Sunday, as he's upgrading to full practice participation Friday along with Cooper.

items.head: Officially limited Thursday
items.body: Cooper (ankle) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice. Cooper officially goes down as a limited participant for a second consecutive practice, matching the participation level of Garrett Wilson (concussion). Since returning from an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve, Cooper has 19 catches for 276 yards and two touchdowns in four games, even with a zero-catch Week 8 performance during that stretch.

items.head: Practicing Thursday
items.body: Cooper (ankle) is participating in Thursday's practice, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports. Both Cooper and Garrett Wilson (concussion) were spotted at practice Thursday after logging limited practice sessions Wednesday. It remains to be seen whether either wide receiver will upgrade to full participation Thursday ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

items.head: Another full practice
items.body: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over the last handful of games to retain a notable role in the Steelers' receiving corps.

items.head: Cleared to practice Wednesday
items.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that Wilson (finger) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports. McCarthy suggested earlier in the week that Wilson could be cleared to play Sunday in Philadelphia, and the Steelers' decision to open the wideout's 21-day practice window is the first step in him potentially playing for the first time since Week 5. Through the Steelers' first five games of the season, Wilson recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns on 25 targets, but it's not clear where exactly he'll settle in the pecking order at receiver once healthy. Like Wilson, veteran wideout Michael Pittman (foot) had his 21-day window opened Wednesday and could be on a similar timeline for a return. Additionally, rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard has proven to be a reliable target for Aaron Rodgers in the short and intermediate areas of the field over the past few weeks and could maintain a notable role once Wilson and Pittman are back in the fold.

items.head: Roman Wilson (Finger) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he's "hopeful" Wilson (finger) will be able to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.

items.head: Full practice Thursday
items.body: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports. It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.

items.head: Workload managed during Week 10 win
items.body: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said that Higgins was held out late in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers for workload-management purposes, Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer reports. Higgins still logged 51 of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps, clearing the 75-percent threshold for the fifth time in his last seven appearances. He finished the game with five catches (on six targets) for 66 yards, and he may have had a better receiving line had the game been closer. If Higgins is working through an injury, it will be known after the Bengals post their first Week 11 practice report Wednesday. Through nine outings on the season, Higgins has produced a 53-824-6 line on 73 targets.

items.head: Five catches in Week 10 win
items.body: Higgins brought in five of six targets for 66 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. Ja'Marr Chase stole the show in the Bengals' air attack with an 11-catch, 231-yard effort, so Higgins was a distant second in receiving yards to his elite position mate. However, the latter's night was still reasonably productive, and Higgins has at least five receptions in four consecutive contests heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Commanders on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.head: Finds end zone twice in win over Falcons
items.body: Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta. While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.

items.head: LeQuint Allen Jr. (injury) is Active
items.body: Allen (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

items.head: LeQuint Allen Jr. (Hamstring) is Questionable

items.head: Remains limited in practice
items.body: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

items.head: Jakobi Meyers (injury) is Questionable
items.body: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Three grabs in Week 10 win
items.body: Meyers caught three of six targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The six targets were second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington's nine, but Meyers' longest gain of the day went for only 15 yards. The veteran wideout has also failed to find the end zone in six straight games, a stretch in which he's managed just a 19-256-0 line on 32 targets. Meyers will try to end that drought in a Week 11 clash against the Giants.

items.head: Jakobi Meyers (injury) is Active
items.body: Meyers caught three of six targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.

items.head: Good to go this week
items.body: Myers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports. Meyers has fought through one injury or another for most of the season. This week, he managed limited practices Thursday and Friday, setting him up to play against the last-place Titans.

items.head: Limited at practice Thursday
items.body: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice. Meyers has managed one injury or another throughout the season without missing any games. His return to practice Thursday after a Wednesday absence suggests this may just be another cause of maintenance/caution. If Meyers plays, he'll face a Tennessee defense that's allowing a league 40.7 PPR points per game to wide receivers.

items.head: Doesn't practice Wednesday
items.body: Meyers (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week, before playing 68 percent of snaps and catching four passes for 65 yards in a Thursday blowout at Baltimore. It's unclear if he ankle has worsened or Wednesday's absence is just a matter of caution/maintenance. Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would all be candidates for additional WR snaps if Meyers were to miss time this year.

items.head: Jakobi Meyers (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Meyers (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports. Both Tremble and Darren Waller (knee) were upgraded to limited work after being DNP on Wednesday. Friday's participation levels and injury designations will tell a better story for their Week 11 availability versus Baltimore. Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are next in line at tight end for Carolina.

items.head: Managing knee issue in Week 11
items.body: Tremble didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, with head coach Dave Canales noting after the session that the tight end's injury is a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports. Canales said the same about Darren Waller (knee), who was also a non-participant to open Week 11 prep. The practice activity of the Panthers' top two tight ends will thus warrant monitoring over the next two days to get a sense if either player will be available to play Sunday versus the Ravens. Beyond Tremble and Waller, the Panthers have three other tight ends -- Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders -- on the 53-man roster.

items.head: Tommy Tremble (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: Tremble didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, with head coach Dave Canales noting after the session that the tight end's injury is a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.

items.head: Four catches in Week 10 win
items.body: Tremble caught four of five targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. The tight end's five targets tie Chuba Hubbard for second on the team behind Tetairoa McMillan's seven. Tremble has yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, and his four catches matched his season high. More of a blocker and red-zone specialist, Tremble has very little fantasy appeal in a Carolina offense that likes to use three tight ends.

items.head: Four grabs, TD in loss to Denver
items.body: Tremble caught four of six targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. The Panthers continue to use three tight ends heavily on offense, and Tremble has settled in as the do-it-all tight member of the trio, while Darren Waller is solely a pass catcher and Mitchell Evans focuses on blocking. Tremble doesn't have nearly the upside of Waller, but the former still draws Bryce Young's eye in the red zone. On the year, Tremble is up to 21 grabs for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 30 targets across eight games. He's not an exciting fantasy option.

items.head: Vikings' Cousins channeling Dantonio's 'slow down' maxim amid whirlwind month
items.body: As he manages the whirlwind of his professional and personal life this month, Vikings QB Kirk Cousins has relied on a maxim he often heard from his college coach Mark Dantonio at Michigan State -- when things speed up, try to slow down.

items.head: How Vikings got Kirk Cousins ready to win on short notice
items.body: Cousins and coach Kevin O'Connell deferred to each other until they each needed to take control Sunday.

items.head: Tosses two TDs in Minnesota return
items.body: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries. Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

items.head: Could stay in Minnesota beyond 2026
items.body: The Vikings have already gauged Cousins' interest in returning to the team in 2027 since acquiring him Tuesday in a trade with the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Cousins -- who will start Sunday's game in Green Bay as he dons a Minnesota uniform for the first time since 2023 -- is set to become a free agent in the spring, but if all goes well over the next several weeks, the Vikings are hoping that the 38-year-old quarterback can be more than just a half-season rental. At the very least, the Vikings are counting on Cousins to provide a short-term upgrade under center from the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring) and Carson Wentz, both of whom struggled to move the chains while Minnesota raced to a 6-2 start thanks in large part to its blitz-happy, aggressive defense. During his time in Las Vegas, Cousins tossed 20 touchdown passes (second in NFL) and compiled 2,340 passing yards (fifth in NFL), despite playing alongside one of the league's weaker wide-receiver groups.

items.head: Starting in Week 10
items.body: Head coach Kevin O'Connell announced Friday that Cousins will start Sunday's contest at Green Bay. Cousins was acquired from the Raiders before Tuesday's trade deadline, and after leading the first-team offense during the entirety of Week 10 prep, he'll get the nod under center in his return to Minnesota. In nine starts with Las Vegas this season, he completed 202 of 315 passes (64 percent) for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions while adding two more TDs on the ground.

items.head: Expected to start versus Green Bay
items.body: Cousins is expected to start Sunday's game against the Packers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and unsurprisingly he's trending toward being immediately installed as the starter, as his new team is in the midst of a two-game skid. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) viewed as week-to-week,  Carson Wentz (ankle, limited at practice Thursday) -- if available -- and Max Brosmer profile as his Week 10 backup options. Prior to being dealt, Cousins was playing well for Las Vegas, and his addition to the Minnesota offense should result in a boost for the team's top pass catchers, Justin Jefferson, T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison.

items.head: Vikings 'hyped' to welcome back 'leader' Cousins on 1st day of practice
items.body: The Minnesota Vikings reveled Thursday in quarterback Kirk Cousins' first full day back with the organization.

items.head: Uncertain to start Sunday
items.body: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that he isn't ready to commit to Cousins as the Vikings' Week 10 starting quarterback, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Minnesota acquired Cousins via trade from Las Vegas on Tuesday, but even though he has experience working under O'Connell from his previous stint with the team in 2022 and 2023, the coach will wait to make a decision. It appears Kyler Murray (hamstring) is set to miss another game Sunday at Green Bay, meaning Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer are the options to get the call this weekend.

items.head: Recovering from meniscus surgery
items.body: Kirk announced Wednesday via his personal Instagram account that he recently underwent meniscus surgery. After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

items.head: Limited with illness
items.body: Jones (illness) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports. Jones managed to practice through his illness in a limited fashion Wednesday. It remains to be seen whether the quarterback will overcome the sickness before Sunday's contest against the Vikings. If Jones cannot suit up, Kurtis Rourke would become the backup to Brock Purdy for Week 11.

items.head: Mac Jones (Illness) is Questionable
items.body: Jones (illness) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.

items.head: Too pricey for Minnesota
items.body: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries in Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports. Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders prior to the deadline.

items.head: Dont'e Thornton Jr. (injury) is Active
items.body: Thornton (back) was a full participant in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Dont'e Thornton Jr. (Back) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Jackson Hawes (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: Hawes (shoulder) was a late addition to Wednesday's injury report, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News.

items.head: Jared Wiley (Ankle) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.

items.head: Jared Wiley (Ankle) is Out
items.body: Wiley suffered a fractured ankle in the Chiefs' 35-13 victory over the Falcons on Sunday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.

items.head: CJ Donaldson (injury) is Active
items.body: Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Yet to practice since Week 7 injury
items.body: Donaldson (shoulder) remained a non-participant at Thursday's practice. Donaldson has yet to resume practicing since sustaining a shoulder injury in Week 7, which suggests he's trending for another absence in Sunday's Week 10 matchup with the Panthers. Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are both expected to be available, while Travis Etienne's (hamstring) status is up in the air as the latter tries to work his way back from a hamstring injury that landed him on IR.

items.head: CJ Donaldson (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: CJ Donaldson (Shoulder) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: Charlie Kolar (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: Kolar (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday.

items.head: Hauls in two passes vs. Baltimore
items.body: Kolar caught two of three passes for 16 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. Kolar's 41 offensive snaps were by far the most among Chargers tight ends, well ahead of a returning David Njoku (19) and Oronde Gadsden (12), although the latter briefly left Monday's game due to an eye injury. That said, Kolar was held to two catches or fewer for the second time in three games, and he has not seen a red zone target from Justin Herbert since Week 6 against the Chiefs. Kolar has amassed a 15-145-0 receiving line on 23 targets across seven regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Tallies three catches against Houston
items.body: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

items.head: Officially limited Wednesday
items.body: Shipley (foot) was a limited practice participant Wednesday. Shipley sustained a partial tear of his plantar fascia in Week 5 against the Jaguars in London, resulting in an IR stint. He missed the last four games before a Week 10 bye before the Eagles designated him for return Monday. No. 1 RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) practiced fully Wednesday, so if Shipley gains clearance to play Sunday versus the Steelers, it'll likely be in a complementary role out of the backfield.

items.head: Practice window being opened
items.body: The Eagles opened Shipley's (foot) 21-day practice window Monday. Shipley landed on IR after being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the wake of Week 5 action, but he now has a chance to play as soon as Sunday against the Steelers. Meanwhile, fellow RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) -- who hasn't played since Week 4 -- remains on IR, and the Eagles signed Jaydon Blue to their practice squad Monday. If Shipley is able to suit up this weekend, he'll reclaim a backup role behind Saquon Barkley that isn't likely to result in much volume for the 2024 fourth-rounder.

items.head: Will Shipley (Foot) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Eagles opened Shipley's (foot) 21-day practice window Monday.

items.head: Giants RB Cam Skattebo to nix backflips in wake of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
items.body: Giants RB Cam Skattebo said he is holding off on doing any more backflips after Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a major knee injury while leaping and celebrating a sack.

items.head: Pair of TDs in close loss
items.body: Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and brought in three of four targets for 44 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. Skattebo put together an impressive all-around performance that included a season high in receiving yards. Skattebo also exceeded the 75-yard mark on the ground for the third time on the campaign, and he went in for his third and fourth rushing touchdowns of the season on one- and 13-yard runs in the first and third quarters, respectively. Skattebo didn't show any ill effects from the hamstring injury that cost him Sunday's win over the Eagles, and he'll now gear up for a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars' elite run defense on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.head: Cam Skattebo (injury) is Active
items.body: Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and brought in three of four targets for 44 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

items.head: Ready to go for Thursday night
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Prior to Tuesday's practice, Skattebo told Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post that the hamstring tear he sustained in a Week 7 overtime win over the Texans "wasn't too bad" and wouldn't prevent him from playing Thursday against the Commanders. With Skattebo proceeding to take every rep during Tuesday's session, he's now officially in the clear to step back into a lead role out of the New York backfield in Week 10. As a result of Skattebo's return to the lineup following a one-game absence, Devin Singletary -- who handled a season-high 23 touches in the Week 9 win over the Eagles -- is expected to see his opportunities get scaled back significantly.

items.head: Practicing again Tuesday
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) was spotted on the field for the media-access portion of Tuesday's practice, Art Stapleton of The Bergen Record reports.

items.head: Limited at Monday's walkthrough
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as limited on Monday's estimated injury report, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Skattebo missed his first game of the season Sunday in Philadelphia due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in the Giants' previous game back in Week 7. Prior to Skattebo being inactive, though, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that the running back was pushing to play, and head coach John Harbaugh told Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News on Monday that he should be "full go" for Thursday's game against the Commanders. Skattebo still has some work to do to prove his health, but he appears to be trending in the right direction for a Week 10 appearance.

items.head: Looks ready to go for Week 10
items.body: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that Skattebo (hamstring) should be "full go" for Thursday's game against the Commanders, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports. After tweaking his hamstring in an Oct. 25 overtime win over the Texans, Skattebo wasn't able to fully shake the injury coming out of a Week 8 bye and ended up missing his first game of the season Sunday in the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles. The second-year back was at least able to close Week 9 prep as a limited participant in practice, and Harbaugh noted that Skattebo was close to playing against the Eagles before the team ultimately chose to hold him out as a matter of caution. Though the Giants will face a quick turnaround for Week 10, Skattebo looks on track to reclaim a leading role out of the backfield against Washington, barring a setback with his hamstring during the team's limited practice time leading up to the contest.

items.head: Doubtful for Week 9
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Skattebo was able to manage one limited practice (Friday) this week, and while head coach John Harbaugh told Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post that the Giants are "keeping the door open" for the running back to play in Week 9, his official listing implies it's more likely just ajar. In any case, if Skattebo ends up sitting out Sunday, Devin Singletary likely will serve as New York's lead runner, with Greg Desrosiers and potentially practice-squad members Eric Gray and Phil Mafah in line for work behind him.

items.head: Remains out, not yet practicing
items.body: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

items.head: Jake Ferguson (Knee) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: In line to miss multiple weeks, per coach
items.body: According to coach Brian Schottenheimer, Ferguson (knee) is in line to miss multiple weeks, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports. At a minimum, Ferguson is on track to miss at least this coming weekend's game against the 49ers, but a 'multiple week' timetable hints at a possible IR stint for the tight end. Next up for the Cowboy's reps at the position are Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) -- when healthy -- and James Mitchell. With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, it's also not difficult to imagine Dallas looking into gaining additional help in Ferguson's looming absence.

items.head: Headed for imaging on knee
items.body: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said after Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts that Ferguson will undergo imaging on his knee Monday, the team's official site reports. Ferguson played just 27 of the Cowboys' 79 offensive snaps and finished with two catches for 21 yards and a touchdown on two targets before exiting Sunday's game in the third quarter after taking a low hit. Schottenheimer noted that Ferguson initially sustained a stinger on the hit, but the Cowboys later classified his injury as a knee issue. The upcoming MRI will reveal the severity of the injury, which tentatively clouds Ferguson's status for the team's Week 10 matchup with the 49ers.

items.head: Suffers knee injury in Week 9
items.body: Ferguson sustained a knee injury during Sunday's game against the Colts, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports. Ferguson tended to a low-ankle sprain during Week 9 prep, but it's now one of his knees that's a concern after he took a low hit in the third quarter of Sunday's matchup. He had two catches (on two targets) for 21 yards and one touchdown at the time of his exit.

items.head: Active in Week 9
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday in Indianapolis. Ferguson left last Sunday's loss to the Cardinals on the Cowboys' first possession and wasn't able to return due to an ankle injury. He was diagnosed with a low-ankle sprain, and while head coach Brian Schottenheimer relayed to Jon Machota of The Athletic on Monday that Ferguson has a chance to play in Week 9, the tight end managed just one limited practice (Friday) and was listed as questionable. Now that Ferguson is confirmed to be active, his workload is unclear with two other TEs (Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell) also available to the offense.

items.head: Listed as questionable for Sunday
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Ferguson returned to practice Friday as a limited participant, after making an early exit Week 8 and missing practice earlier this week. Dallas has downplayed the severity of Ferguson's injury, but he looks no better than 50/50 ahead of a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday at Indianapolis. Brevyn Spann-Ford filled in after Ferguson's first-quarter exit last week, playing 88 percent of snaps on offense and catching four of five targets for 31 yards.

items.head: Could practice Friday
items.body: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer hopes that Ferguson (ankle) will be "back on the field" Friday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Ferguson did not get any work in Wednesday or Thursday due to the ankle injury he sustained in Week 8, but it appears there is a chance he could practice in some capacity Friday. The Cowboys will reveal his official status for Week 9 at some point following the conclusion of Friday's session.

items.head: Full practice Wednesday
items.body: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday. Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

items.head: Jauan Jennings (injury) is Active
items.body: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.

items.head: Won't play Sunday
items.body: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Jennings opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNP listings due to a calf injury and now will miss his second contest of the campaign. With Jordan Addison (thumb) listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Justin Jefferson, Myles Price and Tai Felton currently are the healthy wide receivers on the Vikings' active roster.

items.head: Not practicing Thursday
items.body: Jennings (calf) did not participate at practice Thursday. Jennings was estimated as a non-participant on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9, and he wasn't able to take the practice field Thursday. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably end up missing a second straight game in Week 10, which could leave Myles Price with an expanded role at wideout come Sunday at Green Bay.

items.head: Starts week with DNP
items.body: Jennings (calf) was estimated as DNP on Wednesday's practice report. The veteran wideout missed last Monday night's loss to the Bills. If he's unable to play Sunday against the Packers, Tai Felton would be in line to handle WR3 duties for Minnesota behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Jennings has six catches for 54 yards across six games this season.

items.head: Jauan Jennings (Calf) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Won't play in Week 9
items.body: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's contest versus the Bills. Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Jennings suffered a calf injury at Thursday's practice that is serious enough to sideline him for at least one game. Jennings' next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 15 in Green Bay, while Tai Felton and Myles Price are in for some offensive snaps this week behind the top WR duo of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

items.head: DNP Friday
items.body: Jennings (calf) did not participate in Friday's practice. Jennings downgraded his practice participation Friday after being limited in Thursday's session. The wide receiver will likely need to show up in some capacity Saturday for a chance to suit up for Monday night's primetime showdown with the Bills.

items.head: Jaydn Ott (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Without clear timeline for return
items.body: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that he had no new updates on the status of Conner (foot), who is still "working to return to perform," Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports. "It was not a good injury," LaFleur said. Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

items.head: Still lacking clear timeline
items.body: Updating a previous report, Conner (foot) no longer appears to be a candidate to return from injured reserve to play Week 11 versus the Chiefs, according to Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com. A report Monday from Jess Root of USA Today quoted Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur as stating that Conner was "trending well" and had "a chance" to return to action in Week 11, but Drake clarified that LaFleur was referring to guard/center Jon Gaines (ankle) rather than Conner. The veteran running back hasn't played since Week 3 of the 2025 season due to a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery, and he remains without a clear timeline to return to the field. Conner took part in individual drills during training camp, but after being placed on IR on Aug. 30, he hasn't been cleared to resume practicing since the regular season got underway.

items.head: Set to complement Montgomery in Week 11
items.body: Demercado is expected to serve as the top complement to David Montgomery in Thursday's game against the Colts, with Woody Marks (concussion) ruled out for the contest. With Montgomery sidelined for a fourth straight game this past Sunday against the Browns and with Marks making an early exit, Demercado saw his most playing time of the season in the 27-24 loss. Demercado did little to capitalize on the opportunity, finishing with 15 yards from scrimmage on eight touches (seven carries, one reception). Though Marks wasn't able to clear concussion protocol in a short week, Montgomery has been cleared to play after he was listed as a full practice participant Monday through Wednesday. Montgomery should step back in as the Texans' preferred option out of the backfield, leaving Demercado to settle for more of a change-of-pace role.

items.head: Works as lead back following Marks injury
items.body: Demercado rushed seven times for 16 yards and brought in one of two targets for minus-1 yard in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Demercado opened the game as a reserve in his second appearance in a Texans uniform, but Woody Marks' third-quarter exit due to a concussion left the former in the de facto No. 1 role. That still didn't lead to much opportunity for Demercado in a game during which Houston squandered a 17-0 first-half lead. However, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports Marks is unlikely to play in Week 11 due to the short turnaround for a home matchup against the Colts, meaning Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale could have expanded roles in that game unless David Montgomery (groin) is able to suit up.

items.head: Six rushes in debut with Houston
items.body: Demercado rushed six times for 16 yards and caught one of two targets for eight yards during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Demercado was claimed off waivers by the Texans on Oct. 28, and he made his team debut in Week 9 after the team was off in Week 8. The running back finished second on the team in carries behind Woody Marks (18), and he could operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield again in Week 10 versus Cleveland if David Montgomery (groin) remains sidelined.

items.head: Foot injury in rear-view mirror
items.body: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice. Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

items.head: Does just enough to eke out win
items.body: Young completed 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. He added one rushing yard on his only carry. Chuba Hubbard did most of the heavy lifting on offense for the Panthers, piling up 172 scrimmage yards and both the team's touchdowns. It's the first time this season Young failed to throw a TD, but it was also the first time since Week 6 he avoided committing a turnover. The fourth-year QB will take a 16:6 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash against the Ravens.

items.head: Three TDs not enough Sunday
items.body: Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. He added 13 yards on his only carry and lost a fumble. The fourth-year QB tossed TDs in each of the last three quarters, finding Tommy Tremble, Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan, but Young's attempt to engineer a game-winning drive inside the final two minutes ended on a Nik Bonitto strip sack. It's the third time this season Young has thrown three touchdowns, but his first such performance since Week 2. He'll take a 16:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Saints.

items.head: Ready to play, ankle improving
items.body: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Friday that Young (ankle) is ready for Sunday's game against Denver after a "great week" of practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports. Young has been a full practice participant throughout the week, apparently not too bothered by a sore ankle. The bigger concern for Sunday is Denver's impressive pass rush matching up against Carolina's injury-riddled offensive line.

items.head: Ravens' Flowers 'super frustrated' by latest late-game fumble
items.body: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers said he was "super frustrated" after having the ball ripped away around midfield in the final two minutes of a loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

items.head: Solid night marred by key fumble
items.body: Flowers brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and lost a fumble in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The talented wideout took advantage by finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for Baltimore on the night, but Flowers had the ball stripped from him after a 15-yard catch at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:11 remaining. The lost fumble turned out to effectively snuff out the Ravens' chances of realistically getting into position for a potential game-tying field goal, ending the game on a sour night. Nevertheless, the fact Brissett threw for 340 yards in his first game in the offense bodes well for Flowers' prospects as a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday approaches.

items.head: Works on side Wednesday
items.body: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

items.head: De'Zhaun Stribling (Ankle) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Tyrone Tracy Jr. (Hamstring) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Sticking as backup for Week 11
items.body: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports. Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

items.head: Caleb Lohner (Lower Body) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Broncos opened Lohner's (lower body) 21-day practice window Wednesday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.

items.head: Titans WR Wan'Dale Robinson out for season with ankle injury
items.body: Titans wide receiver Wan'Dale Robinson will miss the rest of the season due to an ankle injury, coach Robert Saleh said Wednesday.

items.head: Wan'Dale Robinson (Ankle) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Titans placed Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Questionable to return Sunday
items.body: Robinson (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jaguars. The Titans were already without Carnell Tate (shoulder) Sunday, and now,  Robinson's status will need to be monitored ahead of next weekend's game against the Cowboys. Next up for the team's WR snaps/targets should one or both of the aforementioned players be sidelined in Week 11 are Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike.

items.head: Not practicing Wednesday
items.body: Murray (hamstring) will miss Wednesday's practice, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports.
