The Vikings are targeting a Week 12 matchup with the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 29, for Murray to be available again, so his lack of activity this week doesn't come as a susprise. Whenever Murray is back, though, he likely will take on No. 2 QB duties due to the arrival of Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas at the trade deadline.

items.head: Targeting Week 12 return
items.body: The Vikings are targeting Week 12 against the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 29, for a return for Murray (hamstring), Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. Murray suffered a Grade 2 hamstring injury during the Vikings' Week 8 loss to the Lions, which prevented him from playing against the Bills in Week 9. The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and the veteran QB will start under center against the Packers on Sunday, with Carson Wentz serving as the backup and Max Brosmer as the emergency QB3 in Murray's absence. It's unclear whether Murray will be ahead of Wentz on the depth chart once the former is cleared to return.

items.head: Out again in Week 10
items.body: Murray (hamstring) was ruled out for Sunday's contest in Green Bay. After head coach Kevin O'Connell called Murray week-to-week due to his Grade 2 hamstring injury Wednesday, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com, the quarterback's second straight absence as a result was expected. O'Connell announced recent acquisition Kirk Cousins as the Vikings' starting QB for Week 10, and that should hold even after Murray gets back to full health.

items.head: Remains week-to-week
items.body: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Murray (hamstring) remains week-to-week, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports. Murray already has missed one game due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain and is expected to be sidelined longer as the Vikings begin prep for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, but O'Connell wasn't ready to commit to him as the team's Week 10 starting QB as of Wednesday. Assuming Murray is out again this weekend, Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer will be the signal-caller options at O'Connell's disposal.

items.head: Expected to miss more time
items.body: Murray is considered week-to-week due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain and isn't expected to be available for Sunday's game against the Packers, James Palmer of Bleacher Report reports. Murray -- who was previously sidelined for the Vikings' Week 2 win over the Bears while recovering from a concussion -- missed his second game of the season in Monday's 23-6 loss to the Bills on account of the hamstring injury. Carson Wentz drew the start in place of Murray, but both quarterbacks will move into reserve roles moving forward after the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. After bringing Murray aboard on a one-year deal in free agency, the Vikings were hopeful the 2019 No. 1 overall pick would bounce back in a new locale, but he posted modest numbers (64.9 percent completion rate, 6.6 yards per attempt, 5:3 TD:INT, 167 rushing yards) and generally struggled to move the offense over his six appearances. Once healthy, Murray should settle in as the Vikings' No. 2 quarterback, but Wentz will likely serve as Cousins' top backup against Green Bay.

items.head: Kyler Murray (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Dealing with Grade 2 strain
items.body: Murray (hamstring) is recovering from a Grade 2 strain "that will keep him out for Monday's game and potentially beyond," Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. Murray has not been officially ruled out for Monday's matchup with the Bills, but Carson Wentz will start under center regardless of Murray's availability, and the latest report indicates that may not be a one-week occurrence. The Vikings will reveal whether or not Murray has any chance to suit up for Week 9 when they release their final injury report of the week later Saturday.

items.head: Likely out Monday, won't go on IR
items.body: Murray likely won't play Monday against the Bills due to a hamstring strain, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Murray is considered week-to-week, paving the way for Carson Wentz to make his second start of the season when the Vikings face the Bills on MNF. Per Lewis, O'Connell said Thursday that a stint on injured reserve isn't under consideration for Murray, suggesting that the starting quarterback's potential absence isn't expected to linger beyond 1-to-3 weeks.

items.head: Adam Randall (injury) is Active
items.body: The Ravens reinstated Randall (neck/hamstring) from injured reserve Wednesday, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Eagles' Sirianni sticking with Milton as QB1, Mannion as offensive playcaller
items.body: QB Joe Milton will start again for the Eagles on Sunday and Sean Mannion will remain as the offensive playcaller against the Steelers, coach Nick Sirianni said.

items.head: Retaining starting job
items.body: Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano. While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. He lost a fumble and took seven sacks in the loss to the Giants, so Milton may need to show that he can avoid negative plays in Week 11 in order to guaranteed himself additional starts.

items.head: Throws for 169 yards, runs for 64 in start
items.body: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble. The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

items.head: Set to start Sunday
items.body: Milton is set to be the Eagles' starting quarterback Sunday against the Giants, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad Oct. 16, and less than a month later, he's getting the call after the Tanner McKee experience so far has resulted in three consecutive losses. In five appearances (no starts) between New England and Dallas in his career, Milton has competed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing 15 times for 66 yards and one TD and losing both of his fumbles.

items.head: Sources: Brandon Aiyuk contacted Jayden Daniels to mend friendship with star QB
items.body: Brandon Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels have patched up their relationship after a falling out earlier this year, sources told ESPN.

items.head: Deemed 100 percent ahead of likely release
items.body: Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver is "100 percent healthy" and fully recovered from his November 2024 right knee surgery and plans to work out for interested teams once he's released by the 49ers, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports. After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco reinstated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him. While it's unclear what kind of market might exist for Aiyuk's services coming off a lengthy layoff from NFL action, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relayed earlier this month that at least one NFC team has expressed interest in adding the receiver to its practice squad.

items.head: Brandon Aiyuk reinstated by NFL; 49ers have 2-game roster exemption for receiver
items.body: The NFL reinstated San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Monday after he reported for a physical, according to the league's transaction wire.

items.head: Reinstated, 49ers granted two-week exemption
items.body: The 49ers reinstated Aiyuk (personal) from the reserve/left squad list Monday and were granted a two-week roster exemption for the wide receiver, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to either add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

items.head: Brandon Aiyuk (Personal) is Out
items.body: The 49ers reinstated Aiyuk (personal) from the reserve/left squad list Monday and were granted a two-week roster exemption for the wide receiver, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: Meets with 49ers on Friday
items.body: Prior to meeting with 49ers officials Friday, Aiyuk (personal) told assembled media that he's "feeling great, healthy" and "looking to get reinstated to the National Football League," Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Per Wagoner, Aiyuk submitted paperwork to be reinstated to the NFL in late October, and since then both the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association have been involved in an attempt to reach a resolution that's agreeable to both the wide receiver and the 49ers. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Thursday that Aiyuk's efforts to secure his release may be hampered by the roughly $13 million in bonus forfeitures that he owes the team, which could mean arbitration comes into play and delays the process. Friday's meeting between Aiyuk, his agent Drew Rosenhaus and San Francisco brass was only the first step. If the sides reach an agreement, the 49ers will have three options: release Aiyuk, trade him before Tuesday's deadline or add him to their 53-man roster.

items.head: Money owed may be hurdle in securing release
items.body: Aiyuk's effort to secure his release by reporting to the 49ers' facility Friday could be complicated by roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture he owes the team, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports. Pelissero notes that the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are both involved in trying to reaching a resolution that is agreeable to both Aiyuk and the 49ers. It's possible that the embattled wideout could ultimately agree to pay back the money in order to potentially have an opportunity to move on with another club, but there's also a chance the issue goes to arbitration. Aiyuk is planning to show up at San Francisco's facility Friday, though that is unlikely to bring the matter to a close. In fact, it could take an extended period of time to sort out a path forward, especially if arbitration is brought into play.

items.head: Path forward murky
items.body: Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both declined to get into specifics when discussing the future of Aiyuk, who has filed his paperwork for reinstatement and plans to show up to the 49ers' facility Friday, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. Lynch previously stated "I think it's safe to say that he's played his last snap with the Niners" regarding Aiyuk in January, but the GM was much less definitive Thursday when asked about a reunion with Aiyuk, responding with "I think everything's possible." Head coach Kyle Shanahan gave a similar answer Wednesday, stating "There's no absolutes in life." The 49ers are working with the NFL management council to find a resolution to Aiyuk's situation, so the team's front office and coaching staff are treating this situation as an ongoing legal matter. If Aiyuk is successfully reinstated, the 49ers could trade him, release him or add him to the active roster.

items.head: Makes return from PUP list
items.body: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Wednesday that Shavers (knee) has been reinstated from the PUP list, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports. Shavers' 21-day evaluation window was set to close this week, so the Bills elected to add him back to the 53-man roster to ensure that he would be available to play this season. The wideout has been a full practice participant for the past two weeks, so he appears to be fully recovered from the torn ACL he sustained in January and should be available for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If active for the Week 11 contest, Shavers will likely slot in as a depth option at receiver behind the trio of DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.

items.head: Tyrell Shavers (injury) is Active
items.body: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Wednesday that Shavers (knee) has been reinstated from the PUP list, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.

items.head: Tyrell Shavers (Knee - ACL) is Out
items.body: Shavers (knee) was not activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of Monday night's matchup with Minnesota, per the NFL's official transaction log.

items.head: Getting first-team reps Wednesday
items.body: Daniels is slated to take all of the first-teams reps Wednesday with Baker Mayfield (foot) sidelined for the Buccaneers' first Week 11 practice, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. While the Buccaneers aren't ruling Mayfield out from playing Sunday in Detroit, the fact that he'll be a spectator in practice coming out of a Week 10 bye suggests that Daniels has the early edge on the Week 11 start. Per Auman, Mayfield appeared to be walking normally off to the side during Wednesday's practice, which could indicate that he'll attempt to test out his strained foot during Thursday's session. The Buccaneers should have some clarity by Friday whether Daniels or Mayfield will draw the start Sunday, with Mayfield's activity (or lack thereof) over the next two days likely to be the determining factor.

items.head: Could be headed for Week 11 start
items.body: Daniels "seems to be trending" toward drawing the start at quarterback for the Buccaneers on Sunday in Detroit while Baker Mayfield tends to a foot strain, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Mayfield injured his foot late in a Week 9 loss to the Bears, and after he was in and out of a walking boot during the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, his status is firmly up in the air for Week 11. Since Mayfield has shown a willingness to play at well below 100 percent in the past, the Buccaneers will likely wait until the end of the week to see where he stands on the health front before naming a starter for Sunday, but Daniels at least appears poised to take some reps with the first-team offense when the team returns to practice Wednesday. When Mayfield was previously sidelined from Weeks 4 through 6 due to a dislocated thumb, Daniels stepped in as the starter and guided Tampa Bay to a 1-2 record while completing 60 of 95 passes (63.2 percent) for 501 yards, three touchdowns and four interceptions to go with 117 yards on 19 carries.

items.head: Could be back around Week 16
items.body: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports. Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

items.head: Facing 6-to-10 week absence
items.body: Jackson (thumb) is "doing well" and is expected to be out for "6-to-10 weeks," per head coach Jesse Minter. Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was recently acquired from the Cardinals, figures to hold down the starting quarterback spot in Jackson's absence.

items.head: Plans to return this season
items.body: Jackson, who is scheduled to undergo surgery on his injured right thumb, has told teammates he plans to return later this season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a turf-toe injury. Brissett's experience gives the team a chance to get back to winning ways after losing four games in a row.

items.head: Multiple factors at play in possible return
items.body: Jackson's odds to play again this season depend on his recovery from a right thumb injury, and also whether or not new QB Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens in the playoff picture long enough to make a return late in the season possible for Jackson, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. The Ravens already have cycled through three starting QBs this season, and with Tyler Huntley sidelined for the rest of the campaign due to a turf-toe injury and Jackson out indefinitely, the team agreed to a trade with the Cardinals for Brissett, which became official Friday. Brissett was serviceable until he wasn't in Arizona, finishing his 2026 season there with 1,719 yards on 63 percent passing, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight appearances, and he'll have top talents in RB Derrick Henry and WR Zay Flowers to work with in his new locale. It remains to be seen if Baltimore, which is three games in the loss column behind Pittsburgh and Cincinnati in the AFC North, can get back to winning ways, but Brissett's performance seemingly will dictate if Jackson makes another appearance by Week 18.

items.head: Officially placed on IR
items.body: The Ravens have officially placed Jackson (thumb) on injured reserve. Prior to Thursday night's game against the Jaguars, the Ravens made a trio of moves to re-shape their Week 9 QB corps. Along with Jackson, Tyler Huntley (toe) landed on IR, while Austin Reed was added to the team's active roster. As a result, Joe Fagnano (Thursday's starter), Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed are available to face Jacksonville, and then in the coming days Jacoby Brissett will be on his way to Baltimore via a looming trade with the Cardinals. Jackson will miss his team's next four games, at a minimum, and it's possible that his injury could be season ending, an outcome that is already reportedly in the cards for Huntley.

items.head: Could benefit from Robinson's absence
items.body: Restrepo, whom the Titans signed off their practice squad Tuesday, could be in store for more playing time out of the slot moving forward after Tennessee placed Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve, Mark Mihalko of USA Today reports. A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the Titans are expected to get rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder) back for Sunday's game in Dallas, Restrepo's strong showing in relief of the injured Robinson last week should at least allow him to stick ahead of Calvin Ridley (four snaps in Week 10) as Tennessee's No. 4 wideout.

items.head: Why Packers can't protect Jordan Love or rush successfully
items.body: The two-year demise of the Packers' offensive line began on March 10, 2025 and has no end in sight.

items.head: Buried by Minnesota pass rush in loss
items.body: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings. The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

items.head: Another prolific performance in win
items.body: Love completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed once for a 13-yard score in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. He also ran in a two-point conversion. Love continued to attack downfield with great efficacy in the significant road upset for the Packers. Love averaged 12.8 yards per attempt while amassing his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, a figure bested only by the 387-yard tally he managed in Week 1. Love generated his second straight three-touchdown day through the air as well, connecting with Matthew Golden (five yards), Savion Williams (10 yards) and Christian Watson (39 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes and kicking off the scoring on the day with a 13-yard rush just 1:41 into the contest. Love is up to 2,618 passing yards with a 19:6 TD:INT and a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

items.head: Source: Cardinals' Gardner Minshew has surgery to repair right UCL
items.body: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II had surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament on Monday, a source told ESPN.

items.head: Underwent UCL surgery Monday
items.body: Minshew (elbow) underwent UCL reconstructive surgery Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. It's a season-ending procedure and will likely keep Minshew sidelined until training camp next summer. The veteran quarterback suffered the injury in Week 9 but somehow kept playing through it, completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. It's Carson Beck's show moving forward, as the Cardinals play out the string on another lost season in what has become a never-ending rebuild.

items.head: In line for surgery on torn UCL
items.body: Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right throwing elbow last Sunday at Seattle and is slated to undergo season-ending surgery, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Minshew incredibly played through the injury in Week 9, logging all 53 offensive snaps and completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in his first start replacing the since-departed Jacoby Brissett. Schefter added that Minshew still is determining the timing of the procedure, but he plans on having it. With Minshew out for the rest of the campaign, rookie third-round pick Carson Beck is taking over under center for the Cardinals.

items.head: Will miss rest of season
items.body: Minshew (elbow) will undergo UCL surgery and is out for the season, Theo Mackie of AzCentral reports. With Minshew already on injured reserve, the surgery confirms he won't return for Arizona this season. Carson Beck is now Arizona's starting QB for Week 11 against the Rams and beyond.

items.head: Gardner Minshew II (Elbow) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Minshew (elbow) will undergo UCL surgery and is out for the season, Theo Mackie of AzCentral reports.

items.head: Could face season-ending elbow surgery
items.body: Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Minshew (elbow) is reportedly seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he likely will require season-ending surgery to address a torn UCL. Minshew's stint as the Cardinals' starting QB thus is shaping up to be a brief one. Assuming Schefter's report is confirmed, Carson Beck is slated to take over as Arizona's QB1, beginning with this Sunday's game against the Rams.

items.head: Gardner Minshew II (Elbow) is Doubtful
items.body: Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Minshew (elbow) is reportedly seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he likely will require season-ending surgery to address a torn UCL.

items.head: Set to undergo testing on arm/elbow
items.body: Minshew is slated to undergo testing on his right elbow/arm in the wake of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks, according to Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site. Minshew took over as the team's starting QB in advance of Week 9 action, and now his status for this weekend's game against the Rams is unclear. In the event that Minshew's issue ends up being long term, which could be a possibility, per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Carson Beck is next in line for Arizona's signal-caller reps.

items.head: Xavier Legette (injury) is Active
items.body: Legette didn't produce any output in the boxscore during Carolina's win over the Saints on Sunday.

items.head: Back in action in Week 10
items.body: Legette (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports. After being activated from injured reserve Saturday but still being listed as questionable heading into Sunday, Legette has now officially been cleared to play for the first time since Week 2. Legette was a full participant in practice throughout Week 10 prep, so he could immediately step back in as the Panthers' No. 3 wideout, the role he held prior to succumbing to the knee injury.

items.head: Questionable for Week 10
items.body: Legette (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at New Orleans. Legette is trending toward a return from injured reserve after the Panthers listed him as a full practice participant all week. They'll need to activate him by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Legette on the active roster for Sunday's NFC South showdown. Legette was Carolina's No. 3 receiver before the injury, often running clear-out routes while Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker dominated the targets. John Metchie and Brycen Tremayne took on more snaps in Legette's absence over the past month-plus.

items.head: Logs full practice
items.body: Legette (knee) was a full practice participant Thursday. The Panthers listed Legette as a full participant Wednesday on their estimated practice report. He gets the same listing after an actual practice and seems to be closing in on a return from injured reserve. Carolina would need to activate Legette by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have him on the roster for Sunday's game at New Orleans. Legette was Carolina's No. 3 receiver earlier this season, and neither John Metchie nor Brycen Tremayne has made much of an impact in his absence.

items.head: Xavier Legette (Knee) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Legette (knee) will be designated for return from injured reserve this week, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.

items.head: Bears QB Caleb Williams has moved on from 4-INT game, but frustration lingers
items.body: Caleb Williams spent his bye week resting his ailing hamstring, supporting his close friend Pete Crow-Armstrong as the Cubs outfielder was named NL MVP, and putting one of the worst games of his career in the rearview mirror.

items.head: Shrugs off four INTs in fourth straight win
items.body: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards. Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

items.head: Impressive performance against elite defense
items.body: Williams completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for one yard in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Williams helped set the tone for the Bears' statement road victory by leading a 17-play, 80-yard march that absorbed 8:32 of the first quarter, one that the third-year signal-caller capped off with a one-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. Williams then managed the game effectively from that point forward, avoiding mistakes while leaning on a workhorse performance from D'Andre Swift (27 carries, three touchdowns) and an often dominating effort from his defense. Williams now has a three-game streak of interception-free performances and is up to 1,267 passing yards through five contests heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: KaVontae Turpin (injury) is Active
items.body: Turpin caught one of three targets for 10 yards Sunday in a Week 10 loss to San Francisco. He also rushed once for nine yards.

items.head: KaVontae Turpin (Ribs) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: Brings in 26-yard pass in Week 10 loss
items.body: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' TE1 in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets of Dak Prescott, With Spann-Ford and five other Cowboys skill-position players logging one catch each. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again be the Cowboys' top tight end for Week 11 on Nov. 22, against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each of its last two games.

items.head: Two snags in victory
items.body: Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts. Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the year, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine regular-season contests so far.

items.head: Does little with season-high seven targets
items.body: Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

items.head: Zero targets in first game since extension
items.body: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday. Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year extension worth up to $26.8 million, which puts him under contract with the Cardinals through the 2029 season. He didn't have any offensive stats to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck under center for the first time this season. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 regular-season games into Arizona's Week 11 tilt against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

items.head: Signing extension through 2029
items.body: Higgins is signing a contract extension with the Cardinals through 2029, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. Higgins was scheduled for free agency after this season, and he's taken on a larger role as the year has progressed, helping the Cardinals get by with limited talent at wide receiver. Higgins has 18 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets, serving as a complementary receiving option alongside Trey McBride when the Cardinals use multi-TE formations. Higgins figures to stick in that role long-term and won't be of much fantasy interest unless McBride misses time.

items.head: Two grabs versus Seattle
items.body: Higgins caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. With all of the injuries at wide receiver for Arizona, Higgins played a season-high 66 percent of the offensive snaps in Seattle. It still didn't translate to an elevated role in the pass game. Higgins has 18 grabs for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets across nine games this season.

items.head: Hauls in 31-yard pass in Week 10 defeat
items.body: Duvernay caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday. Duvernay was on the field for only 10 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (28.6 percent), but the veteran wide receiver connected with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck on passes of four and 31 yards on back-to-back plays late in the first quarter. Duvernay finished the contest second in catches, targets and receiving yards behind Trey McBride, and the former has caught two passes in each of his last three outings. With Michael Wilson (neck, IR) out for the year, the Cardinals' top wideouts for the rest of the season appear to be Duvernay, Simi Fehoko and rookie fifth-rounder Reggie Virgil, which doesn't bring much confidence heading into Week 11 against the Chiefs on Nov. 22.

items.head: Zero targets in Week 10 loss
items.body: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't show up on the box score otherwise during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams. The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck under center, and Arizona finished with a 17:37 time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the Cardinals pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the Cardinals skill-position players (other than McBride), especially with the team heading into a tough Week 11 road tilt against the Chiefs.

items.head: Taking over starting role
items.body: Virgil will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports. A 2026 fifth-round pick, Virgil started his career buried on the depth chart before moving up due to injuries and trades. It's not quite the same as earning a starting job, but he should see routes and targets all the same in the coming weeks. Virgil has been targeted on 11 of 56 routes (19.6 percent) and caught just three passes for 54 yards in five appearances. He should get plenty of playing time this Sunday against the Rams in what will be the first career start for rookie QB Carson Beck.

items.head: One catch against Seattle
items.body: Virgil caught one of four targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Gardner Minshew found Virgil for a 25-yard pass early in the first quarter, but the duo failed to connect with each other for the rest of Sunday's contest. The Cardinals' offense took quite a hit in Week 9, with Minshew sustaining a torn UCL and wide receiver Michael Wilson suffering a fracture in his neck, and those injuries will keep both players on the shelf for the rest of the 2026 season. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are both also on season-ending IR, which leaves Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and superstar tight end Trey McBride as the top targets for rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck heading into Week 10 against the Rams.

items.head: Brevin Jordan (Foot) is Out
items.body: Jordan (foot/illness) did not participate at practice Tuesday.

items.head: Brevin Jordan (Finger) is Questionable
items.body: Jordan (finger) did not practice Wednesday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.

items.head: Hauls in 21-yard pass in Week 10 loss
items.body: Fehoko finished Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams with one catch on two targets for 21 yards. He also recorded a tackle. Week 10 was the Cardinals' first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck on the field. The offense struggled to move the ball down the field and logged only 35 snaps as a whole while finishing with a 17:37 time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Fehoko and the rest of the Cardinals' skill-position players, although the sixth-year pro did connect with Beck on a 21-yard pass early in the first quarter. Fehoko's 26 offensive snaps led all Arizona wide receivers, and with Michael Wilson (neck, IR) out for the rest of the season, the former should continue to operate in an elevated role heading into Week 11 against the Chiefs on Nov. 22.

items.head: Set for more snaps
items.body: Fehoko will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports. Fehoko is a 2021 fifth-round pick who turned 29 earlier this month and has been targeted on just two of 37 routes for the Cardinals this year. He mostly seems to have stuck around the league because his size is useful for special teams and blocking, but Fehoko now has a chance to get more snaps on offense, if only because Arizona's WR depth chart has been decimated. He has a chance to start this Sunday against the Rams in QB Carson Beck's first career start.

items.head: Logs five carries in return
items.body: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday. Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries, although the Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, and Knight and the offense will have its hands full in Week 11 against Kansas City, whose defense ranks eighth in the NFL in yards allowed per game (314.8).

items.head: Bam Knight (injury) is Active
items.body: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.

items.head: Good to go
items.body: Knight (concussion) is cleared to play Sunday against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Knight figures to split backfield work with Tyler Allgeier, who played 96 percent of snaps last week when Knight was inactive for a 17-3 loss at Seattle. Knight suffered the concussion in Week 8, shortly after Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle -- an issue that sent the rookie to injured reserve not long after. Love is out for at least three more games, leaving Allgeier and Knight to split backfield work again.

items.head: Logs full practice Thursday
items.body: Knight (concussion) practiced in full Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports. Knight was limited Wednesday after donning a yellow non-contact jersey in practice, but after ditching it one day later, he was able to handle every on-field rep. That's not to say he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires an evaluation from an independent neurologist, but he's likely on the precipice of doing so. Friday's injury report will determine if Knight heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.

items.head: Out of non-contact jersey
items.body: Knight (concussion) practiced Thursday without a yellow non-contact jersey, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports. Knight didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Sunday's game at Seattle due to a concussion that he suffered one week prior, but he got back on the practice field as limited Wednesday while wearing the non-contact jersey. His ability to ditch it one day later indicates he's making progress through the protocol for head injuries, but Thursday's practice report will unveil whether or not he was full.

items.head: Practicing Wednesday
items.body: Knight (concussion) practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. After suffering a concussion in Week 8 at Dallas, Knight wasn't able to practice last week before the Cardinals ruled him out ahead of this past Sunday's game in Seattle. With his return to drills this week, he's made progress through the protocol for head injuries, but the presence of the non-contact jersey indicates he's a few steps away from meeting with an independent neurologist.

items.head: Officially limited Wednesday
items.body: Knight (concussion) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.

items.head: Bam Knight (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.body: Mallory (hamstring) was estimated as a non-participant for Tuesday's practice walkthrough.

items.head: Won't play against Miami
items.body: Mallory (hamstring) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Mallory was a late addition to the Colts' injury report due to a hamstring issue that cropped up Friday. The fourth-year pro will not be available for Sunday's contest, and with Mo Alie-Cox (groin) placed on injured reserve, Tyler Warren will be backed up by Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown. Mallory's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

items.head: Held without catch in Week 10 loss
items.body: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties moving forward now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

items.head: Hauls in 30-yard catch vs. Miami
items.body: Dulin caught one of two targets for 30 yards and returned three kickoffs for 77 yards during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles on special teams. Even with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being sent out at the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Dulin's 13 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Colts wide receivers behind Laquon Treadwell (52), Deion Burks (34) and Anthony Gould (32). Dulin did connect on a 30-yard pass from Daniel Jones on a 30-yard pass late in the second quarter, which was a pivotal part of the Colts' nine-play, 92-yard drive that ended with a seven-yard touchdown catch by Treadwell. Dulin has logged catches of 55 and 30 yards in each of his last two outings, and he could be the Colts' WR3 for Thursday's AFC South tilt against the Texans if Gould is not cleared to play due to a toe injury.

items.head: Will help fill in for departed Allen
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Dulin will be one of the Colts receivers tasked with absorbing the snaps vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports. Steichen also mentioned Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine as other candidates to fill in at the outside receiver spot opposite Laquon Treadwell, while noting that Anthony Gould will serve as the Colts' starting slot receiver after the team also traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. With Alec Pierce's (heel) return from injured reserve seemingly not imminent, Dulin could have a prime opportunity to see extended snaps over the next few weeks, provided he can hold off the likes of Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine for playing time. Dulin already made a bit of a splash in the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, connecting with Daniel Jones on a 55-yard touchdown reception while also carrying once for a three-yard gain.

items.head: Zero catches despite season-high snap count
items.body: Burks failed to haul in either of his two targets during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded one tackle on special teams. With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being shipped off to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, at the Nov. 10 deadline, the Colts turned to Burks, Laquon Treadwell and Anthony Gould to serve as the top wideouts for Week 10. Burks' 34 offensive snaps were a season high and second among Indianapolis' wide receivers, but the rookie seventh-rounder failed to record a catch for the fifth time in 10 regular-season games, with one of his intended passes from Daniel Jones being intercepted by Michael Taaffe midway through the second quarter. Gould is working through a toe injury, so Burks could step into a bigger role on offense if the former is unable to play against the Texans on Thursday.

items.head: Taking over larger role
items.body: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Burks and Anthony Gould will step into larger roles after the team traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. A rookie seventh-round pick with 4.30 speed, Burks has caught six of nine targets for 60 yards across 49 routes (18.3 percent target rate, 1.22 yards per route). He won't necessarily see a lot of targets in an offense that runs through the RBs and TEs, but Burks should at least get far more playing time in the second half of the season, if only because the Colts' other wideouts are veterans with minimal history of production. Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are the other favorites for regular playing time, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is also on the roster.

items.head: Notches one reception in Week 9
items.body: Burks played 17 of the Colts' 64 offensive snaps in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys, finishing with a zero-yard reception on his lone target. A rookie seventh-round pick out of Oklahoma, Burks has seen sparse playing time through the Colts' first nine games. He's logged less than one-third of the snaps in each of those contests and has posted a 6-60-0 receiving line on nine targets go with 21 yards on three carries. Despite his modest output to date, Burks could nonetheless be primed for more opportunities in the Indianapolis passing game over the second half of the season. Tight end Tyler Warren will likely rank as the team's top pass-catching option, but the Colts should have plenty of targets left over after trading away Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. Meanwhile, top wideout Alec Pierce (heel)

items.head: Churns out 37 yards in Week 10 loss
items.body: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday. Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.

items.head: Zero catches in return from six-game absence
items.body: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. Njoku's snap count Monday was predictably capped, seeing as he was on injured reserve for the Chargers' six prior games while recovering from a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. Njoku could see more involvement in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: David Njoku (injury) is Active
items.body: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.

items.head: Returns to action Monday
items.body: Njoku (fibula) officially is listed as active for Monday night's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports. Since being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku -- who last played in Week 2 -- logged five consecutive limited practice listings before upgrading to full participation Saturday and being deemed questionable for Monday's contest. With his return to the lineup now confirmed, Njoku will bolster a TE corps that also includes Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden. In his only full game with the team this season, Njoku caught all five of his targets for 58 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Cardinals. Now that he's back in the mix, the 2017 first-rounder has an opportunity to reclaim enough of a role in the 0-8 Chargers offense to merit fantasy lineup consideration at his position in deeper fantasy formats going forward.

items.head: Returning for Monday night game
items.body: The Chargers activated Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens. After completing his second week of practice upon being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku had been listed as questionable heading into Monday. The Chargers ultimately came away encouraged enough by how Njoku looked during the week of practice to activate him, giving the team a third option at tight end for Monday's game. Due to his blocking prowess, Charlie Kolar likely will lead the position group in snaps Monday, but Njoku could usurp Oronde Gadsden as the Chargers' top pass-catching tight end as he takes the field for the first time since Week 2.

items.head: Questionable to face Baltimore
items.body: Njoku (fibula) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Ravens. Njoku continues to progress in his recovery from fibula injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September. The veteran tight end turned eight targets into six catches for 67 yards across the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, and his return would result in a reduced offensive workload for Oronde Gadsden.

items.head: Logs another limited practice
items.body: Njoku (fibula), who is still on IR, was limited in practice Friday. Njoku's 21-day practice window was opened Nov. 4, so the Chargers still have plenty of time to activate him. The veteran wideout was limited in all three practices last week and has been limited again Thursday and Friday of this week, so he may need to log a full session Saturday to get the all-clear to suit up Monday in Baltimore. Njoku could provide a boost to a struggling Chargers offense whenever he does return -- in his lone full game of the season so far (Week 1 against Arizona), he caught all five of his targets for 58 yards.

items.head: Limited at practice
items.body: Njoku (fibula) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Thursday. Njoku remained limited at the team's first practice of the week as he continues to work his way back from a fibula injury that has sidelined him since Week 2. The tight end was a limited participant at the team's three practices last week, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Ravens.

items.head: Not activated ahead of Week 9
items.body: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log. Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

items.head: Only one catch in Week 10 win
items.body: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore. Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, and the return of the latter has squeezed Gadsden out of the gameplan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Returns Monday night
items.body: Gadsden (eye) returned to Monday night's game against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports. Gadsden was poked in the eye in the first quarter and had to go to the locker room before returning early in the second quarter. He wasn't targeted in the passing game prior to sustaining the injury.

items.head: Questionable to return Monday
items.body: Gadsden (eye) is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Ravens. It's unclear when Gadsden suffered the injury, but he went to the locker room midway through the first quarter. He wasn't targeted prior to leaving the contest. David Njoku and Charlie Kolar will handle tight-end duties for the Bolts while Gadsden is sidelined.

items.head: Only two catches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

items.head: Tallies two catches against Baltimore
items.body: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (1), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell will continue to operate in rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Totals 36 yards against Houston
items.body: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets. The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

items.head: Minimal impact in Week 10 win
items.body: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday. One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Keaton Mitchell (injury) is Active
items.body: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.

items.head: Cleared to face former team
items.body: Mitchell (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Ravens. Mitchell's practice reps were limited by a hip injury, but he's been officially cleared to play Monday against the team he spent three seasons with from 2023 to 2025. He turned 10 touches into 67 yards during the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, and Mitchell will continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield alongside Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.

items.head: Limited in practice again
items.body: Mitchell (hip) remained limited at practice Friday. It's a new injury for Mitchell, who also was limited Thursday when the Chargers filed their first practice report for the upcoming Monday night game at Baltimore. He'll have some extra motivation, facing his former team in primetime as his current team seeks its first win of the season.

items.head: Limited by hip issue Thursday
items.body: Mitchell (hip) was limited at practice Thursday. In this past Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, Mitchell carried seven times for 33 yards and caught three of his four targets for 34 yards while losing a fumble. The 24-year-old currently is operating in a backfield timeshare with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal in his first campaign with the Chargers, and Mitchell now has two more chances to upgrade his practice participation level ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

items.head: Keaton Mitchell (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: Mitchell (hip) was limited at practice Thursday.

items.head: Leads Chargers RBs with 67 yards
items.body: Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards and caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He also lost a fumble. Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.

items.head: Sits out practice again
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was a non-participant in Tuesday's practice.

items.head: Estimated as DNP on Monday
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was estimated as a non-participant on Monday's practice report. After missing Sunday's loss to the Browns, Harrison opened the new week with another missed practice due to his hamstring issue. If he's unable to return in time for Thursday night's game against the Colts on a short week, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell likely will soak up the vast majority of the snaps at wideout.

items.head: Ruled out for Sunday's game
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns. Harrison's absence leaves more snaps for some combination of Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell, all of whom were productive last week in a win over the Chargers. C.J. Stroud has been spreading the ball around and putting up big numbers in the process, with even Nico Collins seeing his target share suffer as a result. Harrison is unlikely to handle a full-time role even when he gets back to full strength.

items.head: Not seen at Friday's practice
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Harrison also missed Thursday's session, so the WR's apparent absence Friday doesn't bode well for his chances of playing Sunday against the Browns. If Harrison ends up out this weekend, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte would be available to handle WR targets that don't go to top option Nico Collins.

items.head: Downgrades to 'DNP' Thursday
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports. Harrison was limited Wednesday, so the WR's downgrade in participation a day later clouds his status for Sunday's game against the Browns. In three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft has combined to catch six of his 11 targets for 60 yards and a TD in in that span.

items.head: Dealing with hamstring injury
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. It's a new injury for the Texans' newest wideout, who has produced just six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets through three games with Houston. Harrison ran just 14 routes on 40 dropbacks last Sunday against the Chargers, tying him with Kayshon Boutte for fourth among Texans wideouts. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell appear to have emerged as the Nos. 2 and 3 receivers behind Nico Collins.

items.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: Harrison (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.

items.head: Two catches during blowout win
items.body: Harrison caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers. Harrison ranked seventh on the team in targets, and although C.J. Stroud connected with four different wide receivers for five total touchdowns, Harrison was not one of them. Harrison has now reeled in six of 11 targets for 60 yards and a score over three contests with the Texans, and he will remain hard to trust from a fantasy perspective in Week 10 versus Cleveland.

items.head: Sits out another practice
items.body: Marks (concussion) didn't practice Tuesday. Marks' continued absence at practice comes as little surprise after he entered concussion protocol upon sustaining a head injury in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. Head coach DeMeco Ryans has already indicated that Marks is unlikely to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Thursday's game against the Colts, so expect the second-year back to get formally ruled out for the Week 11 contest following Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Woody Marks (Concussion) is Doubtful
items.body: Marks (concussion) didn't practice Tuesday.

items.head: DNP on Monday
items.body: Marks (concussion) missed Monday's walkthrough. Marks sustained a concussion during Sunday's loss in Cleveland, and head coach DeMeco Ryans said afterward that the running back isn't likely to gain clearance to play Thursday versus the Colts, according to DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com. The Texans may make a ruling on Marks' status as soon as they post Wednesday's injury report, and conversely position mate David Montgomery (groin) appears to be closing in on a return to action after logging a second full listing in a row going back to last week.

items.head: Not likely to be cleared for Thursday's game
items.body: Coach DeMeco Ryans acknowledged after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns that Marks (concussion) is unlikely to play in Thursday night's game against the Colts, ESPN.com's DJ Bien-Aime reports. With the Texans on a short week ahead of the contest, Ryans noted of Marks, "Just not enough time for him to turn it around that quickly." As for the Week 11 status of fellow RB David Montgomery (groin) -- who was inactive again Sunday -- Ryans said, "I'm not certain if David can play or not," adding "We'll take it one day at a time to see how he feels and how he can get back." Prior to his exit Sunday, Marks had 12 carries for 50 yards and one catch for 15 yards. Meanwhile, Emari Demercado finished with seven carries for 16 yards and one catch for minus-one yard, while Dare Ogunbowale logged one carry for two yards and one catch for 13 yards.

items.head: Getting checked for head injury
items.body: Marks is being evaluated for a possible concussion during Sunday's game at Cleveland. Marks remained on the turf for some time in the third quarter before making his way to the sideline and the medical tent. If Marks is diagnosed with a concussion, Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale will be the Texans' remaining running backs with David Montgomery (groin) still sidelined.

items.head: Will once again serve as RB1
items.body: Marks will be the Texans' lead back against the Browns on Sunday after David Montgomery (groin) was ruled out for that contest. Montgomery was initially tagged as questionable for Week 10 after logging a full practice Friday, but the veteran running back will end up missing a fourth straight game due to a groin injury. That means Marks will once again operate as Houston's RB1 while Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale -- the latter of whom was signed to the practice squad and elevated to the active roster Saturday -- provide backfield depth. Marks has logged at least 15 carries in each of his last four outings, and over that span, he has turned 67 carries into 254 yards (3.8 YPC) and added eight catches on 12 targets for 67 yards. He has not found the end zone since Week 4 against the Cowboys.

items.head: Cleared to play Sunday
items.body: Following a full practice Friday, Marks (knee) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Browns. After experiencing knee discomfort Wednesday and not practicing Thursday due to lingering soreness from hits, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston, Marks worked fully to close the practice week and heads into the weekend without any availability concerns. Marks has seen the bulk of Houston's backfield work of late, but he may have some competition for carries Sunday, as David Montgomery (groin) -- who hasn't played since Week 5 -- practiced fully Friday and is listed as questionable to face Cleveland.

items.head: Back at practice Friday
items.body: Marks (knee) was back at practice Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. After sitting out Thursday's practice, Marks' return to the field Friday is a positive sign for his chances of being available Sunday against the Browns. David Montgomery (groin) is also practicing Friday, following a limited session Thursday, but it isn't yet clear if he'll be ready in time for Sunday's matchup with the Browns.

items.head: Is Chuba Hubbard the biggest X factor to spark a Panthers turnaround?
items.body: Meet Carolina's team captain, a locker room leader and a relentless running back who is "chasing greatness myself."

items.head: Career-best scrimmage yards total in win
items.body: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. The 27-year-old RB kept the Panthers' offense afloat nearly single-handedly, as he set a new career high with 172 scrimmage yards while scoring both the team's TDs, on a two-yard run in the first quarter and a one-yard plunge in the fourth. Hubbard's 80 receiving yards were easily a new career high, topping the 3-57-0 line on three targets he recorded in Week 15 of the 2022 season against the Steelers. Over Hubbard's last six games, he surged to 697 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he'll look keep rolling in a Week 11 clash with the Ravens.

items.head: Ends just short of 100 scrimmage yards
items.body: Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and caught four of five targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to Denver. The 27-year-old RB nearly produced 100-plus scrimmage yards for the fifth time in the last six games but fell just short. Hubbard remains on track for a career-best campaign, and through eight games he's delivered 619 yards and five TDs on the ground while adding a 26-167-2 line on 31 targets. He lines up for a juicy matchup in Week 10 against the Saints.

items.head: Clears concussion protocol
items.body: Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Tuesday that Burden has cleared concussion protocol, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports. Burden's status was up in the air for a bit with the Bears going on bye immediately after he sustained a concussion in a Week 9 win over the  Buccaneers, but he was spotted working out on the field with teammates Monday and has apparently cleared all five phases of the protocol. The second-year wideout looks like he'll be a full practice participant throughout Week 11, and he shouldn't face any playing-time limitations in Sunday's game versus the Saints.

items.head: Luther Burden III (injury) is Active
items.body: Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Tuesday that Burden has cleared concussion protocol, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.

items.head: Back at practice Monday
items.body: Burden (concussion) was spotted participating in the Bears' unofficial practice session Monday, AllCHGO.com reports. Burden was diagnosed with a concussion after making a late exit in the Bears' previous game Nov. 8 against the Buccaneers, but he appears to have made some progress through the five-step protocol since Chicago went on bye for Week 10. Though head coach Ben Johnson hasn't confirmed that Burden has cleared the protocol, if the wideout is deemed a full participant Wednesday in the Bears' first official practice of Week 11, it would be a strong sign that he's trending toward playing Sunday against the Saints.

items.head: Concussed in Sunday's win
items.body: Burden has a concussion, head coach Ben Johnson revealed after Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports. Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.

items.head: Luther Burden III (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: Burden has a concussion, head coach Ben Johnson revealed after Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Exits late in Sunday's game
items.body: Burden (undisclosed) was helped off the field in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports. Burden took a big hit up high and fumbled the ball on the play on which he got injured. He eventually headed to the blue medical tent. Prior to getting hurt, Burden caught seven of nine targets for 97 yards and a touchdown, with most of his yards coming on a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.

items.head: Stays busy in Week 8 win
items.body: Burden secured seven of nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Bears' 34-17 win over the Seahawks on Monday night. Burden tied Colston Loveland for the team lead in both receptions and targets, and he was on the receiving end of Caleb Williams' one touchdown pass of the night. The second-year wideout's scoring grab came from one yard out in the first quarter and was his third of the season, and Burden now has a 19-281-2 line on 21 targets over the last three games heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Buccaneers on Sunday night.

items.head: Could be back for Week 12
items.body: Jacobs (finger) has a "realistic chance" of returning to action Nov. 25 against the Rams following the Packers' Week 11 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. Kaleb Johnson stepped up as Green Bay's top option out of the backfield while Jacobs has been sidelined for most of the past two games, carrying 24 times for 110 yards and a touchdown between those contests.

items.head: Undergoes finger surgery
items.body: Jacobs underwent surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday and "should be back in the next few weeks," Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. Jacobs fractured his finger in last week's victory over the Patriots, and he underwent a procedure Friday to repair it. It's unclear exactly how much time he will miss, but he has been ruled out for Week 10 and has avoided injured reserve for the time being, so reports of him missing 2-to-3 weeks appear accurate. It's unclear exactly how things will shake out in Green Bay's backfield while Jacobs works his way back, but all of MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson, Chris Brooks (ankle) and Pierre Strong are candidates to fill roles.

items.head: Set for surgery on finger Friday
items.body: Jacobs will undergo finger surgery Friday, and the Packers will have a better sense of his recovery timetable afterward, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. Jacobs exited Green Bay's Week 9 win over the Patriots after fracturing his ring finger and is in line to be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Vikings. A more precise recovery timeline is expected to be established after Jacobs undergoes surgery on the injured finger Friday, though initial estimates put his likely absence at 2-to-3 weeks on the optimistic side. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are currently available to handle Green Bay's backfield duties while Jacobs is sidelined, plus Chris Brooks (ankle) is a candidate to return from IR as soon as this weekend.

items.head: Could return in 2-to-3 weeks
items.body: Jacobs will undergo surgery on his broken right ring finger later this week and could be cleared to play in as soon as 2-to-3 weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Jacobs will be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Vikings, but with the Packers on bye in Week 11, the running back has a shot at returning to action as soon as Week 12 versus the Rams on Nov. 25. The Packers will wait for Jacobs' surgery to be completed before deciding Saturday whether he'll require a stint on injured reserve -- and the automatic four-game absence that comes with it -- or if he'll remain on the 53-man roster. For however long Jacobs ends up being sidelined, the Packers are likely to lean on Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) as their top options on the ground.

items.head: Josh Jacobs (Finger) is Out
items.body: out

items.head: Finger surgery on tap, IR possible
items.body: When asked if IR is a possibility for Jacobs (finger), coach Matt LaFleur said Monday, "I think everything is a possibility," Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, LaFleur confirmed Monday that Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured ring finger. As a result of the looming procedure, Pelissero adds that that the running back is out indefinitely, which supports the notion that an IR stint for Jacobs could be on the table. Given that MarShawn Lloyd is dealing with a knee injury that sidelined him Sunday, Kaleb Johnson is Green Bay's top healthy back at the moment, with Pierre Strong also on hand. However, it's possible help is on the way, and outside reinforcements may not be needed, according to Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com, as Chris Brooks (ankle) could be nearing a return from IR.
