items.head: Reportedly set for finger surgery
items.body: Jacobs is in line to undergo surgery on his injured finger this week and is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. The Packers may provide further clarification, but it looks like the team will be without its top running back this weekend against the Vikings, at a minimum. With MarShawn Lloyd dealing with a knee injury that sidelined him in Week 9, Kaleb Johnson profiles as Green Bay's top healthy back, with Pierre Strong also in the mix.

items.head: Uncertain to play Week 10
items.body: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged after Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots that Jacobs' (finger) availability for the team's Week 10 matchup with the Vikings is uncertain, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports. "Hopefully we can do something to allow him to go out there," LaFleur said of Jacobs. "But he was just having a hard time gripping the ball." Jacobs was limited to just 10 snaps before leaving Sunday's game in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger while attempting to stiff-arm a defender at the end of his fourth and final carry of the day. He made two trips to the locker room with the hope of adding enough protection to his hand to enable him to return to the game, but the Packers ultimately determined that Jacobs wouldn't have been able to securely grip the football if he had checked back in. With MarShawn Lloyd (knee) inactive against the Patriots and Jacobs leaving early, Kaleb Johnson (14 carries for 68 yards) ended up finishing as the Packers' rushing leader on the day.

items.head: Solid production with three catches
items.body: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

items.head: Rashod Bateman (injury) is Active
items.body: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.

items.head: Logs full practice listing Friday
items.body: Bateman (calf) was listed as a full participant on Friday's practice estimation. After being limited at practice Thursday, the starting wideout is in line to face the Chargers on Monday night after being deemed 'FP' on Friday. While Bateman has turned in two consecutive one-catch efforts, there's a chance that working with the team's new QB Jacoby Brissett could spark some added production for the 2021 first-rounder while working alongside top WR Zay Flowers.

items.head: Limited practice Thursday
items.body: Bateman (calf) was limited in practice Thursday. Bateman now has two more opportunities to practice fully and thus avoid an injury designation prior to Monday night's game against the Chargers. The starting wideout is coming off back-to-back one-catch efforts, but he'll perhaps have an opportunity to bounce back against 0-8 Los Angeles, while working with a new QB in Jacoby Brissett.

items.head: Rashod Bateman (Calf) is Questionable
items.body: Bateman (calf) was limited in practice Thursday.

items.head: Career-high yardage total in loss
items.body: Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.

items.head: Shut out in Week 9 loss
items.body: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville. Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.

items.head: One reception in Week 10 win
items.body: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a  night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

items.head: Lone catch goes for 58-yard TD
items.body: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

items.head: Career-best yardage total in win
items.body: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally was also a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Tre' Harris (injury) is Active
items.body: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.

items.head: Full practice participant
items.body: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice. After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.

items.head: Dealing with shoulder issue
items.body: Harris (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Thursday. With teammate Ladd McConkey sidelined by a back injury in Week 9, Harris played 59 of the Chargers' 68 offensive snaps, drawing a team-high seven targets. It seems like he may have picked up an injury of his own along the way though, which makes his availability for Week 10 worth monitoring. He'll have two more chances to manage a full practice before the Chargers publish their last injury report of the week Saturday.

items.head: Tre' Harris (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: Harris (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.

items.head: Three catches in blowout loss
items.body: Harris caught three of seven targets for six yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

items.head: Season-best effort in Brissett's debut
items.body: Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Andrews eased Jacoby Brissett into his team debut by putting on a pretty convincing Trey McBride impression, as the former mustered season-best totals across all three components of his receiving line. Andrews' instant chemistry with Brissett was certainly encouraging after the Ravens' passing attack's moribund state over the prior two contests, and the veteran tight end could continue thriving in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.

items.head: Efficient in first win of season
items.body: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Not on injury report
items.body: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens. Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

items.head: Justin Herbert (injury) is Active
items.body: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

items.head: Likely to play through finger injury
items.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert "should be good to go" for Monday's game at Baltimore after imaging on the quarterback's injured left middle finger returned negative for a fracture, ESPN.com reports. Herbert may still have to manage some discomfort in the finger during Monday's contest, but since the injury to his non-throwing hand, he shouldn't be too affected while throwing or handing the ball off. That being said, Herbert has become increasingly difficult to justify including in fantasy lineups even when he's been in more optimal health entering games. Heading into the matchup with the Ravens, Herbert has completed a career-low 61.3 percent of his passes for 6.8 yards per attempt and just six touchdowns in eight games. He's tied with New England's Drake Maye for the league lead in interceptions thrown (11) and ranks second behind Cleveland's Deshaun Watson in sacks taken (31).

items.head: Chargers' Jim Harbaugh says X-rays on QB Justin Herbert's finger negative
items.body: X-rays on the injured middle finger of Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert's left hand came back negative for a fracture, coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday.

items.head: Avoids fractured finger, per coach
items.body: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh relayed Monday that Herbert (finger) avoided a fracture in his left middle finger,  Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. Herbert sustained the injury in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, but the QB's imaging came back "negative," per Harbaugh. That said, Herbert's status is nonetheless worth monitoring as next Monday's contest against the Ravens approaches. If Herbert's practice participation ends up being impacted in the coming days, DJ Uiagalelei would be be next in line for added QB reps.

items.head: Justin Herbert (Finger) is Questionable
items.body: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh relayed Monday that Herbert (finger) avoided a fracture in his left middle finger,  Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.

items.head: Sustains finger injury in loss
items.body: Herbert sustained a left middle finger injury in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. Coach Jim Harbaugh said after the latest loss that Herbert "could" have a fracture. The quarterback was pulled from the game with the score out of hand in the fourth quarter, but Herbert apparently lobbied to stay in the contest. He'll have an extra day to heal up ahead of next Monday night's date with the Ravens. Herbert has been well off the fantasy radar for much of the season in this broken Los Angeles offense. If he can't face Baltimore, DJ Uiagalelei would likely get the nod under center. He completed two of seven passes for 24 yards and a touchdown in relief of Herbert on Sunday.

items.head: Impressive in team debut
items.body: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas a combined 11 times for 119 yards. Brissett recorded completions to seven different targets overall, but his one interception did lead to a Chargers touchdown. Brissett's prospects in this offense look bright if his first game is any indication, and he'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.

items.head: Ravens QB Jacoby Brissett immersed in 'crash course' for Chargers tilt
items.body: New Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett says he's focused on Monday's game against the Chargers, not the team's plans at quarterback for the remainder of the season.

items.head: In line to start next Monday
items.body: Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports. Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.

items.head: Shipped to Baltimore
items.body: The Ravens are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals that will send Brissett to Baltimore, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The deal is expected to be completed over the weekend. Brissett was set to become a free agent this offseason and was demoted from the starting role earlier this week, making him an expendable piece for the Cardinals, who will move forward with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck as their quarterbacks. Baltimore, meanwhile, had a critical need for an experienced signal-caller after losing Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (foot) to injuries that will send both quarterbacks to injured reserve and potentially keep them out for the rest of the season, so Brissett will fill a void. Since the trade won't be made official for a few more days, Brissett won't be available for the Ravens' Thursday night game against the Jaguars. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will direct the Baltimore offense against Jacksonville, but Brissett could step in as the Ravens' new starter beginning with a Week 10 matchup against the Chargers.

items.head: Two catches in Week 10 loss
items.body: Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

items.head: Set for key role again?
items.body: Dike may have a significant role on offense with Carnell Tate (shoulder) ruled out for Sunday's game against Jacksonville. Tate also missed the previous game, before a Week 9 bye, when Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati. Dike played 83 percent of snaps in the contest, running more routes (33) than both Elic Ayomanor (30) and Calvin Ridley (22). The 70-percent route share was easily a season high for Dike, and his performance suggests a sizable role should be coming again this Sunday.

items.head: Three grabs against Kansas City
items.body: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs. Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. Dotson is fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. He's not a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.

items.head: Two catches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Dotson caught two passes for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.

items.head: Salvages night with two TDs
items.body: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry now has failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

items.head: Trade out of Baltimore unlikely
items.body: The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

items.head: Another tough night in loss
items.body: Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. He also completed one pass attempt for minus-3 yards. With Joe Fagnano under center, the Jaguars unsurprisingly had the luxury of loading up to slow down Henry, and Jacksonville already came into the contest boasting an elite run defense to begin with. Henry therefore ran into a proverbial brick wall for most of the night, and he finished under 60 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive game. However, help is on the way, as impending trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett could be ready to make his first start for the Ravens as soon as a Week 10 home matchup against the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

items.head: Davis Allen (injury) is Active
items.body: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.

items.head: Davis Allen (Oblique) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Sees one target in loss to Detroit
items.body: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions. The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of snaps, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. He's also been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. Raridon is averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

items.head: Produces 52 yards in Week 9 loss
items.body: Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards on six targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers. Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.

items.head: Savion Williams (injury) is Active
items.body: Williams caught two passes for 27 yards on two targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Williams (groin) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports. Despite being listed as limited on all three of the Packers' Week 10 practice reports due to a groin injury, Williams has been cleared for Sunday's matchup. In his four appearances this season, he's turned his 19 touches (11 catches, eight rushes) into 153 yards from scrimmage and one receiving touchdown.

items.head: Remains limited at practice
items.body: Williams (groin) was a limited practice participant Thursday. Since Williams made his season debut in Week 6 against the Cowboys, his snap share has ranged from 48 to 60 percent over the last four games, and he's made his mark on offense in each one, gathering in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and one touchdown and taking eight carries for 44 yards. A groin issue has capped his reps so far this week, and Friday's injury report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Vikings.

items.head: Savion Williams (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: Williams (groin) was limited in Wednesday's jog-through practice.

items.head: Reels in touchdown versus New England
items.body: Williams caught three of four targets for 25 yards and a touchdown while adding three rushes for 13 yards during Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots. Williams was able to reel in multiple passes for the third time in four games since returning from injured reserve following an ankle injury. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he secured a 10-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Jordan Love by making an acrobatic catch. Williams has now reeled in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown while turning eight carries into 44 yards over four contests this season.

items.head: Chris Brooks (injury) is Active
items.body: Brooks rushed two times for one yard and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.

items.head: Returning to action Sunday
items.body: Brooks (ankle) is active for Sunday's game versus the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports. Brooks is back after a five-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle issue that he suffered in Week 4. With top RB Josh Jacobs (finger) out of the lineup and Pierre Strong a healthy scratch Sunday, Brooks rejoins a backfield composed of MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. Brooks got some modest run with the Packers offense before he was sidelined, turning 15 rushes into 70 yards (4.7 YPC) and three catches (on five targets) for 24 yards, but he's most valuable in pass protection for QB Jordan Love.

items.head: Chris Brooks (Ankle) is Injured Reserve
items.body: As Week 10 approaches, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com indicates that Brooks (ankle) may be ready to return from IR.

items.head: Reaches end zone in blowout win
items.body: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers. Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.

items.head: Records 34-yard touchdown grab vs. Las Vegas
items.body: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday. It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Three grabs vs. Arizona
items.body: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (oblique), but the former is dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. If that were the case, then Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the production floors of Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

items.head: Scores TD on only Week 8 reception
items.body: Kupp caught one of three targets for a seven-yard touchdown Monday in a loss to the Bears. Kupp had another low target share, but he at least made the most of his only catch by hauling in a seven-yard TD early in the fourth quarter. That score probably isn't going to be enough to inspire confidence in him in fantasy, though, given that the veteran wideout has drawn three or fewer targets in six of his eight games this season. Kupp's seven receiving yards Monday also were a season-low mark, and there simply doesn't seem to be much room for any wideout aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to regularly find success in Seattle's offense given Smith-Njigba's massive target share. With that said, Kupp at least will have a favorable matchup in Week 9, as he'll face an Arizona defense that has surrendered 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for the most in the NFL.

items.head: No production in Week 10
items.body: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

items.head: Hauls in second TD of 2026
items.body: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

items.head: Tyler Higbee (injury) is Active
items.body: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: Cleared for action
items.body: Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (rib) have both been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. With wideout Puka Nacua (knee) placed on injured reserve this week, there's renewed fantasy interest in the Rams' tight ends. Higbee has run a lot of routes without providing production in recent games, but both he and Parkinson could see more targets over the next few weeks, including Sunday in a favorable matchup with Arizona's subpar pass defense.

items.head: No practice due to illness
items.body: Higbee didn't practice Wednesday due to an illness, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports. With Higbee's addition to the Rams' Week 10 injury report Thursday, the team's top three tight ends on the active roster are dealing with health concerns, as Colby Parkinson has been limited by a rib injury, while Davis Allen downgraded from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later due to an oblique issue. As a result, Friday's practice report will be telling for who among the trio may be available Sunday in Arizona.

items.head: Tyler Higbee (Illness) is Questionable
items.body: Higbee didn't practice Wednesday due to an illness, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.

items.head: Just one catch in Week 9 victory
items.body: Higbee caught one of five targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Higbee was held to just one catch for a second consecutive game, although his 13-yard grab set the Rams up on the Commanders' one yard line and led to a rushing touchdown by Blake Corum on the next play. Higbee has only four catches over his last three games, but he figures to play a larger role in the passing game for at least the next month while Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is on injured reserve. The Rams will hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up six touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL.

items.head: Another quiet performance Week 8
items.body: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory. Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

items.head: Logs two catches against Arizona
items.body: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

items.head: Colby Parkinson (injury) is Active
items.body: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: Remains limited in practice
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) was limited at Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports. While Parkinson continues to operate with a cap on his practice reps due to the rib issue that sidelined him in Week 8 against the Chargers, fellow TE Tyler Higbee showed up on Thursday's injury report as a DNP due to an illness, and reserve option Davis Allen went from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later. Friday's practice report will unveil the odds of each player to suit up Sunday at Arizona.

items.head: Still limited by ribs
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. Parkinson has seemingly been banged up all season, and the ribs are just the latest issue for the tight end. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) vacating more than 45 percent of the Rams' targets, Los Angeles figures to lean heavily on its tight ends to try and get by without its top two receivers and top pass-catching tight end. Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will likely have prominent every-down roles in the coming weeks.

items.head: Colby Parkinson (Ribs) is Questionable
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Grabs all four targets Week 9
items.body: Parkinson notched four catches for 13 yards on four targets in a 20-13 win over Washington on Sunday. Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles in receptions, though he didn't turn them into many yards. Still, it was his third straight contest with at least four catches, so Parkinson looks to be developing into a favorite target of QB Matthew Stafford. That could come in handy in Week 10 and beyond, as Stafford is going to need to turn to other pass catchers to help make up for the massive production being lost in the absence of Puka Nacua, who is expected to land on IR due to a knee injury.

items.head: Active versus Washington
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Commanders. Parkinson, who was inactive in Week 8, managed to log a limited practice Friday, before being listed as questionable for the contest. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) -- who was initially slated to return to action this week but subsequently ruled out -- still not in the mix, the return of Parkinson, who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played, is a welcome boost to a Rams TE corps that also includes Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and Max Klare.

items.head: Questionable for Week 9
items.body: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports. The veteran tight end managed to get in a limited practice Friday, keeping the door open for him to play after missing last Sunday's game against the Chargers. Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was initially slated to return to action this week, but was subsequently ruled out, so the status of Parkinson -- who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played -- is worth monitoring.

items.head: No catches against Carolina
items.body: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

items.head: Upgrades to full Thursday
items.body: Fant Donaldson (back) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice. Fant was limited at Wednesday's practice, but the veteran TE faced no limitations Thursday, suggesting that he'll be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He has worked as the Saints' No. 2 option at the position behind Juwan Johnson.

items.head: Noah Fant (injury) is Active
items.body: Fant Donaldson (back) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice.

items.head: Working through back issue
items.body: Fant (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. Fant may have tweaked his back during the Saints' 23-22 overtime win over the Browns in Week 9, when he finished with one catch on two targets for 12 yards. He'll have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's NFC South tilt against the Panthers. Fant has accumulated 12 catches on 18 targets for 96 yards and three touchdowns through seven regular-season games.

items.head: Noah Fant (Back) is Questionable
items.body: Fant (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.head: One catch in Week 9 win
items.body: Fant caught one pass for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against Cleveland. The veteran tight end logged 47 percent of the offensive snaps but is mainly a blocker at tight end, while Juwan Johnson handles most of the pass-catching duties. Fant has four catches for 30 yards over his last four games and is not even remotely on the fantasy radar.

items.head: Quiet in Week 10 loss
items.body: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

items.head: Two catches against Cleveland
items.body: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

items.head: Five touches on offense vs. Indianapolis
items.body: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

items.head: Jaylen Wright (injury) is Active
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.

items.head: Inactive in Week 9
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) is listed as inactive Sunday against the Lions. After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to a quadriceps injury, Wright was able to get back to limited Thursday and maintain that activity level Friday, at which point he was tagged as questionable in advance of the weekend. On Sunday morning, however, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Wright wasn't expected to suit up, and that's now locked in. With Wright out of the lineup, Kaytron Allen (quad) and Carlos Washington will serve as the reserve RB options behind Ollie Gordon.

items.head: Not slated to play Sunday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) isn't in line to play in Sunday's game against the Lions, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Wright was held out of drills Wednesday due to a quad injury before capping Week 9 prep with back-to-back limited practices. That left him questionable to suit up Sunday, but assuming he's listed among the Dolphins' inactives about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be in street clothes this weekend. Kaytron Allen (quadriceps, questionable) and Carlos Washington are the other options to handle complementary reps behind No. 1 RB Ollie Gordon.

items.head: Deemed questionable
items.body: Wright (quad) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Averaging just 1.9 yards per carry, Wright is unlikely to get more than a handful of touches off the bench if he's active this Sunday. Ollie Gordon has been dominating Miami's backfield work.

items.head: Will practice Friday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) will practice Friday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Averaging a miserable 1.9 yards per carry this season, Wright has no fantasy appeal other than being Ollie Gordon's ineffective backup.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) was limited in Thursday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports. Wright has been battling various issues all season and hasn't been effective when on the field, yet he's still operating as the Dolphins' lightly-used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon. Wright is averaging a microscopic 1.9 yards per carry this season.

items.head: Returns to practice Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) is taking part in practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Wright didn't practice Wednesday, so Thursday's practice appearance is a step in the right direction, but the extent of his participation remains to be seen. Ollie Gordon has cemented himself as the lead back for the Dolphins, while Wright hasn't exceeded six touches in a game this season.

items.head: Does little with two touches
items.body: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

items.head: No catches in blowout loss
items.body: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals. Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

items.head: Finds end zone on Sunday Night Football
items.body: Perine turned six carries into 14 yards and a touchdown and hauled in all four of his targets for 25 yards during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

items.head: Double-digit carries in win
items.body: Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a prominent role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a rather valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.

items.head: One catch on SNF
items.body: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals. Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

items.head: Reels in one pass during win
items.body: Gray caught one of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand to operate as the team's primary tight end in his place.

items.head: Secures one reception in Week 9 win
items.body: Gray caught his only target for 11 yards Sunday in a 35-12 win against the Jets. Gray was a minor factor in the passing game, with his lone reception gaining 11 yards late in the third quarter. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Travis Kelce paced Kansas City with 72 receiving yards on four catches. Gray had a nice two-game run with a combined six catches for 97 yards across Weeks 6 and 7, but since then he's tallied just three receptions for 26 yards and a touchdown across his subsequent two games.

items.head: One catch in victory
items.body: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

items.head: Back in game after getting checked for head injury
items.body: Coleman, who was evaluated for a head injury, was later cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Jets. Coleman previously headed to the blue medical tent after taking a big hit during the contest, per Matt Parrino of News 4 Buffalo. However, after getting checked out, Coleman returned to the field to rejoin a WR corps that also includes DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir.

items.head: Posts three receptions in Week 9 victory
items.body: Coleman finished Monday's 23-6 win over the Vikings with three catches for 17 yards on six targets. Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.

items.head: Set to play in Week 9
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest in Minnesota. Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.

items.head: Limited at practice again
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Friday. Coleman is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4, listed as a limited participant Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder injury. There's been no indication it's serious, so Coleman seems on track to play Monday night at Minnesota. Fellow Bills wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) also is gearing up to play.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday. It's a new injury for Coleman, who is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4. With both DJ Moore (knee) and Dalton Kincaid (chest) healthy last Sunday against the Ravens, Coleman caught just one pass for four yards on three targets.

items.head: Back on Philly's practice squad
items.body: Blue was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Monday. Blue was let go by the Eagles after suiting up for the team in Weeks 8 and 9, a span in which he didn't record a carry and caught his only target for nine yards. Now that he's back on the team's practice squad, the 2025 fifth-rounder will give Philadelphia's Saquon Barkley-led RB corps an added depth option ahead of Week 11 action.

items.head: Cut loose by Philly
items.body: The Eagles waived Blue on Tuesday. Philadelphia is now left with Saquon Barkley as the lone running back on its 53-man roster, but Elijah Mitchell will most likely be signed off the practice squad to replace Blue. After being signed off the practice squad himself in late October, Blue suited up in the Eagles' last two games but played just eight total snaps on offense while recording no rushing attempts and a nine-yard reception. His main contributions came on special teams, where he served as the Eagles' primary kickoff returner and gained 268 yards on 12 runbacks (22.3 average).

items.head: Gets bumped up from practice squad
items.body: The Buccaneers signed Stick off their practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports. Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who was out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.

items.head: George Holani (Knee - MCL) is Questionable
items.body: Holani is week-to-week after suffering an MCL sprain in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday.

items.head: Won't return Sunday
items.body: Holani (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Seahawks. Holani exited the first quarter of Sunday's contest with a knee injury. The running back will not return, leaving another player to fill his special-teams role as Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet continue to dominate the Seahawks' running game.

items.head: Exits with knee injury
items.body: Holani (knee) is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders. Holani exited the first quarter of Sunday's contest with a knee injury. The running back likely sustained the injury on kick coverage. Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet are still set to receive all the rushing volume for the Seahawks in Sunday's game.

items.head: Gets no touches Week 10
items.body: Holani didn't log any touches or targets Sunday in a 17-3 win over Arizona. Holani logged just one offensive snap, by far his lowest count of the season. He's trending toward playing primarily on special teams now that Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are back in the fold at running back for Seattle. Emanuel Wilson is also on the roster, but he didn't see any action at all Week 10.

items.head: Skyy Moore (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Moore's ankle injury is not considered serious, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Back in action in Week 10
items.body: Moore (ankle) is listed as active Sunday versus the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports. Moore has spent the requisite four contests on injured reserve due to an ankle injury, and his activation from the list Saturday set him up for his first game action since Week 5. Prior to the stint on the sidelines, he had a bit role on offense (7-35-0 on 14 targets) while handling most of the return responsibilities. Expect Moore to serve behind fellow WRs Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams in Week 10.

items.head: Skyy Moore (Ankle) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Packers designated Moore (ankle) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.

items.head: Athan Kaliakmanis (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: Kaliakmanis (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Giants but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback.

items.head: Thomas Fidone II (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Needs thumb surgery, IR possible
items.body: Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Addison will require surgery on his thumb and will miss a few weeks, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. O'Connell indicated that Addison will be a candidate for injured reserve, though if he does end up being deactivated, the Vikings anticipate that the wideout would be able to return after sitting out the minimum four games. Addison injured his thumb at Friday's practice and subsequently was inactive for Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay. For as long as Addison is sidelined, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price and Tai Felton will be the options to see added reps behind No. 1 receiver Justin Jefferson.

items.head: Won't suit up Sunday
items.body: Addison (thumb) is inactive for Sunday's game at Green Bay, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. A late addition to the Week 10 injury report, Addison took a questionable tag into Sunday after sustaining the thumb injury during Friday's practice. After Addison went through a pregame workout, the Vikings opted to hold him out for Sunday's contest while the thumb issue was seemingly inhibiting him while catching the football. With Addison and top tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist) both sidelined, trade-deadline pickup Kirk Cousins won't have many weapons to work with beyond No. 1 wideout Justin Jefferson in his first start for Minnesota since 2023.

items.head: Questionable due to thumb injury
items.body: Addison is listed as questionable for Sunday's game in Green Bay due to a thumb injury. Addison didn't make an appearance on the Vikings' Week 10 injury report until Friday, and now his status is up in the air ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. If he's able to suit up this weekend, he'll be on the receiving end of passes from new starting QB Kirk Cousins.

items.head: Solid yardage on two catches
items.body: Addison secured two of three targets for 28 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. Addison finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the night for a low-volume Vikings passing game, and his final catch, which went for 16 yards, came on Minnesota's last drive from the arm of Max Brosmer. Carson Wentz's game-long ineffectiveness depressed the production of the air attack as a whole, but Addison would be in better position to boost his numbers if Kyler Murray (hamstring) is able to return for Sunday's Week 10 road matchup against the Packers.

items.head: Joining active roster
items.body: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday. Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

items.head: Cleared of head injury
items.body: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports. London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

items.head: Concussion evaluation in Week 10
items.body: London is being evaluated for a possible concussion during Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports. Before his departure late in the fourth quarter, London recorded six catches (on 12 targets) for 109 yards. If he's diagnosed with a concussion, he'll be subject to league protocol in order to gain clearance to play again, but the Falcons are on bye in Week 11, so he'll have plenty of time to recover for a Week 12 road matchup with the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Leading receiver in Week 9 loss
items.body: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

items.head: Trending toward Week 12 return
items.body: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that he's "really optimistic" Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) will be able to get a full week's worth of practice coming out of the Seahawks' Week 11 bye and start their next game Sunday, Nov. 29, against the 49ers, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Darnold, who last played in Week 8, still is working his way through a pair of injuries, but barring any setbacks, he's trending toward a Week 12 return. Macdonald reiterated that Darnold will be the team's starter once healthy, even though backup Drew Lock has guided Seattle to a 4-0 record while coming on in relief or starting in place of an injured Darnold in the first two games of the season as well as the most recent two contests.

items.head: Expected back after Week 11 bye
items.body: Darnold (quadriceps), who won't play this coming Sunday at Las Vegas, is expected to return in Week 12 at San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29 after a Week 11 bye, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports. Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

items.head: Not ready to return in Week 10
items.body: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) won't be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Meanwhile, Macdonald noted that the Seahawks got a "good exam" for Drew Lock, who is nursing an oblique injury but is expected to be able to play through the issue and make a second straight start in Week 10. With a bye on tap for the Seahawks in Week 11, Darnold will benefit from some extended time to recover from his injuries and will turn his focus toward returning to action Nov. 29 versus the 49ers.

items.head: Could miss Week 10
items.body: Darnold (quadriceps) may miss Seattle's Week 10 game at Las Vegas, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Darnold already has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, and the combination of the quadriceps injury and cracked ribs he suffered last Monday against the Bears is threatening to sideline him for multiple weeks. The Seahawks have a Week 11 bye on the schedule, so getting him healthy for the stretch run from late November through early January may sway the team's decision-making. As long as Darnold is out, Drew Lock (right elbow) will direct Seattle's offense.

items.head: Won't play in Week 9
items.body: Head coach Mike Macdonald announced that Darnold won't play Sunday against the Cardinals due to a quadriceps injury, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports. In addition to a quad issue that Darnold sustained late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Macdonald revealed that the quarterback suffered a rib injury early in that contest. The pair of health concerns may have played a part in Darnold's subpar performance, which included 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception on 17-for-34 passing and two carries for 20 yards. With Darnold out for the first time since Week 2, backup QB Drew Lock will draw the Week 9 start under center for the Seahawks.

items.head: Middling numbers in Week 8 loss
items.body: Darnold completed 17 of 34 passes for 188 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding two rushes for 20 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Darnold averaged just 5.5 yards per attempt and took three sacks from a Bears defense that made an impact addition in Jeffery Simmons on Thursday via trade with the Titans. Darnold's 50.0 percent completion rate was a season low for him in non-injury-shortened games, and the veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the sixth consecutive contest. Darnold did toss multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 4, connecting with Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43 yards) and Cooper Kupp (seven yards) for his pair of scoring strikes. Darnold will take an unsightly 10:9 TD:INT heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: Could continue to fill in for Maye
items.body: Mike Reiss of ESPN.com notes via ESPN's Adam Schefter that there are fears  DeVito's teammate, Drake Maye, may have sustained a fractured ankle during Week 10 action. Regarding Maye's status going forward, head coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he'll wait for further information before estimating how long his starting QB might be out, but he also acknowledged he "wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the (Week 11) bye," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports. As a result, DeVito is in a position to start Sunday, Nov. 29 against the Chargers and possibly beyond. That said, as NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests, New England is expected to explore the QB market in the coming days, be it through a practice squad addition or a veteran free agent such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who previously worked with  offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels.

items.head: Forced into action in Munich
items.body: DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich. He added 19 yards on four carries. Drake Maye (ankle) was forced to leave the game early after an Aidan Hutchinson (knee) sack, putting DeVito under center for the third time this season, but the first time with the outcome still in doubt. The 28-year-old QB had little luck moving the ball, and his 10-yard TD toss to Lan Larison in the fourth quarter came when the score was already 28-3. The severity of Maye's ankle injury isn't yet known, but the Patriots fortunately get a bye in Week 11 to give him extra recovery time. If he's still unavailable after that, DeVito could find himself starting in Week 12 against the Chargers.

items.head: Set to join Tampa Bay practice squad
items.body: Rush is in line to sign with the Buccaneers' practice squad, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. Rush will give Tampa Bay added QB depth with starter Baker Mayfield dealing with an injury to his foot and ankle area that he sustained in Week 9. Jalon Daniels currently is Mayfield's top backup ahead of Week 11 action, while Easton Stick is on the team's practice squad.

items.head: TBD on whether surgery is needed
items.body: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Willis (groin/core) has not undergone surgery and that the Dolphins are still determining if a procedure is needed, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Hafley noted on that subject Monday, "We will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

items.head: Surgery not ruled out
items.body: The Dolphins hope Willis (abdomen) will return this year but haven't ruled out season-ending surgery, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports. With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "He'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

items.head: Expected back this season
items.body: Though Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Wednesday that he doesn't have a timetable for the potential return of Willis (abdomen), he does expect the QB back at some point this season, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. What is known is that the earliest Willis is eligible to be activated from IR is ahead of Miami's Week 14 game against the Bears. Of course, with the team's record at this stage standing at 1-7, there's no compelling reason to rush Willis back. In his absence, Kyle McCord is next in line for QB1 duties, with Brady Cook a candidate to be summoned from the practice squad leading up to this weekend's game against the Colts.

items.head: Dolphins hopeful QB Malik Willis will be back this season
items.body: Coach Jeff Hafley said Miami sees Malik Willis as its starter regardless of when he returns from his groin injury.

items.head: Malik Willis (Abdomen) is Injured Reserve
items.body: ir

items.head: Pedestrian numbers in Week 9 loss
items.body: Willis completed 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for seven yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Willis was back under 200 passing yards for the first time in three games, and he failed to throw at least one touchdown pass for the first time since Week 4. The 2022 third-round pick connected with seven different targets overall, and following the game, Joe Schad of the Palm Beach Post reported that Willis was dealing with both groin tightness and a tight hamstring during the game. Willis and the Dolphins' Week 10 matchup is a Colts team that could trade away multiple key players before Tuesday's deadline.

items.head: Malik Willis (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: Willis completed 13 of 25 passes for 128 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for seven yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.

items.head: Goes without reception in Week 10
items.body: Dulcich failed to haul in either of his two targets while logging 42 of 69 offensive snaps in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Second-year signal-caller Kyle McCord threw for 209 yards on 32 attempts in his first NFL start, but he couldn't forge much of a connection with Dulcich, who was held without a catch for the second time this season. With Malik Willis (core) out for at least three more contests while on injured reserve, Dulcich will have more time to build a rapport with McCord, but the tight end was far from a reliable fantasy option even when Willis was directing the offense. Despite playing more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Dolphins' nine games, Dulcich has been limited to 24 receptions for 270 yards and has yet to find the end zone.

items.head: Quiet in loss to Detroit
items.body: Dulcich caught two of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.

items.head: Three catches versus Las Vegas
items.body: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

items.head: Two short TDs against Arizona
items.body: Barner caught two of four targets for seven yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He added three carries for three yards and an additional touchdown. Barner was the Seahawks' closer, finishing off both touchdown drives with short scores against Arizona. His first was a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Barner then caught a seven-yard score from Drew Lock. Both touchdowns came in the second quarter. For the season, Barner has 23 grabs for 210 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets. He's also rushed for two scores. Barner is in the large group of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.

items.head: Pair of catches in Week 8 loss
items.body: Barner brought in two of five targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Barner was third in receiving yards and targets, although the tight end still finished below 30 receiving yards for the sixth time this season. Barner remained in a minor role despite the fact the Seahawks were down Rashid Shaheed (knee), and with 21 receptions for 203 yards and zero touchdowns, the third-year pro remains behind the pace of his career-best 52-519-6 line from last season. Barner will look to capitalize on a favorable matchup against the Cardinals defense in a Week 9 home matchup on Sunday.

items.head: One catch in return to lineup
items.body: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders. After missing the previous tow games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

items.head: Rashid Shaheed (injury) is Out
items.body: Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

items.head: Rashid Shaheed (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Won't play Sunday
items.body: Shaheed (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of 933 KJR reports. With Shaheed out last week, Tory Horton handled a 72 percent route share in Seattle's loss to Chicago. It'll likely be a similar look this week with Horton and Cooper Kupp taking most of the WR snaps alongside Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The big difference will be under center, where Drew Lock is filling in for Sam Darnold (quad) for the second time this season.

items.head: Misses another practice
items.body: Shaheed (knee) didn't participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Shaheed has now missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to work his way back from the knee injury that forced him to miss the team's Week 8 loss to Chicago. The wide receiver's chances to play Sunday versus Arizona seem thin, so Tory Horton could serve as the team's No. 3 option at wide receiver again in Week 9.

items.head: DNP on Wednesday
items.body: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Shaheed missed Monday night's loss to the Bears, which allowed Tory Horton to log a season-high 43 offensive snaps, which he turned into a 3-26-0 receiving line on six targets. Horton would again be in line for WR3 duties if Shaheed needs to sit Sunday against Arizona.

items.head: Iffy for Week 9
items.body: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Tuesday that Shaheed (knee) has a chance to play Sunday against the Cardinals, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports. Shaheed was sidelined for the first time all season in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears, after his knee injury kept him from practicing throughout the week. In Shaheed's absence, Tory Horton handled elevated snaps as the Seahawks' No. 3 wideout behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, while George Holani served as the team's top kickoff returner. Shaheed may need to turn in a full practice at some point during Week 9 prep to put himself on track to return to action Sunday.

items.head: Two catches in loss
items.body: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

items.head: Three catches in loss
items.body: Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.

items.head: One catch in Week 10 win
items.body: Gesicki caught one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers. Gesicki caught six touchdowns in the first seven games of the season, but he's now produced just three grabs for 20 scoreless yards over the past two contests. The fluky touchdown rate was never going to hold up, and Joe Burrow funnels so many of his targets through Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown that there isn't a whole lot more to go around to Cincinnati's ancillary weapons. Gesicki is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks despite running a bunch of routes as the de facto slot receiver.

items.head: Touchdown streak snapped
items.body: Gesicki caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win versus Atlanta. Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.

items.head: Gets into end zone in loss
