Assuming Mahomes indeed logs a full session Wednesday, he'll be in line to play this weekend, and if so, will be working with a WR corps bolstered by Tuesday's trade deadline acquisition of Josh Downs from the Colts.

items.head: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes announce baby No. 4 on NFL trade deadline day
items.body: The couple shared the news on a busy trade deadline day that also brought receiver Josh Downs to Kansas City.

items.head: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes day-to-day with elbow injury
items.body: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is considered day-to-day after suffering an injury to his throwing elbow.

items.head: Tops 100 scrimmage yards in Week 10
items.body: Hall rushed 11 times for 41 yards and caught all four of his targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. Hall narrowly topped Braelon Allen (eight carries for 40 yards) for the team lead in rushing yards and finished second behind Garrett Wilson (seven catches for 106 yards) in both receptions and receiving yards. While Allen continues to be more efficient as a rusher, Hall's superior receiving ability should help the latter maintain the edge in playing time for a 2-8 Jets team that often finds itself playing catch-up. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik, who played most of the second half Sunday, could be more reliant on check downs to Hall than veteran Geno Smith (ankle) was, but it remains to be seen who will get the nod under center in Week 11 against the Chargers.

items.head: Gets 18 touches in return
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) rushed 15 times for 61 yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.

items.head: Looks like Sunday starter
items.body: Based on pregame warmups, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic suggests that it seems like Hall will start at RB for the Jets in Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Hall, who hasn't seen game action since sustaining a quad injury in Week 3, approached Sunday's contest minus an injury designation, thus setting him up to rejoin a Jets backfield that had been capably paced by Braelon Allen in his absence. While it looks like Hall is set to reclaim his key role in the team's backfield, offensive coordinator Frank Reich said Thursday the Jets intend to utilize "a mix" of the two running backs Sunday, per Al Iannazzone of Newsday Sports, an approach that makes sense given how well Allen has produced of late.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) "has been medically cleared" and is expected to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Hall has not taken the field since sustaining a quad injury in Week 3, but he practiced fully Thursday and appears primed to return to action Sunday. Braelon Allen has shined in Hall's absence, but Hall entered the season as the starter, so both figure to be involved to some degree in Week 9.

items.head: Practices fully Thursday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. After opening the week with a limited session, Hall upgraded to full participation Thursday, indicating that he's in the clear to return Sunday against the Chiefs for his first action since Week 3. Braelon Allen has thrived in the lead role during Hall's absence, and offensive coordinator Frank Reich said Thursday that the Jets intend to utilize "a mix" of the two running backs Sunday, per Al Iannazzone of Newsday Sports. Hall is the superior receiving back, but Allen is averaging 5.0 yards per carry while Hall averaged just 3.2 YPC prior to getting hurt.

items.head: Says he's ready to go this week
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) indicated Thursday that he's ready to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Hall, who hasn't played since Sept. 27, participated in Thursday's practice, though it remains to be seen if the Jets list him as a full or limited participant. In any case, the running back is trending toward a return to action this weekend, and if he is indeed available versus Kansas City, Hall will rejoin a backfield that's been capably paced paced by Braelon Allen in his absence.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) is participating in Thursday's practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Hall, who was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice session, was also limited throughout the week leading up to the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders, which the running back sat out. While the team's coaching staff has expressed optimism that Hall will be ready to return Sunday against the Chiefs, his status will remain up in the air until he's able to practice without limitations. Thursday's participation level has yet to be revealed, but Hall's presence at practice suggests that he has at least avoided a setback.

items.head: Set for limited practice Wednesday
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Hall (quadriceps) will be a limited practice participant Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports. Hall, who hasn't played since Sept. 27, was also limited at practice last week, but Glenn said that the running back is "trending in the right direction" as Sunday's game against the Chiefs approaches, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com. As for how the workload might be split between Hall and Braelon Allen should Hall return this weekend, Glenn declined to go in specifics beyond noting that "both will play" in such a scenario, according to Cimini.

items.head: Season-high 14 targets in return
items.body: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

items.head: Garrett Wilson (injury) is Active
items.body: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.

items.head: Active for Sunday's game
items.body: Wilson (concussion) is listed as active Sunday against the Bills. Wilson emerged from a Week 8 loss to the Raiders with a concussion and required nearly two weeks to make his way through the protocol for head injuries, seemingly getting the all-clear from an independent neurologist either Friday evening or Saturday. In any case, all three of the Jets' top three injured wide receivers -- also, Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell (knee) -- are available Sunday, but Wilson should retain his standing as the clear No. 1 among the group, which has translated to a 43-527-3 line on 63 targets in eight games.

items.head: Slated to return Sunday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) is expected to be cleared to play against the Bills on Sunday, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports. Wilson was held out of the Jets' 35-12 loss to the Chiefs in Week 9 while in the league's concussion protocol. The star wide receiver was a full participant in Friday's practice, and while he was tagged as questionable for Sunday's game, the Jets appear confident that the fifth-year wideout will clear the league's protocol and be available to play against Buffalo.

items.head: Nearing clearance for Sunday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) has one more step to complete in concussion protocol, and Jets coach Aaron Glenn believes that will happen before Sunday's game against the Bills, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports. Wilson will upgrade to full participation Friday after logging limited practices earlier in the week. He's on track to return after missing just one game, but he'll still need clearance from a neurologist if Friday's practice goes as planned.

items.head: Limited again Thursday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice. Wilson was limited in a second consecutive practice Thursday, though he took a step in the right direction, as Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports that Wilson shed the red non-contact jersey at Thursday's practice. If Wilson can practice without limitations Friday, that would go a long way in his quest to clear concussion protocol in time to face the Bills on Sunday.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Wilson (concussion) was present at Thursday's practice, Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News reports. Wilson is taking part in practice again Thursday after being a limited participant Wednesday. An upgrade to full participation would be a step toward Wilson exiting the NFL's concussion protocol, which would put him in position to return Sunday against the Bills following a one-game absence. His participation level Thursday will be clarified later in the day.

items.head: Returning to limited parctice
items.body: Wilson (concussion) will be a a limited participant in Wednesday's practice,  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athleticreports. That's a step in the right direction for Wilson, who didn't practice last week before being ruled out for Week 9 action. Given that the wideout is still limited at this stage, Wilson has some hurdles to clear before he completes passage through the NFL's concussion protocol. However, if he's able return to action this weekend versus the Bills, he'll reclaim his lead role in a WR corps that was paced by Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell in his absence from this past Sunday's loss to the Chiefs.

items.head: Solid numbers in blowout loss
items.body: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Sources: Giants called Falcons to ask about Bijan Robinson before trade deadline
items.body: The Giants made a call to the Falcons before the NFL trade deadline inquiring about star running back Bijan Robinson, multiple sources told ESPN.

items.head: Big workload in loss to Cincy
items.body: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

items.head: Three total TDs in Week 10 win
items.body: Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing five times for five yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Allen scored one-yard rushing touchdowns in the first and third quarters, bringing his season total up to 11 rushing TDs. He added his 13th touchdown pass of the campaign on a 45-yard strike to DJ Moore later in the third quarter, and Allen's fourth-quarter interception on third-and-long was basically an arm punt. Heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins, the star QB has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all but one outing this season.

items.head: Survives Vikes D in win
items.body: Allen completed 21 of 31 passes for 234 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding six carries for 15 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night. Allen came into the night undoubtedly expecting to have to work for everything he got, and Brian Flores' aggressive defensive unit helped validate that prognosis by sacking the star signal-caller on four occasions. However, Allen was able to navigate the dangers pretty effectively, spreading the ball around to eight different targets overall. He connected with Keleki Latu from 25 yards out late in the first half for his one touchdown pass, and Allen's one turnover, a first-quarter interception at the Vikings' seven-yard line, didn't lead to any Minnesota points. Allen hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 1, but he'll take 2,027 passing yarsd and a 12:6 TD:INT alongside 285 rushing yards into a Week 10 road divisional clash against the Jets on Sunday.

items.head: Breaks off 74-yard rushing TD
items.body: Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Buffalo relied primarily on its ground game in the lopsided victory, as Cook's 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter provided the cherry on top after a pair of one-yard Josh Allen rushing scores helped the Bills pull away. Cook extended his touchdown streak to eight games by scoring his ninth rushing TD over that span. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game during the productive stretch, bouncing back effectively after being held to 69 scoreless yards by the Texans in the season opener. Cook has a nice opportunity to keep rolling in Week 11, when the 8-1 Bills host the 1-8 Dolphins.

items.head: Thrives again in workhorse role
items.body: Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night. Cook was repeatedly stonewalled through three quarters by a Vikings run defense that had been fairly beatable, but the star running back continued to get opportunities to test Minnesota's defensive front. That approach finally began paying off on an early fourth-quarter marathon scoring drive, one where Cook recorded runs of nine, six and 11 yards before capping off the march with a five-yard scoring rush to extend Buffalo's 13-6 lead. Cook ultimately fell just a carry short of tying his career high, and he eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the fourth time this season. The fifth-year pro's trip to the end zone extended his touchdown streak to seven games as well, and Cook will head into a favorable Week 10 road matchup just 186 rushing yards short of his fourth straight 1,000-yard campaign.

items.head: Healthy scratch for Week 10
items.body: Cooks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys. Mike Evans (Achilles) is also inactive for a third consecutive game, but Cooks' services are not needed Sunday due to the return of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the acquisition of Keenan Allen from the Colts on Tuesday. It's unclear if Cooks will have any role in the 49ers' offense once Evans is cleared to return. For now, Cooks' next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Vikings on Nov. 22.

items.head: Tallies two catches against Las Vegas
items.body: Cooks brought in both of his targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Cooks and other 49ers wide receivers operated in elevated roles Sunday due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 25 receiving yards ended up being third-most on the Niners behind Jordan Watkins (86) and tight end George Kittle (58), and Cooks' 32 offensive snaps were also third-most among San Francisco wide receivers. The 49ers hit the road for Week 10 against the Cowboys, and Cooks' workload on offense would decrease if one or both of Evans or Samuel was cleared to return.

items.head: Quiet trip to Munich
items.body: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch. The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

items.head: Not viewed as trade candidate
items.body: The Lions have received trade calls on LaPorta leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the team prefers to keep him with the hope of signing the tight end to a long-term deal, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. Earlier in the season, LaPorta expressed his frustration with the Lions for the organization's inability to come to terms on an extension with him, but both sides still appear to be on good terms and willing to re-engage in discussions on a new deal before he becomes a free agent in 2027. The fourth-year tight end has likely helped his case for earning a lucrative contract by having thus far stayed healthy throughout the season while putting together a 35-399-3 receiving line on 49 targets over the Lions' first eight games.

items.head: Quiet on four catches Sunday
items.body: LaPorta brought in four of five targets for 32 yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. LaPorta finished a distant second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on a quiet day for the Lions' passing attack. The fourth-year tight end had back-to-back 80-plus-yard efforts in Weeks 4 and 5, but he's totaled a modest 83 total receiving yards over the subsequent three contests. LaPorta will look to boost his production back up in the Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Hunter Long (injury) is Active
items.body: Long (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Hunter Long (Knee) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Cardinals designated Long (knee) for return from injured reserve Wednesday.

items.head: Bo Melton (Thigh) is Questionable
items.body: Melton (thigh) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Bo Melton (injury) is Active
items.body: Melton (head) was removed from the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against Minnesota, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.

items.head: Bo Melton (Head) is Questionable
items.body: Melton exited Sunday's game against the Patriots and is being evaluated for a concussion.

items.head: Healthy scratch in Week 10
items.body: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game at Arizona. Since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to the lineup in Week 8 against the Bears, Wilson was contained to special teams in that contest and then was active but didn't log a snap last Sunday versus the Cardinals. Now, Wilson will yield all the RB reps to Charbonnet, Price and George Holani in Week 10.

items.head: Four grabs in win over Pats
items.body: Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

items.head: Two touches in Week 9 win
items.body: Williams brought in one of two targets for 31 yards and rushed once for nine yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Williams and the rest of the Lions' air attack had a quiet afternoon, as Jared Goff threw for just 170 yards overall. Williams was efficient on his two touches, but he finished with a new season low in receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick, who's averaging 16.7 yards per reception on the season, will likely be busier in a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Two trips to end zone in Week 10 win
items.body: St. Brown caught four of five targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early. St. Brown took full advantage of the volume he saw however, scoring on a 56-yard catch and run in the first quarter and then taking another short pass from Jared Goff and turning it into a 28-yard TD in the third. It was St. Brown's third multi-TD game of the season but his first since Week 2, and he'll take a 65-755-7 line on 91 targets through nine games into a Week 11 clash with the Buccaneers.

items.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown (injury) is Active
items.body: St. Brown caught four of five targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.

items.head: Active in Week 10
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) is listed as active Sunday against the Patriots in Munich. St. Brown has dealt with a rib injury that limited him in practice the last two weeks, but he's still suiting up for the ninth time (in as many chances to do so) this season. He ranks seventh in the NFL with 86 targets, which he's parlayed into a 61-657-5 receiving line, and he's now facing a New England defense that has allowed the most receiving touchdowns (12) and most YPT (9.7) to opposing wide receivers in nine games in 2026.

items.head: Expected to suit up Sunday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. As he was during Week 9 prep, St. Brown was limited in practice this week due to a rib injury, but he also isn't slated to be among the Lions' inactives for Week 10. Assuming he's active ahead of an 8:30 a.m. ET kickoff, he again will serve as the No. 1 WR in Detroit's offense

items.head: Stays limited Thursday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday. For a second week in a row, St. Brown is enduring practice restrictions due to a rib injury. Having said that, he still suited up this past Sunday in Miami and earned a 75-percent snap share en route to eight catches (on 10 targets) for 86 yards. Friday's injury report will determine if St. Brown has a designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Patriots in Munich.

items.head: Limited by rib injury
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) was limited at Wednesday's practice. St. Brown also was limited on all three of the Lions' Week 9 practice reports due to a rib injury, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday at Miami and log a typical 75 percent snap share en route to eight catches (on 10 targets) for 86 yards. Friday's injury report will determine if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

items.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown (Ribs) is Questionable
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) was limited at Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Eight catches in Week 9 win
items.body: St. Brown brought in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. St. Brown set the pace across the board for the Lions in receptions, receiving yards and targets. St. Brown was playing through a rib issue that had limited him throughout the practice week, but he turned in an efficient effort that included his fifth straight game with six or more catches. St. Brown's touchdown drought did extend to five games, and he'll once again aim to snap it in next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany.

items.head: Only one catch in Week 10 defeat
items.body: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.head: Exceeds century mark in loss
items.body: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Massive numbers in Week 10 romp
items.body: Gibbs carried the ball 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns while catching seven of eight targets for 99 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots. Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game early for New England, setting the stage for the rout, and Gibbs took full advantage as he set new season highs in receiving yards and scrimmage yards. It's the fourth time in 2026 that the star RB has topped 150 rushing yards, and his fourth game with multiple TDs. Gibbs has amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine contests as he gets ready to face a stingy Buccaneers run defense in Week 11.

items.head: Rush TD in Week 9 win
items.body: Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. It was a relatively quiet day by Gibbs' lofty standards against a Dolphins team that's proven to have plenty of fight despite its losing record. The standout back salvaged his fantasy day with an eight-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, Gibbs' second score on the ground in as many games and ninth overall. Gibbs failed to record at least one reception for the first time this season, but he's already amassed 1,132 scrimmage yards and 11 total touchdowns across eight games heading into next Sunday's showdown against the Patriots in Germany.

items.head: Limited to two catches in Munich
items.body: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

items.head: Hunter Henry (injury) is Active
items.body: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.

items.head: Cleared to play Sunday
items.body: Henry (foot) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Lions after logging another limited practice Friday. Though Henry was limited at practice all three days leading up to the contest, the Patriots were likely managing his reps in anticipation of having the tight end available this weekend. While it's possible that the team will get top WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) back versus Detroit, RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is still out and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, questionable) is banged up, so Henry figures to be a key available option for QB Drake Maye to work with, provided he avoids any setbacks with his foot.

items.head: Limited again
items.body: Henry (foot) was a limited practice participant Thursday. Henry played through the injury in last week's loss to Green Bay and has now managed back-to-back limited practices to open Week 10. He'll likely gut it out again Sunday against the Lions in Munich, and while the matchup is favorable, rookie Eli Raridon had been cutting into Henry's snaps and targets even before the veteran injured his foot in a Week 8 win at Miami. Henry played 49.2 percent of snaps in the Week 9 loss to Green Bay, catching each of his three targets for 35 yards.

items.head: Limited Wednesday
items.body: Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday's practice. After injuring his foot in Week 8 against Miami, Henry played through the limited practice reps last week against the Packers and turned three targets into three grabs for 35 yards. Assuming he didn't suffer a setback, Henry should be fine for Sunday's game against the Lions in Germany.

items.head: Hunter Henry (Foot) is Questionable
items.body: Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday's practice.

items.head: Three catches in blowout loss
items.body: Henry caught all three of his targets for 35 yards during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers. Henry returned to action after suffering a foot injury in the first half of the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins and missing the majority of that contest. The tight end was held in check versus Green Bay, finishing with three or fewer catches for the sixth time this season. Henry has now reeled in 32 of 37 targets for 361 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

items.head: Active for Sunday's game
items.body: Henry (foot) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Packers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports. After opening the week with back-to-back missed practices, Henry was able to work in a limited fashion Friday before heading into the weekend with a 'questionable' designation. With his active status confirmed, in the absence of any setbacks or limitations Sunday, Henry a" who leads the Patriots with 29 catches and is second in receiving yardage (326), to go with two TDs through eight games -- will have an opportunity to remain a key target for QB Drake Maye in a New England passing offense that continues to be without top WRs A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder).

items.head: Tosses three TDs in Munich
items.body: Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry. A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

items.head: Full practice Thursday
items.body: Goff (chest) practiced fully Thursday. Goff kicked off Week 10 prep as limited Wednesday due to a chest injury, but his return to all activity one day later puts him in the clear for Sunday's contest against the Patriots in Munich. He'll be taking on a New England defense that was just torched by Packers QB Jordan Love for 372 yards and three touchdowns in Week 9.

items.head: Jared Goff (injury) is Active
items.body: Goff (chest) practiced fully Thursday.

items.head: Dealing with chest injury
items.body: Goff was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury. Goff is making his first appearance on the injury report this season, but he at least logged some reps Wednesday as he tends to a health concern. A return to full participation Thursday and/or Friday should put him in the clear for Sunday's game versus the Patriots.

items.head: Jared Goff (Chest) is Questionable
items.body: Goff was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury.

items.head: Quiet day in Week 9 win
items.body: Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while also rushing four times for five yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Goff was the latest quarterback to scuffle some against a Dolphins defense that's fought hard all season, as the veteran signal-caller took three sacks and finished with a new season low in passing yards. Goff also failed to throw a touchdown for the first time this season, and he threw a pick for the second time in as many games after going without an interception for the first six contests of the campaign. Goff has completed at least 68.0 percent of his passes in three straight games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Leading receiver in ugly loss
items.body: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich. In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

items.head: Returns to lineup Sunday
items.body: Hollins (calf) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Packers. Hollins, who had landed on IR prior to Week 5 action, was activated from IR/designated to return Saturday but still carried a 'questionable' designation ahead of the contest. In his first game action since Week 4, Hollins could make an immediate contribution to a WR corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, but remains without A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Prior to his injury, Hollins recorded a 15/209/0 receiving line on 20 targets through four games.

items.head: Questionable for Week 9
items.body: Hollins (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers. The Patriots would need to activate Hollins from injured reserve by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to have him available for Sunday's game against the Packers. The team could certainly use him with A.J. Brown (knee) out again, but Hollins never made it back to full practice participation, instead logging limited sessions Wednesday through Friday.

items.head: Limited in return to practice
items.body: Hollins (calf) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice after being designated for return from injured reserve. After the Patriots opened up his 21-day evaluation window, Hollins took the field for his first practice since Week 4. Hollins will be eligible for activation from IR at any point, but unless he upgrades to full participation by the end of the week, he could have a tough time gaining clearance for Sunday's matchup with the Packers. Through New England's first four games before he sustained a calf injury, Hollins produced a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets.

items.head: Set to resume practicing Wednesday
items.body: The Patriots are expected to designate Hollins (calf) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Hollins' last game appearance came back in Week 4, but with his return to practice on the horizon, he could be an option for the Patriots as soon as this Sunday's game against the Packers. With Romeo Doubs (shoulder) currently on IR and A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) availability for Week 9 looking cloudy, Hollins could have a chance at claiming a meaningful role right off the bat if he's cleared to play versus Green Bay. Prior to sustaining the calf injury, Hollins logged a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets through New England's first four games.

items.head: Modest numbers in loss to Lions
items.body: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit. Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

items.head: First career TD in loss
items.body: Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

items.head: Struggles in Week 10 loss
items.body: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich. The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

items.head: Rhamondre Stevenson (injury) is Active
items.body: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.

items.head: Suiting up in Munich
items.body: Stevenson (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich. Though he initially appeared likely to miss multiple weeks after sustaining a knee tendon injury in last Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers, Stevenson won't end up being sidelined for any game action at all. After being held out of the Patriots' first practice of Week 10, Stevenson proceeded to turn in a pair of limited sessions en route to taking a questionable designation into Sunday. He appears to have made it through a pregame workout no worse for the wear and should be on track to lead the New England backfield once again, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison on hand as his backup options after TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was moved to injured reserve Saturday.

items.head: Appears poised to play
items.body: Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. It initially appeared that the knee injury that forced Stevenson from his team's Week 9 loss to the Packers would cost him a few weeks of action, but it now appears he will not miss any time at all. Stevenson's status for Week 10 will be confirmed when the Patriots release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's game kicks off at 9:30 am ET.

items.head: Not in uniform for Friday's practice
items.body: Stevenson (knee) was present but not in uniform for Friday's practice, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports. Stevenson was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, but it's worth noting that Chad Graff of The Athletic described that as a "pad-less, extremely light" session. With the running back presumably in line to log a 'DNP' a day later, Stevenson could be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions later Friday, and in that scenario, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) still sidelined, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next in line for backfield work versus Detroit this weekend, with Terrell Jennings a candidate to be elevated from the team's practice squad.

items.head: Returns to practice Thursday
items.body: Stevenson (knee) returned to practice Thursday as a limited participant. Stevenson's participation may come as a surprise after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that the running back was likely to miss a few weeks. The Patriots have a Week 11 bye, but first they'll face the Lions in Munich this Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET. Corey Kiner is next up as New England's lead runner if Stevenson doesn't play. Patriots wideout DeMario Douglas told reporters that Stevenson hopes to play, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.

items.head: Working off to side Thursday
items.body: Stevenson (knee) was working off to the side at the start of Thursday's practice, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports. Previous reports suggested that Stevenson, who registered a 'DNP' on Wednesday,  is expected to miss time after exiting this past Sunday's loss to the Packers. While it's encouraging to see the running back get some level of work in Thursday, chances are he'll officially be deemed a non-participant on the Patriots' upcoming injury report. The team has a bye in Week 11, which figures to factor into the decision-making process ahead of this weekend's game against the Lions in Munich.

items.head: Not practicing Wednesday
items.body: Stevenson (knee) is absent from Wednesday's practice, Evan Lazar of Patriots.com reports. Stevenson is expected to miss time after an early exit from Sunday's loss to the Packers. A Week 11 bye may or may not help him avoid a multi-game absence, but he's unlikely to play this Sunday in Munich against the Lions.

items.head: Set for 2026 debut Week 10
items.body: Jones was elevated from Arizona's practice squad to the active roster Saturday. Jones signed with the Cardinals' practice squad Oct. 28, and this is his first elevation since joining the organization. The veteran wideout could immediately slide into a major role in Arizona's passing game among a depleted wideout corps that has lost Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) for the season. Jones spent the past two campaigns with the Cardinals, and he caught 12 passes (on 18 targets) for 182 yards over eight games last year.

items.head: Placed on IR
items.body: Henderson (illness) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

items.head: Working toward return, but timetable TBD
items.body: Coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that Henderson (illness) is working hard to get back, while acknowledging that he doesn't have a timetable for when that may occur, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports. On the topic of when the running back might return, Vrabel noted Friday, "when that is, I don't know. I don't have a timetable." Henderson, who last saw game action in Week 7, has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions, and based on Vrabel's statement, the 2025 second-rounder's status beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye is unclear. Fellow RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) returned to a limited practice Thursday, but if he ends up being held out this weekend, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next up for the team's backfield work versus Detroit, with Terrell Jennings representing a possible practice squad elevation.

items.head: Absent from Wednesday's practice
items.body: Henderson (illness) was absent from Wednesday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. With Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) both absent, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are left as New England's top running backs ahead of a Week 10 matchup in Munich against the Lions on Sunday. After that, the Patriots have a Week 11 bye, and it's still unclear when Henderson might be available again.

items.head: Deemed out for Sunday's game
items.body: Henderson (illness) didn't practice Wednesday and is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.

items.head: TreVeyon Henderson (Illness) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Won't play Sunday against Green Bay
items.body: Henderson (illness) won't play Sunday against the Packers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots won't put a timeline on Henderson's return, while adding, per Lazar, that the team is "just trying to make sure that TreVeyon is cared for and his recovery plan is intact and he's comfortable with it." In the absence of Henderson -- who recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms" -- Rhamondre Stevenson will pace New England's backfield, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison also mixing in.

items.head: Provides medical update Friday
items.body: In a statement posted to social media Friday, Henderson -- who hasn't practiced since last Wednesday -- noted that he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms," Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. Henderson was unavailable for New England's Week 8 win over Miami due to an undisclosed illness, and he's now indicated that tests have "come back positive and reassuring," adding "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions." The running back noted that for now he is "committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health" and that his "health and long-term well-being" are his foremost priorities. In six games this season while working in a Patriots backfield that also includes Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, Henderson has carried 52 times for 203 yards a touchdown, while adding five receptions for 45 yards.

items.head: Not present Thursday
items.body: Henderson (illness) was not seen at Thursday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports. Henderson hasn't practiced since last Wednesday as he deals with an illness. Unless he returns to drills Thursday and/or Friday this week, he may be in danger of missing a second game in a row Sunday against the Packers. Thursday's injury report will reveal Henderson's activity level.

items.head: Won't return for Week 10
items.body: Iosivas (thumb) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Steelers. Iosivas was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Steelers despite logging full practices Thursday and Friday. He'll remain on IR for at least one more game, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

items.head: Set to return to practice
items.body: Iosivas (thumb) was cleared to return to practice Thursday. Iosivas, who landed on IR on Sept. 26, is bouncing back from surgery to repair a torn ligament in his thumb, and the wideout's looming return to Thursday's practice has him trending the right direction ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers. Once he's back in action, Iosivas will slot back in behind top WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, a role that doesn't typically yield steady volume.

items.head: Not ruled out for Week 10
items.body: Head coach Zac Taylor said Monday that Iosivas is doing well in his recovery from left thumb surgery, and the Bengals will "continue to work through this week" to determine when the receiver might return from injured reserve, Laurel Pfahler of the Dayton Daily News reports. Cincinnati has yet to open Iosivas' 21-day practice window since he landed on IR on Sept. 26, so until that happens, the wideout's return to game action shouldn't be considered imminent. While Iosivas has been sidelined for the Bengals' past six games, Dohnte Meyers has been serving as the primary No. 3 wideout behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and tight end Mike Gesicki has also benefited from an expanded profile in the passing attack.

items.head: Andrei Iosivas (Thumb) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Head coach Zac Taylor said Monday that Iosivas is doing well in his recovery from left thumb surgery, and the Bengals will "continue to work through this week" to determine when the receiver might return from injured reserve, Laurel Pfahler of the Dayton Daily News reports.

items.head: Brought up from practice squad
items.body: The Cowboys elevated Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports. With Tyler Goodson (knee) on injured reserve and Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the rest of the year, Abanikanda is expected to operate as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for the foreseeable future, starting with Sunday's game against the 49ers. Abanikanda last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he logged 22 carries for 70 yards (3.2 YPC) and added seven catches on 11 targets for 43 yards across six regular-season games with the Jets.

items.head: Prepping for RB2 job
items.body: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that Abanikanda likely will be promoted from the practice squad to replace Tyler Goodson (knee) as the No. 2 running back ahead of Sunday's matchup with San Francisco, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports. A 2024 fifth-round pick, Abanikanda has six regular-season appearances and 29 career touches -- all back in 2023 for the Jets. He offers sub-4.5 speed at 215-plus pounds, but he won't necessarily have the same role as Goodson, who earned the team's trust with solid performances after latching on earlier this fall. With Abanikanda as the No. 2 back, Javonte Williams may be tasked with even larger workloads than before.

items.head: Tyler Goodson (Knee - ACL + MCL) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Cowboys placed Goodson (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Dealing with ACL, MCL sprains
items.body: Goodson sustained ACL and MCL sprains in his knee during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, a source tells Todd Archer of ESPN.com. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer already confirmed Monday that Goodson would be sidelined for multiple weeks due to the injury, and now that details have emerged regarding the severity of the issue, it's conceivable that the 26-year-old could be headed for injured reserve. The loss of Goodson leaves the Cowboys with no healthy running backs on the active roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but team owner Jerry jones said that the team plans to sign a free-agent back Tuesday, per Archer. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as backfield options on the practice squad.

items.head: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
items.body: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.head: Set for multi-week absence
items.body: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" after spraining his knee in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Goodson likely will undergo further testing as the Cowboys look to hone in on a more definitive timeline for his return, but Schottenheimer's comments suggest that the reserve running back can safely be ruled out for at least Week 10 against the 49ers and Week 11 versus the Titans. Despite succumbing to the knee injury, the 25-year-old delivered his best performance of the season Sunday, finishing the day with 77 yards on 12 carries. The Cowboys currently have no other healthy running backs on the roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but one or both of practice-squad members Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin will be candidates for elevation to the 53-man roster while Goodson is sidelined.

items.head: Likely out for Week 10
items.body: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said Monday that Goodson is expected to miss time after injuring his knee in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports. Goodson has emerged as the Cowboys' clear No. 2 back in recent games and turned in his best performance of the season against his former Colts squad in Week 9, carrying 12 times for 77 yards while failing to corral his lone target. The running back injured his knee at some point along the way, and though he was able to check back into the contest, Goodson may have been running on adrenaline. He'll presumably undergo further testing before the Cowboys provide an update on the extent of his injury, but with Goodman on track to miss at least next Sunday's game versus the 49ers, Dallas could turn to practice-squad members Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin to serve in backup roles behind lead back Javonte Williams.

items.head: Strong showing against former squad
items.body: Goodson rushed 12 times for 77 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. Facing the team for which he played two-plus seasons from 2023-25, Goodson put together a highly efficient performance as a complementary option to Javonte Williams, even after leaving the game for a spell to be checked out for a knee issue. Goodson's carry and yardage totals were both season highs, as was his average of 6.4 yards per carry. The Iowa product is seeing steady usage in a run-heavy Cowboys offense, and he's logged 29 rush attempts over the last three games heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers.

items.head: Returns to game
items.body: Goodson (knee) has returned to Sunday's game against the Colts, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports. Goodson returned in the third quarter of Sunday's contest after previously exiting with a knee injury. Now that he's back in action, Goodson should continue to work in his usual change-of-pace role behind Javonte Williams for the remainder of the game.

items.head: Exits with knee injury
items.body: Goodson (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Goodson exited in the second quarter of Sunday's contest with a knee issue after compiling 44 yards on seven carries. Javonte Williams is the sole remaining active running back active for the Cowboys in Week 9.

items.head: Mo Alie-Cox (Groin) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Colts placed Alie-Cox (groin) on injured reserve Saturday.

items.head: Mo Alie-Cox (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: Alie-Cox is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Dallas due to a groin injury.

items.head: Continues quiet campaign in Week 10 loss
items.body: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders. Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

items.head: Hauls in just two of five targets Week 10
items.body: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington. Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

items.head: Upgrades to full practice
items.body: Mooney (chest) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice, Mooney took every rep a day later to erase any concern about his status heading into Thursday's game against the Commanders. The veteran wideout has played more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in all but one of the Giants' eight games to date, but he exceeded two receptions and 50 receiving yards for the first time all season in this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. He remains a relatively unappealing fantasy option while receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely are locked in as the Giants' clear top two pass catchers.

items.head: Considered limited Monday
items.body: Mooney (chest) was estimated to be a limited participant at the Giants' walkthrough practice Monday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports. Mooney reeled in a season-high three passes for 54 yards and also had a rush for minus-4 yards during Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The wide receiver may have picked up a chest injury during the victory, and as a result, he was considered to be less than 100 percent Monday. Mooney will have two more chances to be upgraded to a full participant prior to Thursday night's matchup with the Commanders.

items.head: Darnell Mooney (Chest) is Questionable
items.body: Mooney (chest) was estimated to be a limited participant at the Giants' walkthrough practice Monday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Scores touchdown on Thursday Night Football
items.body: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants. Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

items.head: More playing time on tap
items.body: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Daniels "will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports. Daniels has seen minimal playing time this season, but he'll be thrust into a more prominent role offensively due to both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being on injured reserve. As such, Daniels -- a sixth-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, with Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also in the mix for snaps on offense. During his final college season in Miami, Daniels recorded 50 catches for 557 yards and seven touchdowns across 13 games.

items.head: Cleared for backup role
items.body: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback. Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

items.head: Carson Wentz (injury) is Active
items.body: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.

items.head: Limited again Thursday
items.body: Wentz (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday. Wentz had his left ankle stepped on by Vikings left guard Joe Huber during Monday's loss to the Bills, and while he didn't miss a snap before Max Brosmer took over for the final possession, the former has operated with practice restrictions to begin Week 10 prep. With the acquisition of Kirk Cousins on Tuesday and Kyler Murray still week to week due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Wentz is expected to return to a reserve role Sunday at Green Bay, but head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn't announced a starter for that contest as of Thursday.

items.head: Listed as limited
items.body: Wentz (ankle) is listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports. Wentz injured his ankle Monday night during his disastrous start against the Bills. The Vikings have since traded for Kirk Cousins, who likely will take over as the starter for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Coach Kevin O'Connell wouldn't commit to starting Cousins and suggested Kyler Murray (hamstring) is unlikely to play, but Cousins' familiarity with the scheme and terminology means he shouldn't need long to prepare.

items.head: Carson Wentz (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Wentz (ankle) is listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.

items.head: Forgettable performance in spot start
items.body: Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed once for no gain in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night. He also lost a fumble.

items.head: In line to draw MNF start
items.body: Wentz is stated to start Monday night's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Wentz will get the Week 9 assignment at QB for the Vikings, with Kyler Murray viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Max Brosmer will be the team's backup versus Buffalo, and perhaps longer than that should Murray's injury linger. Wentz thus represents an option for those in Superflex formats or otherwise are in need of signal-caller help due to injury or bye week issues.

items.head: Plays just five snaps
items.body: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders. Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

items.head: Expected to back up Skattebo on Thursday
items.body: Singletary is expected to return to a change-of-pace role Thursday against the Commanders, as Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation. Singletary recorded a season-high 23 touches in Skattebo's absence during the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 but mustered only 39 yards with all that volume. Prior to that win, Singletary hadn't exceeded six carries in a game this season. Skattebo is expected to lead the backfield in his return, with Singletary likely to feature in passing situations since Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) remains on IR. Greg Desrosiers is also on the roster at RB.

items.head: Inefficient in lead role
items.body: Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards and caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Singletary blew by his previous season high of six carries, as fellow running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy were both sidelined by hamstring injuries. Skattebo has a chance to return for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, while Tracy won't be back prior to Week 12, so Singletary is likely to maintain an elevated role unless the Giants trade for another running back prior to Tuesday's deadline. Singletary didn't make the most of his added opportunities against the Eagles, averaging a meager 1.5 yards per carry.

items.head: Ticketed for RB1 duties
items.body: With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful to play Week 9, Singletary is expected to operate as the Giants' lead back Sunday against the Eagles, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports. Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) is on injured reserve and required to miss at least the next four games, and Najee Harris was recently released, so it'll be Singletary's job Sunday. Practice-squad types Greg Desrosiers and Phil Mafah are in tow as the backups but both have little-to-no experience carrying the ball in the NFL. Volume alone will put Singletary in the fantasy RB2 mix.

items.head: Productive with three catches Thursday
items.body: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.head: Three catches in Week 9 win
items.body: Fields caught three of five targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The rookie wideout is a distant third in pecking order for targets behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely in the New York offense. For the season, Fields has 19 catches for 288 yards and one touchdown on 35 targets, averaging 36.0 yards per game across eight contests.

items.head: Finds end zone in Week 10 win
items.body: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.head: Three grabs in loss
items.body: Williams caught three passes for 25 yards on six targets in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the year, Williams led the team's wide receivers and tight ends in snaps and routes against Los Angeles, but it was a tough matchup against a top-tier pass defense. Williams should have better games moving forward in one of the league's pass-happiest offenses. The rookie wideout should be a full-time player down the stretch in the second half of the season.

items.head: Solid involvement in Week 10 win
items.body: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

items.head: Tallies 10 touches in Week 9
items.body: Ekeler rushed eight times for 16 yards and caught two of three targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Ekeler led the team in carries, toting the rock one more time than fellow running back Rachaad White in the loss. Ekeler was also able to reel in multiple passes for the second time in three games, and he figures to remain in a relatively even backfield split with White against the Giants in Week 10.

items.head: Impressive numbers in loss
items.body: McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

items.head: Won't be limited in Week 10
items.body: McCarthy (hip pointer) is "good to go" and isn't expected to be limited for Thursday's game against the Commanders, James Palmer of NFL Network reports. McCarthy missed much of the third quarter of this past Sunday's win at Philadelphia due to a hip pointer but was able to return to action, completing 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing four times for 22 yards. Considering he ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back full practices, he seemingly was in the clear for Thursday's matchup, and Palmer's report indicates McCarthy will take on every rep, leaving Jameis Winston as the No. 2 QB, and on the sidelines Thursday.

items.head: J.J. McCarthy (injury) is Active
items.body: McCarthy (hip pointer) is "good to go" and isn't expected to be limited for Thursday's game against the Commanders, James Palmer of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Practices fully, ready for Thursday
items.body: McCarthy (hip) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. McCarthy was sidelined for most of the third quarter of this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles after sustaining a painful hip pointer, but he was able to finish out the game. Head coach John Harbaugh expressed confidence afterward that the injury wouldn't be anything that jeopardized McCarthy's status for Thursday's game against the Commanders, and the quarterback's ability to take every rep Tuesday clears the way for him to start on a short week. Through two starts and two appearances off the bench with the Giants, McCarthy has completed 43 of 68 pass attempts (63.2 percent) for 622 yards (9.1 YPA), one touchdown and one interception to go with 51 yards on nine carries.

items.head: Taking part in practice Tuesday
items.body: McCarthy (hip) was spotted on the field for the media-access portion of Tuesday's practice, Art Stapleton of The Bergen Record reports.

items.head: Managing hip issue
items.body: McCarthy (hip) is listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. McCarthy exited Sunday's win at Philadelphia for a spell in the third quarter due to a hip injury but returned to action. Head coach John Harbaugh told Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News on Monday that McCarthy has a hip pointer but is expected to play Thursday versus the Commanders. McCarthy likely will need to be listed as full Tuesday and/or Wednesday to head into Week 10 action without a designation.

items.head: J.J. McCarthy (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: McCarthy (hip) is listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.

items.head: Harbaugh: Giants 'feel fairly good' about McCarthy (hip) playing vs. Commanders
items.body: Giants coach John Harbaugh says he feels "fairly good" about quarterback J.J. McCarthy's availability this week after he suffered a hip injury in Sunday's win against the Eagles.

items.head: Records game-winning TD in victory
items.body: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.

items.head: Just three grabs in Sunday's loss
items.body: Diggs caught three of five targets for 51 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo ended up leading the Commanders' injury-depleted group of pass catchers with seven targets each, and the former led the team in receiving yards and caught Jayden Daniels' only TD pass. Diggs' modest showing still represented his biggest yardage total since Week 1, although he did see his two-game scoring streak come to an end. Diggs will try to ramp up his production in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.head: Overcomes turnovers in win
items.body: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday. It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, he subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. Daniels ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.head: First turnover of season in loss to Rams
items.body: Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. He also gained 16 rushing yards on four carries and lost a fumble. The lost fumble was the first giveaway of the season for Daniels in six games. The third-year QB also struggled to sustain drives while working with a badly depleted wide receiver room, and his lone TD was a seven-yard toss to Van Jefferson -- a player who had zero catches on the year coming into Sunday -- in the second quarter. Injuries have derailed the first half of the season for the Commanders, but Daniels will try to spark his team to life in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.head: Middling production in Week 10 loss
items.body: Nabers secured five of seven targets for 44 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.

items.head: Quiet in Week 9 win
items.body: Nabers caught five of eight targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Nabers recorded at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye but failed to extend that streak in Sunday's low-scoring win, during which J.J. McCarthy (hip) and Jameis Winston combined to throw for just 198 yards. The star wide receiver led the team with eight targets but finished third in receiving yards behind Darnell Mooney (54) and Isaiah Likely (53). Nabers had his hands on what would have been a 20-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter but failed to secure a diving catch attempt. McCarthy left in the third quarter but managed to return later in the second half, and he can be tentatively penciled in as the starting QB for Thursday's home game against the leaky Commanders pass defense.

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia. Nabers was held out of drills Thursday due to a knee injury, but his return to all activity one day later lines up with head coach John Harbaugh's assessment of the situation Friday, when he told Matt Citak of the Giants' official site that the wide receiver "practiced fully" and is "full go" for Week 9. As a result, Nabers will look to build upon the massive 36-509-2 line on 51 targets that he's accrued over the last four contests.

items.head: 'Full go' for Week 9
items.body: Head coach John Harbaugh said Nabers (knee) "practiced fully" Friday and will be "full go" for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Matt Citak of the Giants' official site reports. That's not to say Nabers won't be tagged with a designation once the Giants post their final Week 9 injury report Friday, but it appears his absence from Thursday's practice due to a knee issue was merely a blip on the radar. He's strung together four consecutive 100-yard performances, a stretch in which his receiving line sits at 36-509-2 on 51 targets. Nabers' presence will be key for New York's offense led by J.J. McCarthy, who will be making his second start of the season since assuming the Giants' QB1 role.

items.head: Looks ready for Sunday
items.body: Nabers (knee) was catching passes during Friday's walkthrough and should be "good" to go For Sunday's game against the Eagles, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports. After sitting out Thursday's practice due to the knee issue, Nabers appears to be trending in the right direction for Sunday's game at Philadelphia. Still, the Giants' final injury report will provide the clearest indication of whether the wide receiver takes a designation into the weekend.

items.head: DNP due to knee injury
items.body: Nabers didn't practice Thursday due to a knee injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Nabers opened Thursday's session working on the side with trainers, and afterward he told Art Stapleton of USA Today, "I'll be good," as it pertains to his status for Week 9. In any case, the reason for Nabers' absence is a knee issue, which could be related to the right ACL tear that ended his 2025 season in Week 4. He'll have one more chance to prove his health Friday, at which point the Giants may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

items.head: Offers positive update
items.body: Nabers (undisclosed) said Thursday, "I'll be good," for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Art Stapleton of USA Today reports.
